Acting out is the defense here: the person discharges the impulse in assault instead of thinking it, so you take the history of what they already did, not the feeling of the hour.

2010-174.sentence: Split treatment is still one relationship: you write the prescription while another clinician holds the hour, and the two of you are making the care together. You keep full responsibility for the patient, not a 50/50 pill-only slice, so you must talk, consent to communicate, and own safety as if the therapy were in the room with the meds.

2010-176.sentence: Childhood-onset schizophrenia still hits the same attentional, learning, and abstraction systems adults lose—so ego strength is already thin before identity has even coalesced. Do not ask that child to “process” the psychosis; measure whether they can still hold a thought, delay an impulse, and test reality as school and peers change around them.

2010-177.sentence: An overvalued idea of adultery sits between doubt and delusion: the spouse is still used as a regulator, but closeness now means scanning for betrayal. Ask how certain they are and whether they can entertain being wrong—that is the attachment test, not the content of the jealousy.

2010-178.sentence: A no-show one month after bipolar hospitalization is not a cultural identity crisis in the room; it is a break in the holding arrangement. Call, say you are concerned, and ask why they missed—so the patient learns absence still brings a person, not a letter threatening discharge.

2010-179.sentence: At three-and-a-half, dressing in mother’s clothes is social learning on the initiative-versus-guilt stage: she copies the same-sex model she sees reinforced. Social learning does not need a triangular Oedipal plot or a genital self-concept—just watching Mom and being rewarded for looking like her.

2010-183.sentence: At fourteen the developmental job is still school, peer work, and keeping the day organized—not proving that the elders are “not real.” Treat the declining grades as the capacity that is slipping; leave the culturally held visions intact unless function, not cosmology, is what failed.

2010-185.sentence: Taped razor blades, done carefully enough not to actually kill him, followed by an honest admission that he wanted time out of his cell — that's a clear, external secondary gain, which is what makes this malingering rather than the internal need-to-be-sick of factitious disorder or the identity chaos of borderline personality.

2010-187.sentence: The frequent pairing of autistic disorder with mental retardation is the clinic’s reminder not to dump every limitation into one diagnosis—that is a paranoid-schizoid move, splitting the child into “just autism” so no one has to face the extra damage. Depressive concern, Klein’s capacity to stay with mixed reality and try to repair, means you actually measure IQ, language, and adaptive skill and then help the family grieve and plan for both.

2010-190.sentence: When antiretrovirals interact with methadone and the dose destabilizes, patients often get labeled 'nonadherent' or 'drug-seeking' before anyone checks the pharmacology — check the interaction first, because that assumption is exactly the kind of bias that costs people their treatment.

2010-191.sentence: Menninger’s triangle—here with the therapist, there with partners, then with early caregivers—is raw until someone names the link. That naming is interpretation: Bion’s containing, taking the evacuated fear that everyone is disappointed and returning it as a thinkable pattern instead of another nameless dread.

2010-193.sentence: A trial comment that tests insight is: “I hear the pain and the diagnosis—what I have to write down is what you still cannot do at work, at home, and in public, week after week.” If they can help you name missed days, failed tasks, and lost roles, they are already doing the real work of a disability exam: translating inner life into degree of functional impairment, not into a sadder story.

2010-195.sentence: Witnesses will recruit you as the neurologist who must call this a seizure, and your countertransference urge is to over-treat the jerks so you do not “miss epilepsy.” Stay with the sequence they actually saw: faintness and pallor, collapse, a few bilateral jerks, then flushing—that is vasovagal syncope, not a bid to make you the crash-cart doctor.

2010-196.sentence: The humiliation they expect is often never a story they can tell; it lives as a freeze in the throat, so they stay mute in groups while still wanting friends. Avoidant personality disorder is that unrepresented shame enacted in the room: they treat your slightest frown as the criticism they cannot remember having survived.

2010-197.sentence: The calm line “my significant other dumped me” is a compromise formation: the wish to be held collides with a ban on looking needy, so feeling is stripped out. Confrontation is the first move—you name the split between words and affect—before you interpret the buried wish.

2010-200.sentence: Generativity is the 40-to-60 job: feeling useful by protecting people who come after you, not mastering intimacy or making peace with death. Hold the hour as that developmental work—do not turn empty-nest doubt into extra visits, a rushed diagnosis, or a fee that implies midlife meaning is an emergency you must fix.

2010-201.sentence: Recurrent unsuccessful efforts to control use is the DSM-IV dependence criterion; role failure, fights, and legal trouble stay on the old abuse list. The drug has become the regulator the person reaches for first—proximity to a chemical 'secure base' that soothes, even while every stop attempt fails.

2010-204.sentence: The 2008 meta-analysis put long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy ahead of CBT, DBT, supportive, and family therapy for personality disorder plus chronic mixed illness. Years of a steady therapist can function as a selfobject: reliable mirroring of competence so esteem is borrowed until a more stable self can hold.

2010-207.sentence: A trial comment is whether she can see the low desire as part of her own depression—anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, appetite loss—rather than a standalone sexual disorder. If she can use that, the DSM-IV-TR mapping is a symptom of a major depressive episode, not hypoactive desire or arousal disorder.

2010-209.sentence: The family recruits you as either reckless prescriber or withholding savior when they invoke the black-box warning on quetiapine in this 82-year-old with dementia. Name the feeling they put in you, then tell the truth: atypical antipsychotics increase mortality, and that risk is weighed against benefit—not denied or inflated.

2010-210.sentence: Calling it neurasthenia can already be an enactment: patient and clinician repeating a cultural script of exhaustion instead of thinking undifferentiated somatoform disorder. Stay with what the body is doing—fatigue, aches, poor concentration—rather than living the old label as if it were the whole relationship.

2010-212.sentence: Parity treats the psychiatric prescription as the same feed as insulin, not as a luxury demand or a slightly shameful extra. Justice is the principle that lithium or an antipsychotic is not a second-class meal just because the organ is the mind.

2010-214.sentence: Freud parked genital focus plus the opposite-sex-parent wish in the phallic stage, not in latency or the later genital stage. Insight is whether they can try on that comment as a map of rivalry and desire, not as a police report about last Tuesday.

2010-219.sentence: Ego psychology sits on Erikson’s industry-versus-inferiority task: envy and rage at someone who seems more competent get handled by defenses, not by drive discharge. Name the defense—devaluation, denial, projection—and you are watching how the person tries to stay industrious without collapsing into inferiority.

2010-221.sentence: CATIE found second-generation antipsychotics were no more effective than first-generation ones; most patients still quit. Ego strength here is the capacity to stay on a drug through weight gain or akathisia without treating “newer” as a magic increase in coping.

2010-222.sentence: Dissociative fugue is flight used as a defense: the person leaves the name and the past so the trauma does not have to be felt. Repression then seals the autobiography, which is why the history cannot be recalled even after the traveling stops.

2010-223.sentence: The condolence call can already be an enactment: you and the spouse are living the old rescue instead of naming the loss. Stay with the spouse's feelings; explaining the five-year treatment or offering to treat the family repeats the rescue you could not finish.

2010-224.sentence: The concert lobby is the frame: confidentiality is the limit you hold when no one asked you to speak. Walk past unless the patient greets you first; initiating contact, steering your spouse away, or making introductions spends the patient's secret in public.

2010-227.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler's first insight: I went too far, I am separate, I can come back. The work is the reunion after that brief rupture with the parent, not peer life, adolescent renegotiation, or simply checking in before a risk.

2010-230.sentence: The automatic thought is a fast defense: it slams the door on other meanings so the patient never has to sit with not-knowing. Eliciting and testing that thought is how you stop the defense mid-sentence and ask whether incompetence is fact or just the mind’s first shield.

2010-235.sentence: A threatened court commitment is coercion, not a real choice, so the signature is not informed consent. Suicidality already taxes affect tolerance and impulse control; stacking a legal threat on top does not restore ego strength, it just produces compliance.

2010-236.sentence: ERP works by habituation: the feared cue stays present, the ritual is blocked, and the anxiety curve falls on its own. That is a supportive-behavioral dose, not uncovering; you do not interpret the contamination fantasy while the patient is still flooding.

2010-239.sentence: The rehab team is recruiting you to become the one who smashes the chipper stance and forces mourning. That is countertransference: their anxiety about denial. Support the tetraplegia patient's existing coping and do not confront the medical realities until function, not the team's discomfort, requires it.

2010-244.sentence: Leaving the public place stops the panic, so escape is negatively reinforced: relief teaches the next flight. A trial comment is whether they can see their own part—that the relief, not the street, is training the attacks.

2010-246.sentence: Minimally conscious state means inconsistent command-following, a gesture, or a word—not coma and not reliable awareness. Families will treat that flicker as a full return of the person; you hold the bond without inflating a thumbs-up into recovery.

2010-247.sentence: Suppression is the parent putting fear on a shelf on purpose so she can call the neighbor and get to the hospital. The affect is not gone; it is parked until the kids are covered and she can feel it.

2010-248.sentence: The after-meal cigarette is a cue, not a character flaw: the plate, the coffee, the chair already 'ask' for nicotine. Name the trigger so the craving is a learned pairing you can swap, not proof he cannot quit.

2010-250.sentence: You are being hired as the court's eyes on now, not as biographer or crime-scene mind-reader. If you feel pulled toward old charts or the alleged offense, that is countertransference: you are sliding into advocate or detective instead of testing current grasp of charges, roles, and consequences.

2010-253.sentence: Bringing unconscious conflict into awareness is what the hour is for: the scheduling change is not just logistics, it is the old authority fight arriving as “you are harsh.” Once that collision can be named, the patient has a chance to think it instead of only living it with you.

2010-258.sentence: Preschool animism is expected work, not a diagnosis: the toy bear gets to be “alive” so the child can practice leaving and being left without losing the object. When a 4-year-old says the stuffed animal is sad alone, you are hearing symbolic play come online—ask about language and reciprocity, not whether the bear needs a prescription.

2010-261.sentence: Saying whether Mr. X is even in the practice already breaks the frame: confidentiality covers the fact of treatment, not only what is said in the room. The limit you hold is a sentence that neither confirms nor denies, so a colleague’s curiosity does not become an unauthorized consult.

2010-263.sentence: IPT works the psychosocial task in front of the person—here a role transition—not unconscious conflict, automatic thoughts, or repressed memory. Erikson would name the same job: renegotiate identity and generativity after a life-structure change, in current relationships, not in the buried past.

2010-264.sentence: The essential finding is not theatrical switching; it is extensive inability to recall personal information, the stretch of life that never got a continuous ‘I.’ What cannot be remembered as one story is repeated as another self, so lost time is trauma showing up as a gap rather than a narrative.

2010-266.sentence: The parents’ startle is a harsh conscience scanning the playroom for pathology; the child’s “monster will never catch us” is ordinary preschool private speech, not a command hallucination. Let the child keep the monster in the toys so the real-world rules stay light enough to play with.

2010-268.sentence: Autonomy is not a pamphlet dump; it is matching diagnosis, options, and risks to what this ego can actually hold without flooding. If you outrun their affect tolerance or reality testing, you have performed informed consent on paper and left them alone with the choice.

2010-269.sentence: Nightly clonazepam, now 5 mg after a spouse’s death, has become the stand-in for the person who used to make sleep feel safe. A slow taper is a planned separation: you stay as the secure base while the pill stops pretending it can replace a lost attachment.

2010-270.sentence: After one surge of cramps and palpitations in the OR, the surgeon rearranges the world so help is always nearby—no ED call, no crowds, no noisy rooms. That is agoraphobia without panic: using proximity to safety to regulate the body instead of trusting the setting to be survivable.

2010-271.sentence: Intrafamilial violence hits the ego’s shock absorbers hardest because the person who should help the child metabolize terror is often the source of it. Affect tolerance and reality testing then have to grow inside a home that keeps rewriting what “safe” means.

2010-274.sentence: A prior alcohol or other-drug abuse history is the finding that should raise concern, not daily alprazolam, potency, or rebound after a taper. Denial here is not “I have no anxiety”; it is treating physiologic dependence as if it were proof of character, so the real risk factor gets waved away.

2010-276.sentence: Conversion can split motor control off from awareness: the teen’s legs fail while the person stays in the chair, not faking and not fully owning the paralysis. Rehabilitative treatment works because it invites the body back into function without forcing the split to confess.

2010-279.sentence: The surgeon cannot keep the hospital’s ordinary demands inside as thinkable disappointment; he evacuates them as persecution so they will not become nameless dread. Containment here means holding the raw betrayal-feeling long enough to ask what happened, without agreeing that peer review was an attack.

2010-282.sentence: A self-help group is not there to remodel personality or harvest insight; it mirrors competence while people practice not drinking. Self-esteem grows from “I did the next right behavior,” not from being idealized as newly analyzed.

2010-283.sentence: A trance is not “spacing out.” It is evacuation: the mind dumps a raw, unthinkable feeling so it never has to become a thought. Bion would say nobody contained the dread—held it and named it—so the patient leaves the scene in altered consciousness instead of remembering it.

2010-285.sentence: A no-show fee is ethical only after the rule has actually arrived—told in advance, in words the patient can use. Surprise billing is not a frame; it is a parent who invents the law after the child already broke it.

2010-287.sentence: Ask for the patient’s explanation of the illness or you will be recruited as the knowing outsider who already named it. That is the cultural formulation’s job: keep their story in the room so your countertransference does not write the chart first.

2010-288.sentence: Liaison is teaching, not another consult note. Staff often use denial—they refuse the feeling the patient is dumping on the ward—and a brief lesson names that feeling so it does not have to become a fight.

2010-290.sentence: Adult inattention is the ADHD piece most likely to stay, and a harsh superego—the inner judge—often misreads missed deadlines as laziness rather than a remaining attentional deficit. Treat that moral verdict as the problem in the room: guilt is doing diagnostic work that belongs to history of childhood onset, not character.

2010-292.sentence: The topographical model (conscious / preconscious / unconscious) is not furniture; it names what a memory is doing for the person. A childhood address can sit preconscious—available after a prompt—while a conflictual wish stays unconscious so it can only arrive as a dream, a slip, or a defense.

2010-297.sentence: Rotter’s internal locus is not “I caused everything”; it is the expectation that my act will reach a valued goal. Until that expectancy is even a little believable, stay supportive and behavioral; heavy uncovering of why they feel powerless will only confirm that luck and other people run the show.

2010-298.sentence: In late-life depression the clock of thought—information-processing speed—can come back when mood remits; motor dexterity, visuospatial skill, and performance IQ are less likely to snap back. Hold the frame around time: slower answers now are a treatable state, not a new identity as “demented,” so you do not drop the hour or the hope just because the visit runs long.

2010-299.sentence: The stamped-envelope question tests judgment: can they choose a safe, socially fitting act in a made-up bind. Insight is whether they see their own part; if they cannot even pick a decent hypothetical action, a trial comment about motive will bounce—stay concrete until judgment is back online.

2010-300.sentence: Gradual personality change, hygiene collapse, anomia, and grasp/suck reflexes point to frontotemporal dementia, not Alzheimer or Lewy body disease. Meds here are not a feed that restores the old self; they are often experienced as a demand on a frontal system that no longer holds the “who I am” object, so you treat the family relationship and safety, not a pill as proof you can give the person back.

2011-4.sentence: Ethnicity is the developmental we-ness that ties common ancestry to a shared story, not the surface markers of race, language, or religion. Asking which communities the patient belongs to treats identity as a living task, not a box you can infer from the face.

2011-5.sentence: Blows to the abdomen in pregnancy attack a third who cannot yet speak; the violence is written on the body when it cannot be named in the room. Unexplained abdominal pain and a fearful partner visit are that unrepresented assault repeating until someone asks in private.

2011-8.sentence: Clarification is not a clever paraphrase; it is a secure-base move: you put their wish into words so they can feel held before anyone reaches for a pill. The last psychiatrist’s brief, med-only visits were a failed proximity—no listening, no regulation through another mind.

2011-12.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sort Test asks whether the patient can drop a dead rule after feedback and take a new one—that is executive set-shifting, not naming or word-list memory. Psychological mindedness is the same muscle: can they use a trial comment (the tester’s “wrong”) to see their own stuck strategy and change it.

2011-13.sentence: Hold the frame at one week: maternity blues is a time-limited lability, not a license to skip safety, bonding, or follow-up just because she “has no complaints.” Name the limit out loud—crying without persistent sad mood or psychosis is expected now, but if sleep, attachment, or reality testing break, you escalate, you do not wait for her to ask.

2011-15.sentence: The sick role is the prize: assuming the patient identity soothes something that ordinary life does not, even when no lawsuit, narcotic, or disability check is on the table. That is not malingering’s external incentive and not hypochondriasis’s fear of disease—it is a defense that keeps the self organized around being cared for as ill.

2011-16.sentence: The phallic-stage discovery isn't really about anatomy — it's the child first grasping that mom and dad have a relationship that exists without him, and that jolt of exclusion is where ordinary oedipal jealousy comes from.

2011-18.sentence: Insecure attachment tracks the caretaker who does not answer hunger, distress, or reunion—not the job, the adoption papers, or a temperament mismatch. Ego strength in the infant grows when someone reliably metabolizes those signals; unresponsiveness plus poor-quality daycare leaves the baby with no place to put the affect.

2011-19.sentence: A loaded gun in the house is not a secure base; it is a lethal object sitting where attachment should regulate panic. Ask about firearms and lock them away so the resident, partner, or parent can be the person who holds the affect instead of a trigger.

2011-20.sentence: Directed masturbation plus couples therapy is the dose of uncovering this complaint can use: the couple’s bed, not a couch. Yohimbine, tramadol, a group, or psychoanalysis would treat a different mind than anorgasmia that lives between two people.

2011-21.sentence: Neglect is the most common maltreatment because it is a two-person failure: no one keeps showing up with food, school, medicine, or eyes on the child. Abandonment, sexual abuse, ritual abuse, and physical abuse are louder; the prevalent pattern is the caregiver who simply does not complete the care.

2011-24.sentence: Hair-pulling isn't a thrill-seeking act — it's tension relief: the urge builds, the pull makes it drop, and that relief is what negatively reinforces the habit and keeps it going.

2011-26.sentence: The cousin is doing the attachment work the interview asked of the patient: proximity to a vivid other instead of staying with you as a secure base for a yes-or-no about mania. Tangentiality is that departure—the story never comes back—so the patient regulates closeness by talking about someone else rather than risking a direct answer.

2011-28.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler’s ethics of the frame: mother is the one who holds time and location, and the child keeps checking where she actually is. The 18-month-old’s marked worry about separation is not regression into symbiosis; it is the work of using a real parent as the limit while still wanting to roam.

2011-32.sentence: An 8-to-12-year-old with depression more often brings a stomachache than adult-style hopelessness, anhedonia, or hypersomnia. Stay near the body first: name the pain, keep school going, and do not force uncovering of despair the child’s mind cannot yet put into words.

2011-34.sentence: The developmental move is to let the patient use a current AA member as a third, not to become the parent who drives, hints, waives the copay, or makes care hostage to a signed card. That is how a reluctant adult grows a capacity to borrow another recovering ego instead of remaining fused with—or defiant toward—you.

2011-35.sentence: Ask how the family actually reads with the child. That scene shows whether learning lives under a harsh “do it or else” conscience or under a shared, usable voice the child can take in. Discipline history and diagnoses matter later; the reading pair is where guilt or pride about letters is being installed right now.

2011-36.sentence: Six admissions, no stable housing, and no follow-through on treatment mean this patient can't yet hold his care together on his own — assertive community treatment builds the team around him instead of expecting him to walk it in the door.

2011-39.sentence: When someone says exercise is pointless until the back is gone, the pair can start living that rule instead of treating it: that is an enactment, a two-person repetition of “nothing counts until pain is erased.” Group CBT’s actual target—function despite pain—is the move that stops that scene.

2011-40.sentence: Naming alprazolam at 2 mg four times a day is the wish for instant quiet; the blank first-attack history is the colliding prohibition against being seen as a seeker. Substance abuse lives in that collision: the drug is requested as medicine so the craving never has to be named.

2011-41.sentence: In CBT, feelings of devaluation—not anergy or anhedonia—are what keep major depression going. Often that “I am useless” line is not a new thought at all; it is an old verdict that never became a memory, so it keeps repeating as a body-and-mind shutdown.

2011-42.sentence: The many-site complaints after a negative workup recruit you either as the doctor who dismisses the body or the one who chases another specialist. Regular scheduled visits with a physical exam refuse both roles: you stay a steady, examining presence instead of proving or disproving the lump in the throat.

2011-44.sentence: What arrives in separation anxiety is not generic clinginess but a specific mental picture: while we are apart, something catastrophic will happen to me or to my caretaker. Other childhood anxieties can look like the same tears at the door; this one is organized around harm-to-the-dyad, not around social scrutiny or a grab-bag of worries that only happen to quiet near mom.

2011-46.sentence: Trust versus mistrust starts before speech because the newborn already comes equipped: face preference, voice tracking, and cross-modal matching that let a caregiver become a recognizable person. Attachment is not something you install after a mythical autistic phase; those built-in perceptual skills are how the infant recruits a reliable other in the first months.

2011-48.sentence: In Capgras the loved person is split: the face is recognized, but the feeling of “this is my father” is ripped off and dumped into an impostor. Klein would call that projective identification in delusional form—the bad or dead version of the object is evacuated into a look-alike so the mind does not have to hold love and threat in one father.

2011-53.sentence: Between eight and eleven, ego strength shows up as internalization of parental values: the rule holds when no adult is watching. That is impulse control moving inside; altruism and abstract rights come later and should not be demanded yet.

2011-54.sentence: Catastrophe skips to termination—“I failed, so I never graduate”—and tries to end the story in one sentence. Listing evidence for and against failing out of college is the CBT limit: stay in the hour, do not soothe or excavate childhood, and do not let the exam become a premature goodbye.

2011-57.sentence: Flat face is not an empty tank; the pleasure that actually drops in schizophrenia is social interaction, the live give-and-take with another person. A pill can feel like feed or poison, but it cannot substitute for that missing social reward—so do not treat the face as if the meal, the song, or the drug high were gone too.

2011-60.sentence: Secure preschool attachment shows up as empathy and altruism: the child can feel another’s distress and still offer a toy, because the caregiver remains a usable base. That is not a split-off self leaving the room; it is one mind that can stay with both need and the other person’s need.

2011-62.sentence: Interviewing all parties is the forensic version of a secure base: the child and each parent get a fair proximity to the evaluator, not just the parent who hired you. Skip one side and you become an attachment figure for the retaining parent’s protest, not a neutral assessor.

2011-63.sentence: Reactive mood in atypical depression means the ego can still take in a good object and briefly lift—affect tolerance is not locked in melancholic shutdown. That flicker of lift after a friend or good news is a strength sign, not proof the depression is “not real.”

2011-64.sentence: The enuresis alarm asks the child and family to stay with wet nights until the signal becomes internal; that is more uncovering of a habit loop than desmopressin’s overnight cover. Lower relapse is the payoff of building a mind that can wake itself, not a drug that holds the symptom while camp week passes.

2011-65.sentence: Months after whole brain radiation, the leukoencephalopathy can look like the patient “checked out” of the relationship—apathy, slow thinking, unsteady gait—when the white-matter hit is doing the withdrawing. Name the delayed radiation injury with the family so you do not treat the pair as if they are jointly refusing care.

2011-68.sentence: Talking about an advance directive while the patient is competent is mirroring: you reflect a whole self that can still choose, not a collapsed one on a vent. Wait until life support or “only if they ask,” and you stop idealizing their agency and treat competence as something the family or the admission desk can lend them.

2011-69.sentence: Competence to proceed is a current-functioning question—can this defendant understand the courtroom and assist counsel today, Dusky-style—not what psychosis did at the time of the offense. The evaluator’s wish to settle guilt collides with the legal prohibition against turning a CST exam into a stealth insanity or mens rea interview.

2011-72.sentence: Preparation is the moment the patient can name marijuana’s cost to school, money, and mood and commit to a plan without having changed use yet. The old cancelling was a vertical split—the using self left the room while the body stayed booked; showing up consistently means those parts are in the same chair long enough to plan.

2011-74.sentence: Davanloo treats the defense as the problem in the hour, not as a polite delay. When the patient smiles, intellectualizes, or goes vague, you name that maneuver and hold them to the feeling it is covering, rather than chasing Oedipus, a preset termination date, or an interpersonal formulation.

2011-79.sentence: Staff’s “she’s getting back at us” story is a sanctioned gap in morality: incontinence is recoded as a moral offense so the unit can feel righteous instead of late. Timed voiding, independent of requests, treats the bladder and the memory deficit, and it also stops punishing an 82-year-old for urgency she cannot hold.

2011-81.sentence: The remembered train-and-panic scene is the manifest dream: the version the mind can hold after sleep has done its work. Dream work has already contained the raw wish and dread—Bion’s nameless feeling made thinkable—so what you hear at the seminar is the evacuated night, not the latent content.

2011-82.sentence: Suicide or attempted suicide is the allegation that most often lands in court, and it hits the psychiatrist’s self where competence and the wish to be a protecting ideal live. Careful documentation of thoughts, intent, plan, means, and the why of your decision is also a self-object function: it mirrors that you thought, so you can survive the patient’s despair without collapsing into omnipotent rescue or frozen shame.

2011-83.sentence: In CBT, humor is licensed when it loosens a distorted cognition—one error equals total incompetence—so a new perspective can enter. The wish to be flawless and the prohibition against looking foolish collide in that all-or-nothing thought; a well-timed joke lets the collision become thinkable instead of another humiliation.

2011-84.sentence: Norming is when members stop using avoidance of difference as their group defense and can show who they actually are. Early silence and waiting for the leader is suppression of conflict; once that thins, experiential learning can start because disagreement is no longer treated as a threat to the group’s skin.

2011-85.sentence: Bradylalia is not just a motor lag; it can feel like the session itself is starving you of a reply. The slow words become a demand for patience, and if you fill the silence too fast you are treating the delay as poison instead of as the depression speaking.

2011-86.sentence: Burning, shock-like neuropathic pain is a real limit, not a debate about whether the patient is “psychogenic.” Hold the frame: name the pain type, treat the nerve injury, and do not make the patient prove they deserve relief.

2011-91.sentence: She is treating the household food as poison, not as a meal. A family meeting puts the contested feed on the table so you do not answer that fear with risperidone or a clearance stamp.

2011-95.sentence: The note has to show you could stand the anxiety of not restraining or over-intervening. Write why you rejected those other responses so the chart records judgment, not only a risk label.

2011-98.sentence: A ten-year sentence on an adult child often lands as a verdict on the parent: the conscience may treat the conviction as proof of failed rearing and collect the debt as low mood and middle insomnia. That is adjustment disorder with depressed mood, not major depression—the sadness is a guilt payment timed to the courtroom, not a free-standing episode.

2011-99.sentence: APA ethics treat the erotic transference as never fully discharged: you remain the doctor in the patient's inner courtroom even after the last session. A date request from a former patient is recruitment into that leftover role, not informed consent—so sex with current or former patients is not allowed.

2011-100.sentence: Four sessions of a monopolizer turn the group into a hanging jury: members stop listening and start punishing, which is how a group conscience goes rigid. Cohesiveness—the felt we that lets people stay in the room—is what that moral rallying against the talker quietly kills.

2011-101.sentence: Primary process is the mind running on wish alone — time collapses and the wanted thing simply arrives, the way a dream just hands you what waking life makes you work for.

2011-103.sentence: Telepsychiatry asks for a developmental capacity that many psychiatrists never quite grew: staying present with a person when the body is not in the room. Reluctance is not only logistics; it is a late-arriving comfort with a new way of being with someone, and until that capacity arrives the platform sits unused.

2011-105.sentence: Socratic questioning is containment: you hold the raw “I am incompetent” long enough for it to become a thought you can examine, not a feeling that has to be evacuated as fact. Exposure, free association, guided imagery, and motivational interviewing do other jobs; they do not turn the automatic thought into something thinkable the way a good question does.

2011-109.sentence: This patient has learned that medications betray him with side effects before they help — stopping fluoxetine now would confirm that story instead of testing whether it's still true. Treating the night sweats with terazosin lets the first medication that's actually working stay in place, so trust in treatment gets built rather than broken again.

2011-110.sentence: Two years out from a car accident, it's tempting to hear 'new weakness' as secondary gain or a stalled lawsuit — but the cape-like loss of pain and temperature with reflexes gone is a syrinx, a real lesion that can take years to become symptomatic. Let the exam, not your suspicion about litigation, decide whether this is anatomy or exaggeration.

2011-111.sentence: Saying she's 'okay' about a rape she just disclosed is not denial to argue her out of — it's likely dissociation, her mind's way of not being fully present for something unbearable. Grounding her in the room, in her body, in now comes before you ask her to narrate the trauma; you can't process a memory from outside your own body.

2011-112.sentence: Little Hans’s horse phobia is castration anxiety with a costume: the boy’s conscience, his emerging superego, converts the forbidden Oedipal wish into a single avoidable animal. Stay off the street and you never have to feel guilty about wanting mother or rivaling father.

2011-119.sentence: Winnicott's point isn't that a parent should shield a child from every frustration — it's that the parent stays attuned enough to notice when the child is ready to push outward and explore. That responsiveness to a child's own timing, more than any specific technique, is what lets curiosity grow instead of being smothered or abandoned.

2011-122.sentence: The suicide attempt is doing work the patient could not say: it turns “I could not reach you” into a crisis that cannot be ignored. Abandonment is the legal name for that same rupture—vacation without coverage—so the act is both a plea and an indictment of the missing covering clinician.

2011-123.sentence: What never quite arrived in this adolescent is a reliable brake: the capacity to pause between feeling and act. The reported cluster with serotonin dysregulation, suicidality, and aggression in borderline youth is impulsivity, not merely anger—so safety planning has to treat the missing delay, not only the mood.

2011-128.sentence: A pregnant patient hearing 'stay on methadone' often carries the same fear the field once had — that any drug near a fetus must be poison, even when it's the treatment that protects the pregnancy. Naming methadone maintenance as evidence-based care, not a lesser evil, is often what actually keeps a mother in treatment.

2011-129.sentence: The cancel splits the hour: one self sits in the chair, another is already back with the unavailable father. Interpret that transference out loud so the two states can meet instead of the patient leaving the treatment to stay loyal to the old absence.

2011-133.sentence: Clozapine is not only the last-line antipsychotic here; for a patient who gets more paranoid and then uses cocaine, the pill can feel like a feed that quiets the voices enough to make abstinence imaginable. If the resident treats clozapine as a demand for blood draws and compliance, the patient hears poison, not help—and the coke returns when the relationship around the tablet goes cold.

2011-134.sentence: A first focal-onset seizure that secondarily generalizes at 58 is a brain that may be carrying glioblastoma, not a mind ready for uncovering work. Keep the stance supportive and concrete: image, neurology, and containment of panic, because digging for meaning while the cortex is under a mass is technique that outruns what this ego can use.

2011-135.sentence: A self-help group is two (or twenty) people practicing a new interpersonal pattern: they interrupt drinking together, they do not excavate childhood. The goal is overcoming maladaptive behaviors—the room becomes a living lab where the old drinking dyad is replaced by a sober one, not insight into psychodynamics or a personality overhaul.

2011-137.sentence: Needle exchange is harm reduction: you meet a mind that cannot yet tolerate abstinence and you shore up ego strength—impulse control, reality testing about overdose and infection—without demanding an identity change first. Supply, access, and demand strategies fight the drug market; this one fights death while the patient is still using.

2011-139.sentence: Age less than 35 is the suicide risk that belongs to schizophrenia, not to the general population, because the drive to live and the wish to erase a new, shaming identity collide before a workable self has formed. The early course is not just statistics; it is a young ego still arguing with a diagnosis it cannot yet metabolize.

2011-140.sentence: Tuskegee failed on the risk:benefit ratio because investigators used denial: they called untreated syphilis “observation” so they would not have to feel they were harming Black men. Denial here is not forgetting facts; it is keeping the harm out of awareness so the study can continue.

2011-141.sentence: Ask about the escalating time and the upgraded equipment, then the irritability when the connection is cut, as a story about a relationship the patient can't easily leave — not just a checklist of criteria. Naming tolerance and withdrawal to internet use out loud, rather than only counting them, is what actually gets a patient talking about the loss of control underneath.

2011-143.sentence: Most hypnosis isn't the therapist handing down commands — it's an invitation for the patient to use coping resources they already have, with the clinician as guide rather than authority. Treating trance as something done with the patient, not to them, is what actually makes most techniques work.

2011-145.sentence: The daughter's request to keep the patient home can hide her own exhaustion, so burnout is the part of the story that needs to be seen, not another behavior plan. A trial comment—“How are you holding up with this?”—tests whether she can use that insight, or whether time-outs and restraints will just get dumped on an already depleted caregiver.

2011-147.sentence: Panic turns a heartbeat into nameless dread: a raw sensation that the mind cannot think, so it gets evacuated into another ER visit. CBT’s job is containment—rename palpitations as a misfired alarm, not a dying heart, until the feeling becomes thinkable instead of something to dump.

2011-151.sentence: Intense mood is not just “a difficult kid.” It is a signal the child is using to move the environment: get you closer, get you to stop the novelty, get the world back on a predictable clock. Thomas and Chess’s difficult temperament clusters that intensity with irregular sleep/feeding and withdrawal from new situations, so the job is to name the signal without treating the child as a character defect.

2011-153.sentence: A patient who develops priapism on trazodone needs to hear, in advance, that a prolonged erection is a medical emergency and not something shameful to hide until it's too late. Counseling this plainly turns embarrassment into action — the difference between calling you and losing tissue to ischemia.

2011-155.sentence: Cortical brain death leaves no shared memory of the person, so the adult child and the dissenting nurse repeat the lost relationship in the unit: they keep the body “alive” as a stand-in for a goodbye that cannot be thought. Meet family and staff separately first; the polarization is the unrepresented grief, not a debate you win by confronting hope.

2011-156.sentence: Klein put the infant’s earliest objects—breast, mother, the split good/bad other—at the center, earlier than Freud’s later Oedipal theater. When a patient floods the team with idealization then condemnation, they are evacuating raw bits they cannot yet think; your job is to contain that (hold it, name it) so it can become a thought instead of a war.

2011-158.sentence: The DSM-IV-TR label of impulse control disorder NOS fits because skin picking often happens without the patient noticing the urge until the skin is already broken. Asking what they feel in the second before their fingers move starts building the awareness that has to exist before any urge can be resisted.

2011-159.sentence: Extinction is an ending you cannot hurry: you withdraw the unconditioned stimulus and wait while the conditioned response dies of neglect. The association weakens only after the expected catastrophe keeps not arriving; rushing that interval is just more pairing in disguise.

2011-160.sentence: The MMPI-2 Lie scale catches denial dressed as virtue: the person endorses social-desirability items and erases ordinary faults. That is not a pretty personality; it is a defense that says nothing bad about me can be seen, so you do not interpret the clinical scales until you name the lie.

2011-162.sentence: A no-harm contract has no significant empirical support, and it can invite a vertical split: the patient signs while another part stays suicidal. They leave without leaving the chair—the signature is dissociated compliance, not a whole person agreeing, and it lets both of you stop looking.

2011-166.sentence: IPT starts by mapping current social connections, not childhood or unconscious conflict, because the work lives in the living network. Holding that frame means you do not drift into character analysis when the task is grief, role change, dispute, or thin support.

2011-172.sentence: Middle-phase IPT keeps the work inside current relationships—the role dispute this week—not transference or childhood archaeology. The limit is the clock: you do not rush an old wound into insight on IPT time.

2011-174.sentence: The observing ego is the part of the mind that can step back and turn a raw urge into a sentence — 'I felt small, then I wanted to attack' — instead of just acting on it. Strengthening that capacity to watch one's own drives is much of what insight-oriented work is actually building.

2011-176.sentence: Psychosis and mania leave families with terror that has no story, so they repeat it as blame, hovering, and sleepless nights. Multifamily psychoeducation that provides knowledge and direct guidance gives the illness words and a map, so the group can think instead of only living the unrepresented panic.

2011-178.sentence: If this mind can make a story from an ambiguous TAT picture, it can probably use uncovering of unconscious drive and conflict. Reach for the TAT when you need those themes; the SCID and MMPI-2 will inventory symptoms and traits but will not show you the wish.

2011-180.sentence: You cannot rush the end of the drinking; motivational interviewing holds that limit by refusing advice and confrontation. Develop discrepancy—the gap between the valued self and what alcohol is costing—and let the patient’s own timeline close it.

2011-181.sentence: A 77-year-old with stable bipolar disorder who says work feels slower, while mood and pleasure are intact, is easy to wave off as 'aging' or a med side effect — but that mismatch is exactly why you check B12 before blaming the illness or the drugs. Taking a new complaint seriously enough to test for a reversible cause, instead of folding it back into the psychiatric story, is its own form of respect.

2011-184.sentence: Ease, named pain, compassion, a look at insight, and shown expertise loosen the patient’s first defense—often a stiff, judging distance that keeps the doctor from mattering. Rapport is what fills that space once they can suppress (hold back, not bury) the fear of being exposed, instead of needing reflection or transference as the main tool.

2011-185.sentence: It's easy for a team to file a suicidal patient under 'personality,' 'just anxiety,' or 'it's the alcohol' and let the underlying despair go unspoken — but mood disorders are the diagnostic category most associated with completed suicide, more than any of those labels. Naming the depression instead of the story around it is what keeps the visit a real suicide assessment.

2011-186.sentence: The frame here is not to turn church-shopping and guilty doubt into OCD or bipolar when the rest of the mental status is clear and she will not act against her morals. Hold the limit as a religious or spiritual problem: explore meaning and supports without medicalizing her faith, and do not report or medicate a crisis of affiliation.

2011-190.sentence: Object relations says the mind is stocked with pictures of self and other; self psychology asks what those pictures do for esteem. When the therapist stops mirroring, the inner other flips from idealized protector to cruel rejecter — same furniture, different job: holding the self together.

2011-191.sentence: The street offense is a collision: a wish to stay free and untreated versus a community that wants punishment. Mental health court is the compromise formation — it aims the same defendant at treatment rather than jail instead of pretending the drive or the prohibition disappeared.

2011-193.sentence: A worried family often wants an IQ number long before seven, hoping a score will settle 'is something wrong with my child' — but a number given that early can't hold still and mostly repackages the anxiety, not the truth. Waiting until IQ is actually stable turns that fear into a fact you can work with, instead of a verdict handed down too soon.

2011-199.sentence: Isolation of affect lets this patient keep every detail of watching his father kill the puppy while the feeling that belongs to it stays elsewhere — he can recite horror without touching it. Your own wave of distress listening to him is a clue to what's missing from his account, not proof that he felt nothing at the time.

2011-200.sentence: ADHD here is a developmental lag in the child's own brakes, not a failure of will. Parent behavioral management is the adult becoming a temporary external executive—clear cues, consistent consequences—until that capacity arrives more fully.

2011-202.sentence: Infants under three cannot recruit you with words, so they recruit you with an injury that does not match what a baby can do. Countertransference will pull you toward the caregiver's story or toward rage; hold the protector role and get pediatrics and safeguarding in the room.

2011-203.sentence: A dinner-table monkey at four and a half is ordinary preschool play, not a crime against reality. The worry to watch is a rigid parental conscience that treats imagination as lying; if the play is friendly and the rest of development is on track, you loosen that rule, you do not pathologize the child.

2011-204.sentence: Skepticism about “talking about the past” is happening now, in the hour, as a test of whether you will lecture, go silent, or stay with him. The frame is the alliance: explore what in this session makes partnership feel unsafe before you sell the method or call it resistance.

2011-205.sentence: Asking for S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAMe) is often a bid to change mood without taking on the identity of a psychiatric patient. SAMe is a methyl donor with modest antidepressant signal, so the wish is not empty—but it still needs the same bipolar, severity, and interaction screen you would give any mood treatment.

2011-206.sentence: Severe factitious illness often rides with borderline personality because the need to be held is acted out on the body instead of said. That is acting out: the ward becomes the theater of care-seeking and rage, while the wish to be dependent stays out of words.

2011-210.sentence: Twice-weekly binge–purge at a normal weight is bulimia nervosa, and the referral already recruits you as the one who will watch the body. Watch the countertransference—disgust, fascination, or an urge to police food—because that is the old audience being installed in the room.

2011-212.sentence: Lorazepam 2 mg IM, with a repeat at 45 minutes, is the adult capacity that this intoxicated patient never quite has in the moment: a frontal brake that can wait, listen, and not throw the tray. You are not treating a character; you are lending a late-arriving inhibitory function until the brain can hold it again.

2011-215.sentence: A few beers and occasional cannabis with friends, while school and attachments hold, is typical adolescent use: the symptom is doing affiliation, not self-destruction. It marks belonging at the party more than a hole in self-esteem or a hidden family war.

2011-217.sentence: Go/no-go is a test of the ego's brake: tap once when asked, hold still when the second tap arrives. Executive functioning is that pause between impulse and action, the same pause a distractible inpatient loses when a line or button is sitting there to be pulled.

2011-218.sentence: Selective mutism is not a language hole; it is a solution that keeps the child's voice at home, where it feels safe, and locks it at school. The silence is the symptom's job: it avoids the feared audience rather than proving the child cannot speak.

2011-219.sentence: Ordinary grief still lets longing and even a sense of the dead person's presence do their work; early, heavy depressive symptoms mean the anger of the loss has already turned inward. That is turning against the self: the 80-year-old is attacking the surviving self instead of mourning the spouse.

2011-221.sentence: Financial stress is not a moral verdict on parents; it is a load that thins affect tolerance and impulse control while several children still need care. Abuse risk rises when the caregiver's ego is depleted by rent, job loss, and exhaustion, not because two-parent homes or older teens are the usual setting.

2011-223.sentence: The team can use denial—the mind simply refuses to register a cause that is sitting in the med list—and treat the new gloom, anxiety, and fog as “just hepatitis C.” Interferon-alpha is the named culprit; name it so the affect can be treated instead of waved away.

2011-227.sentence: You cannot rush a crisp story out of someone whose job, in a compensation case, is to stay blurry. Vaguely defined, shifting symptoms are the tell; the consulting limit is to record the fog, not to write the plot they will not give.

2011-231.sentence: The late-maturing prefrontal cortex is the brake on a wish that adolescence still floors: drive arrives first, prohibition arrives later. That is why a 15-year-old can name a future in a calm room and still chase the impulse when the wish is hot.

2011-234.sentence: Huntington’s CAG story asks for support first: this mind is losing cortical control, so deep uncovering of irritability will not restore a dying striatum. Technique follows prognosis—name the autosomal-dominant illness, then keep the work concrete and containing.

2011-235.sentence: Frotteurism uses the ordinary cover of a routine exam — the stool, the angle, the knees — to get contact with a forbidden object without ever having to name the wish out loud, even to himself. The exam room's normal choreography is exactly what lets the impulse hide in plain sight.

2011-236.sentence: Sedative-hypnotic (and alcohol) withdrawal can kill with seizures and delirium; cocaine, opioids, PCP, and MDMA withdrawal are miserable, not typically lethal that way. The moral trap is a harsh conscience that treats “just stop” as virtue while ignoring GABA downregulation—guilt about using is not a substitute for a taper.

2011-237.sentence: Contemplation is “it may be a problem… I’ll think about it”: he can see the alcohol and still not choose. You are being recruited as either the scolding wife or the enabler who lets him off the hook; stay the third person who names ambivalence without becoming either.

2011-244.sentence: DBT’s telephone consultation is a developmental crutch: a brief coach in the gap where a reliable inner parent never quite arrived. The call is not extra therapy; it is practice holding the urge until distress-tolerance can live inside the patient.

2011-245.sentence: The spiritual language in AA can function as a container for craving, but the outcome data do not make a spiritual awakening the engine of abstinence. Treat “higher power” as one possible meaning of the ritual, not as the required mechanism—and do not force a religious story on someone who needs a different one.

2011-247.sentence: A remote suicide attempt or a period of deep hopelessness doesn't expire — it can sit quietly for years and still be the risk factor that matters most when you're assessing someone today. Ask about the old attempt and the old despair as if they happened last month, because for suicide risk, they still count that way.

2011-256.sentence: Pretend play hinges on using one object to represent another, so a trial comment can land: “The block is Grandma’s phone.” If the child can play with that idea, you are seeing the start of psychological mindedness, not just language, peer cooperation, or following rules.

2011-259.sentence: Disruptive behavior is the ticket that gets the child into the room, not the diagnosis. The outburst can be doing work for the child—protest, rescue-seeking, or a way to make an unbearable classroom feeling land on someone else—so you still have to ask what the fighting is accomplishing before you treat the referral label.

2011-261.sentence: A sponsor is not a pamphlet; it is a living other who can hold what the alcoholic cannot yet put into words. Unrepresented craving and shame get repeated in the body as the next drink unless they are spoken into a relationship that can stay when the story is ugly.

2011-262.sentence: Lithium is the one to hold before ECT because it can worsen postictal confusion and prolong seizures—you are not being recruited as the withholding parent, you are protecting the brain during a seizure. Notice the countertransference pull to keep every mood stabilizer going so you do not feel like you abandoned a bipolar patient; the team still stops lithium.

2011-265.sentence: Postpartum psychosis does not wait for insight to ripen. The hard limit is the infant’s life: infanticide can arrive before the mother can think, so the job is hold and protect, not wait for her to “settle.”

2011-268.sentence: Supportive therapy gratifies dependency on purpose: you do some of the holding so the patient need not pretend they can. Watch the enactment—the two of you living “I cannot function unless you do it”—and name that rather than only filling out more forms.

2011-269.sentence: Binge eating disorder usually does not keep a normal weight because nothing cancels the intake. Bulimia’s typical defense is undoing—vomit, restrict, exercise—to erase the binge; without that ritual, the body records what the mind will not metabolize.

2011-271.sentence: A child who passes the false-belief marble task can hold two minds at once: what they know and what the other doll still believes. That capacity is your green light for more uncovering work; if the patient cannot yet imagine a mind that is wrong, stay supportive and name states rather than interpret hidden motives.

2011-272.sentence: Right after an assault, her body doesn't automatically know the danger is over -- until someone puts words to "you are safe now, he is not in this room," every stranger in scrubs can still register as another threat. Naming the safety out loud is the first repair, before insight or information can even land.

2011-276.sentence: A self-help group keeps the shared problem—the drink, the illness—as the task and does not treat the group itself as the patient. That is the point of the symptom there: it organizes belonging and practical hope, not exploration of who is angry at whom in the room.

2011-279.sentence: Antisocial personality recruits the group into prey and predator: you will feel used, and the other members will feel unsafe. That is the transference you are refusing to host—an outpatient process group cannot survive becoming the crime scene.

2011-284.sentence: Boundary crossings -- a longer session, a small gift accepted -- aren't automatically violations; the real question is what this particular crossing means for this particular patient, not whether a rule was broken. A gesture that steadies one patient can unsettle another, so judgment has to replace the rulebook.

2011-287.sentence: Reframing turns “lazy” and “controlling” into a family trying to negotiate independence, which is what the fight was doing for them all along. The symptom was a crude job description; positive language lets the same work happen without the insult.

2011-288.sentence: Animism -- believing the teddy bear is alive -- isn't a cognitive error to correct; the toddler is using the object the way Winnicott described, as a bridge between inner feeling and the outside world, where the bear can hold what the child can't yet say. Correcting it with "it's not really alive" takes away the bridge before the child has another way across.

2011-291.sentence: Handing the neighbor a treatment plan makes the two of you a clinical pair, even at a party. Advising cognitive-behavioral therapy with named providers is that step; a card, a resource list, or a general remark about the economy is not.

2011-294.sentence: Avoidance is the defense in play: he will not talk about the crash so the horror stays out of the room, while the dreams and the “spirit leaving the body” still leak through. At three weeks that cluster is acute stress, not PTSD.

2011-298.sentence: A no-show fee is ethical only after you have named the limit out loud, in advance—the APA annotation is notice, not insurance permission or a secret penalty. Ending an hour the patient never used is still an ending; surprise billing turns the limit into a slap.

2011-300.sentence: Conjoint marital therapy is the wrong first technique in active domestic violence: it asks the couple to uncover the fight in the same room where coercion already lives. Start with individual work, meds if needed, and group only if it is safe; joint sessions can worsen the prognosis by putting the victim back under the partner’s gaze.

2012-1.sentence: Transference is the patient bringing an old relationship into the room and living it out with you as though it were new -- anger at a parent showing up as anger at the clinician for running five minutes late. Naming it, rather than accepting or rejecting the feeling at face value, is what turns the reenactment into something you can both use.

2012-5.sentence: Advising sits at the supportive end of the spectrum: right now this patient needs you to lend some organizing structure, not to explore the wish behind the paralysis. Save the interpretation of dependency for later, once the basics -- sleep, meals, function -- are back online.

2012-7.sentence: After sertraline 200 mg, duloxetine 90 mg, and phenelzine 90 mg have failed, the will-updating is recruiting you into shared hopelessness: you become the doctor who agrees nothing works. Feel that pull, then still offer ECT—the modality with the highest chance of remission—instead of matching the despair with another pill trial.

2012-9.sentence: “Doctor, you believe this is happening” is a wish that you join the assassin-and-rape scene; the prohibition is that you must not certify it as fact. “It sounds terrifying” stays with the affect and refuses both the collusion and the cold rebuttal.

2012-12.sentence: Oculogyric crisis after haloperidol 5 mg bid can make the body feel stolen—“can’t see,” stuck looking up—and that terror is not a reason to raise the antipsychotic. Give benztropine 1 mg IV now so the patient can re-own the body; oral diphenhydramine or more haloperidol asks for more affect tolerance than this moment has.

2012-13.sentence: Childhood abuse can leave panic disorder behind as a body that remembers what the mind never got to narrate -- a racing heart and the urge to flee with no story attached to explain why. Treating only the physiology can miss that the alarm is doing exactly what it learned to do.

2012-14.sentence: Adolescence is when the superego finally softens enough to separate "I failed at this" from "I am a failure" -- the capacity to hold a real limitation without it collapsing into shame. That's what lets a teenager set a goal sized to who they actually are, not the perfect self they're still mourning.

2012-18.sentence: IPT’s sick role is a cultural third: depression gets named as illness so class-and-duty talk (“I should snap out of it”) stops running the hour. Permission to recover is not laziness; it is a temporary identity that makes getting well the job.

2012-21.sentence: Suppression is the ego’s deliberate pause: you keep the family fight in awareness and park it until after conference. That is not repression (the conflict is not banished from mind) and not denial (you already know it hurts); it is a conscious, time-limited diversion so thinking can stay online.

2012-22.sentence: “Best interests of the child” is the legal frame, but the consult is already an enactment: two adults are fighting through you instead of holding the child’s anxiety. Your job is to stop living their custody war and name the child’s needs so the court hears functioning, safety, and care, not the parents’ old script.

2012-24.sentence: Offering frequent small sips of water instead of an IV or a feeding tube isn't giving up -- it lets the dying process stay natural while the family's instinct to "do something" gets held instead of acted on. Comfort here means holding the family's panic, not medicalizing the body's failing appetite.

2012-25.sentence: The family and the phone call were her secure base after the overdose; don't let a reassuring lab number become a false one that lets everyone stop paying attention too soon. Staying for the EKG and continued monitoring is what a secure base actually does -- it sticks around until the danger is verified, not just narrated as over.

2012-27.sentence: These parents can use a trial of ordinary curiosity more than they can use uncovering for trauma, a Denver screen, or a lecture on paternal ADHD and ODD. Start by exploring what the tantrums mean to them; if the mind in front of you is the parents’ anxiety, support and clarification beat premature technique.

2012-30.sentence: The temptation is to slide from fact witness into expert witness -- to have an opinion about the lawsuit itself, not just report what you observed and treated. Naming that pull to yourself before you're on the stand is what keeps your testimony honest instead of persuasive.

2012-31.sentence: Around age three, a child can put a birthday or a fall into words after it is over—so time is no longer only now. That new capacity cannot be rushed: until language can hold a past event, you cannot treat the child as if they already have a narrative you can simply interview.

2012-33.sentence: Contemplation is genuine ambivalence, not resistance -- the smoker already knows quitting is right, and pushing for a quit date before they're ready just makes them defend the cigarette to save face. Reflecting the ambivalence back keeps the alliance intact until the patient supplies their own reason to move.

2012-34.sentence: Neurasthenia's fatigue and body complaints usually travel with an anxiety disorder underneath -- and the exam room can quietly replay that split, with you chasing a lesion while the patient hands you a body instead of a fear. Naming the anxiety is what lets the exhaustion stop being the only language available for it.

2012-35.sentence: DBT starts with mindfulness because without noticing the urge, the usual defense is acting out—doing the cut instead of knowing the feeling. Practice observing first so suppression and crisis skills have a mind to land in, not just another behavior to stack.

2012-39.sentence: The suicide threat is doing work: it makes the parents drop the demand, not express a plan to die. Sending her home names that meaning, so you treat coercive rage in a euthymic, logical child instead of using the ED or a locked unit as the parents’ new giving-in.

2012-40.sentence: At home the parents may be caught in projective identification—they feel the “bad, suicidal girl” has been put into them and they surrender. A teacher report is the third mind that checks whether that all-bad object is only a family creation or whether the same split lives at school.

2012-41.sentence: Do not crown the “better” parent or let the child pick a referee; that makes you the extra adult who splits the couple. Explore why they cannot share one limit, because the outburst is living in the gap between two disciplines.

2012-42.sentence: This child does not need insight, mindfulness, or a lecture on how maladaptive she has been. She needs supportive technique: parents ignore the scream, keep the rule, and stop the negative reinforcement that used to cancel the demand.

2012-43.sentence: After a spouse dies, grief needs somewhere to go besides turning the marriage into either a saint story or a well of regret -- good social support is what gives the widow someone to actually say both the love and the anger to. That's why quality of support outpredicts almost everything else in who gets through bereavement well.

2012-45.sentence: Dissociative amnesia hits episodic memory: the lived scenes of “what happened to me with you,” not how to ride a bike or what a chair is called. Two people often keep that gap in place together—the patient cannot recall, and the other quietly agrees not to ask, so the relationship never has to hold the scene.

2012-48.sentence: Start with sex education: menopause, desire, and aging bodies are facts, and naming them undercuts the wife’s quiet denial that she is still a sexual person. Her offer that he find a younger woman is reaction formation dressed as generosity—she turns shame about not feeling sexy into a “kind” push-away.

2012-49.sentence: The patient isn't being difficult -- dry mouth and constipation are real reasons to distrust a drug, and arguing them away only turns the medication into one more thing being forced on them. Choosing desipramine, the least anticholinergic TCA, treats the depression without asking the body to prove the patient's fear wrong.

2012-51.sentence: The transplant is over and the hospital is ending; the anxiety is about leaving a frame that held him through bone marrow transplantation, not a new personality or a full major depression. Adjustment disorder with anxiety names that limit: sleep and discharge fear after an uneventful BMT are a mind catching up to a finish line you cannot rush.

2012-52.sentence: When a patient treats CBT like the one true treatment, the modality itself becomes a badge of being a good patient rather than just a tool. The meta-analyses showing other therapies work about as well are really pointing at what carries the outcome: the relationship, not the brand.

2012-53.sentence: The ethical frame here is whose definition of a healthy self you enforce in the room: Western esteem built on inner attributes and self-defined goals, or non-Western esteem built on contribution to the group and harmony. If you treat caregiving and not burdening relatives as only guilt or dependence, you have already broken the frame by scoring their culture as pathology.

2012-56.sentence: Exposure and response prevention is an ego-strength drill: the patient touches the contaminant and then holds the urge to wash long enough for anxiety to crest and fall. You are building affect tolerance and impulse control, not arguing the germs away.

2012-58.sentence: Clozapine is the only atypical that consistently beats typicals in psychosis, and it only works as a two-person treatment: weekly blood, agranulocytosis talk, the clinic that keeps showing up. The superior efficacy is not a solo receptor story; it is a relationship that can hold the labs and the risk together.

2012-59.sentence: Asking what they think will happen if they refuse treatment isn't a formality -- it tests whether the patient can hold you in mind as someone helping them think through the danger, not just recite the right words back. Competence is that capacity to actually reason with the risk, not just name it.

2012-60.sentence: A corrective emotional experience is what happens when the patient braces for the old parent's judgment and gets acceptance-with-limits instead -- the same expected blow lands differently this time, and that difference is what does the healing. It only works because the new response is real, not staged: the patient has to test it against you before they can believe it.

2012-63.sentence: Activity monitoring is a frame: you hold the hour-by-hour log and the mastery/pleasure ratings so “I do nothing” can be checked against the day, not argued. The psychiatrist sets that task the way one sets a fee or a session time—the limit is the record, not a pep talk.

2012-65.sentence: After a recent attempt, whatever couldn't be put into words often comes back as another act instead of a memory. Suicide-focused CBT works by walking through the moment in language -- naming the thoughts and the sequence -- so the mind has a story it can hold onto instead of a crisis it has to repeat.

2012-66.sentence: Six weeks after a parent’s sudden death, pangs of grief are the wish to find the parent colliding with the fact of loss; that conflict is ordinary bereavement. Persistent avoidance of death reminders marks traumatic grief—the mind refusing the collision rather than letting the wish and the prohibition meet.

2012-69.sentence: Sexual side effects on citalopram can feel like the pill stole a piece of closeness, so the patient starts to pull away from you and the treatment. Offering bupropion is a secure-base move: you stay with the depression work without asking them to sacrifice desire.

2012-70.sentence: The therapeutic alliance is not a nicety; it is what the treatment is doing for the person—making it safe enough to stay. Technique and transference interpretations only work if that bond is already carrying the load.

2012-71.sentence: Regular scheduled visits with the primary doctor answer the trust-versus-mistrust question: someone will be there even when the workup is empty. That appointment is the treatment for somatoform illness, not a courtesy before the next scan.

2012-72.sentence: A young woman with post-flu exhaustion and a day-long crash after housework is easy to recode as depression or personality, and that gendered dismissal is the third person in the room. Name chronic fatigue syndrome so her energy economy is not treated as a character flaw.

2012-78.sentence: Piaget's stages aren't a preference you can talk a child out of: a seven-year-old in concrete operations can't be reasoned into abstract, formal thought no matter how badly the moment calls for it. Meet the mind at the level it actually has, not the level the conversation needs it to have.

2012-82.sentence: In hypochondriasis the feared disease is a bad object parked in the body; the doctor’s clean workup cannot be taken in as a good object. Keep one consistent relationship so good and bad findings can live in the same room instead of each visit becoming a hunt for the hidden killer.

2012-84.sentence: Attraction that blurs the patient’s best interest is a superego emergency: conscience has gone offline and the wish is driving. Supervision is the first use of a borrowed conscience; telling the patient or shrinking the hour just hands them your guilt.

2012-86.sentence: The guilt is doing a job: it keeps the 14-year-old from treating independence as a crime against the parents he still loves. Those harsh parental introjects—inner copies of mom and dad that went quiet in latency—wake up when he pushes back, so he argues and then pays a moral tax.

2012-87.sentence: Insanity work asks whether reality testing held at the moment of the act, not whether schizophrenia is old or whether he took his pill today. "What were the voices saying?" tests if command content, not duration of illness, can show he could not know wrongness when the assault happened.

2012-88.sentence: Ideas of reference already pull you into a two-person scene: the newscaster is "talking about me," so you become either the confirming audience or the one who denies the message. Ask if the link is literal and personal; if you start arguing the news, you are living the conviction instead of examining it.

2012-93.sentence: Family psychoeducation, not structural or paradoxical family therapy, is what actually cuts relapse -- because families are already holding the patient's split-off terror and rage, and dumping it back as blame only makes it worse. Naming the illness, its course, and how to respond turns that unbearable mess into something the family can actually use.

2012-95.sentence: Outpatient groups for schizophrenia aim at social skills, not uncovering unconscious material or delusional content -- the goal is rehearsing something concrete, like greeting a supervisor, while staying grounded in the room. Practice beats interpretation here; the deficit is functional, not a meaning waiting to be found.

2012-104.sentence: A 3½-year-old asking "why is it so fat?" is ordinary curiosity about a whole, real father, not evidence that something is wrong -- kids this age are genuinely fascinated by anatomy, not traumatized by seeing it. Read this as normal development first, before reaching for abuse as the explanation.

2012-105.sentence: An ataque de nervios is the moment the family field cannot hold good and bad in one piece, so the mix dumps out as shaking, shouting, and feeling out of control. That same unheld mix is why these patients so often also meet criteria for major depression, GAD, or PTSD.

2012-108.sentence: Fidelity is the promise that someone who knows the work will still be there; vacation without coverage breaks that promise in the frame. The patient is left holding the treatment alone, which is abandonment dressed up as time off.

2012-111.sentence: Call depersonalization a disturbance of perception and you keep the frame honest: the patient is watching the self from outside, not believing a delusion that must be reported or certified. Insight stays inside the hour—“I know this is not literally happening”—so you treat panic and the body, not thought content.

2012-112.sentence: The well twin’s dread that shared genes mean shared illness is nameless until you hold it: concordance is not destiny. A two-hit model—genetic load plus an environmental second hit—turns that raw certainty into something thinkable instead of evacuating it as “I am next.”

2012-114.sentence: The frame is the prohibition—fixed time, fee, cancellation, confidentiality—set against the wish to be special, late, unpaid, or endlessly available. When those rules stay consistent, the collision shows up as material instead of becoming an extra session or a broken boundary.

2012-118.sentence: The capacity to bounce back from a small slight is a developmental achievement, not a moral one. If caregivers never supplied timed, accurate empathy, that resilience never quite arrives, and ordinary feedback still lands as a collapse of the self.

2012-120.sentence: Avoidance is the defense: the person never stays long enough for fear to update. D-cycloserine only helps if the exposure actually happens; it does not replace facing the cue, it just makes the unlearning stick once the defense is set aside.

2012-123.sentence: Finding meaning in the loss is a sign of psychological mindedness: the mourner can look at their own grief and use it, not only suffer it. A trial comment that lands is something like, “You are trying to keep them inside you without staying frozen in the day they died.”

2012-124.sentence: APA ethics draw a hard termination line: no sexual relationship with a current or former patient, period. Time, marriage, supervision, and “no exploitation” do not reopen the door, because the old transference does not expire when the last session ends.

2012-127.sentence: Psychogenic blindness is a compromise: a wish not to see something forbidden collides with a prohibition against admitting that wish, so vision itself becomes the battlefield. Evoked potentials still fire because the pathway is intact; the conflict is in looking, not in the optic nerve.

2012-128.sentence: Therapeutic privilege can look like protecting the patient, but it's really deciding for them that they can't handle the truth -- a kind of paternalism dressed up as care.
