The more honest move is naming the fear out loud and still telling them what they're facing; that respects what they can actually hold.

2012-129.sentence: This adolescent is not splitting the nose into an all-bad object that must be endlessly remade; it is a real, dated hockey injury he wants returned to ordinary. When good and damaged can sit in one face, rhinoplasty often lifts quality of life instead of feeding a new preoccupation.

2012-130.sentence: The MMSE has a ceiling effect in a former history professor: easy items never reach the height where his actual decline lives. The complaint is the meaning—lost keys and lost names in a mind built for lectures—not a screen that still looks 'normal' because it never asked him to work that high.

2012-133.sentence: Supportive therapy is a two-person bargain: you and the patient agree to leave standing the defenses that are currently holding the hour together. Accepting those defenses is how you stay in a usable relationship instead of turning care into a fight about insight.

2012-135.sentence: A five-year-old still thinks a wish can move the world, so “I hate you” and Mom’s crash feel like one event. That is age-appropriate egocentric causality, not a precocious conscience and not a break with reality.

2012-136.sentence: Family systems count who actually soothes, feeds, and stays—the grandmother and the neighbor belong if they function as attachment figures. Working families share those attributes of care and reliability more than they share a blood-and-roof structure.

2012-137.sentence: The parent–teacher split is already an enactment: homework chaos at home and adequate attention at school are two relationships producing two different kids. You do not pick a villain; you treat the rating discrepancy as expected data about setting and dyad.

2012-138.sentence: Nightmares, feeling detached during the assault, and pulling away from friends at one week is acute stress disorder, not yet PTSD -- the diagnosis just needs more time to declare itself. The silence with friends isn't only avoidance of the memory; it's often shame keeping her from reaching for the people who could actually help her feel less alone.

2012-143.sentence: Both IPT and CBT stay in the here and now: they use the current relationship field—work conflict, withdrawn friends—as the secure base for change. Neither asks you to excavate childhood or interpret transference as the main tool.

2012-145.sentence: A fitness-for-duty exam is not a treatment alliance, so the frame has to be spoken before you take a history: who asked for the report, and what will leave the room. If you wait until after the resident has talked, you have already borrowed a confidentiality you cannot keep.

2012-147.sentence: Once addiction turns compulsive, the next drink isn't chasing a high anymore — it's negative reinforcement, use that exists only to make withdrawal, craving, and shame stop. That's a different treatment problem: you're no longer competing with pleasure, you're competing with relief.

2012-149.sentence: Couples work sits on Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task: can two people stay in a we without collapsing into blame or flight. Pointing the camera at the relationship problem, not at whose family of origin is worse, is how you keep that task in the room.

2012-151.sentence: It's tempting to read the silverware ritual as a wish sneaking past a prohibition — some dishwasher-shaped compromise. It isn't: the one-to-two-minute chewing automatisms and total amnesia are complex partial seizures doing the cutting, so you order an EEG, not an interpretation.

2012-152.sentence: Checking the already-taken-off orders is undoing: she tries to cancel a death-wish that her conscience still treats as causal after her brother’s tularemia. The superego will not accept “I wished it and he died” as coincidence, so she keeps rewriting the chart until the fantasy of harm feels reversed.

2012-156.sentence: Five years of dermatologists failing to find her 'bumps' hasn't reassured her — each negative exam just proves to her they looked in the wrong place. Fluvoxamine treats that as BDD; reaching for pimozide instead treats her like she has a fixed delusion about parasites, which risks confirming the very belief you're trying to loosen.

2012-158.sentence: Preparation means they already call truancy a problem and are picking tactics, which is still one step short of walking through the school door. That is suppression: they can park the wish to skip long enough to name a Monday plan, without having to deny the wish is there.

2012-159.sentence: Insight is the hinge: they can still entertain “maybe this is fear, not a tumor,” which is what keeps hypochondriasis from becoming a somatic delusion. If you keep ordering another scan to soothe your own doubt, that is an enactment—the two of you are living the hunt for a perfectly certain body instead of talking about the terror.

2012-166.sentence: After suicide or homicide, the early grief looks familiar, then dysphoria stays. The system often enacts a two-person repetition: you get recruited to prosecute, acquit, or explain the death instead of sitting with the unanswerable. Name that pull so the interview does not become a courtroom.

2012-168.sentence: Catatonic excitement is excessive purposeless motor activity that does not track you—you are not the stimulus. Countertransference may rush in as “they’re ignoring me” or an urge to over-control the floor. You are being recruited as a bystander to a motor storm, not as a failed interpreter.

2012-170.sentence: Imaginal exposure is already a two-person enactment: you and the patient are crossing the bridge in the office instead of walking to a real one. Name that bargain out loud so the image stays a rehearsal, not a collusion that forever postpones the actual height.

2012-172.sentence: Bill Wilson did not lecture Dr. Bob; he lent ego strength—impulse control and affect tolerance around craving—when the surgeon’s own coping had collapsed into drink and withdrawal. AA starts as one person borrowing another’s capacity to stay sober until that capacity is internalized.

2012-173.sentence: The child doesn't win the argument with mother — he ends it by pulling grandmother into it, and now two adults are managing what used to be one boundary. That's triangulation: conflict between two people gets detoured through a third instead of resolved between the original two.

2012-175.sentence: School-age minds first assimilate: they fold the penguin into the old “bird” schema before they rewrite the schema. Do not push uncovering or sudden accommodation; support the existing construct until it can stretch without collapsing.

2012-176.sentence: Alprostadil, given transurethrally or into the corpus cavernosum, makes erection a local prostaglandin event, not a verdict on whether the partner is “good” tonight. Treat the vascular failure first so the couple stops using every limp episode as proof the relationship is bad.

2012-177.sentence: Stopping shaving and toothbrushing is not a conversion symptom; it is realistic avoidance of trigger zones in trigeminal neuralgia, those seconds-long V2/V3 jolts set off by light touch. Interpret the frown as pain, not as a wish to punish the face or the examiner.

2012-178.sentence: Collecting the rarest cards, outdoing his friends, sharing the hobby with dad — this is industry versus inferiority in action: competence measured against peers and modeled by a parent. Whether card-collecting becomes 'I'm good at something' or the slipping grades become 'I'm not' is exactly what this stage is testing.

2012-179.sentence: Contemplation means she can hold both truths at once — the meetings scare her and she still went. Reflect her own ambivalence back to her instead of pushing toward action; a push right now reads less like encouragement and more like an argument she has to win or lose.

2012-180.sentence: This is identity work, not a date: she shadowed the resident’s stores to try on the therapist’s self, Erikson’s identity versus diffusion lived as a shopping route. Interpret the longing to identify; confront, test, or transfer her and you confirm she will be “fired” for needing a model.

2012-182.sentence: Repeated respiratory illness can freeze a child's lesson that air hunger equals dying. Panic disorder is that lesson never updating—the adult still treats a tight chest as catastrophe instead of a body signal that can be named and waited out.

2012-184.sentence: Lock the door and you are recruited as the only doctor they can have—that is the necessaries doctrine, not charity. Notice the countertransference that they forfeited care; the duty exists because they cannot walk out and seek it themselves.

2012-188.sentence: “My apple” is not greed; it is the child discovering a self that is not mother’s. The protest marks a developmental arrival: two minds, two owners, one fruit.

2012-190.sentence: Absorption is a developmental capacity: attention can finally stay inside one imagined scene the way a child stays inside play. Hallway noise drops out not because the mind splits, but because that hold has arrived.

2012-192.sentence: Refeeding sits on Erikson’s first task: can the body take in care without collapsing. A phosphate crash two days into high-calorie feeds is trust vs. mistrust written on the myocardium—too much offered, too little intracellular store to metabolize it.

2012-193.sentence: The Nuremberg Code names consent as the first ethical act, not a formality after the protocol is already written. For the inpatient you want to interview, that rule is doing protective work: it keeps “research subject” from collapsing into “patient who cannot refuse.”

2012-194.sentence: A prior attempt matters more than any mood scale because the wish already became an act once — the line between thinking about dying and doing something about it has already been crossed. That's why the standardized mortality ratio is highest here: the next crossing is statistically closer, not just emotionally more likely.

2012-196.sentence: New confusion days after an SSRI in a 70-year-old with Alzheimer disease is a medical emergency first, not an invitation to interpret the dementia. Order electrolytes before you uncover anything: hyponatremia is the finding that can drop consciousness, and this mind cannot use insight work until sodium is safe.

2012-201.sentence: Alcohol is doing a job for antisocial personality: it shortens the already thin pause between impulse and act, so deceit, aggression, and rights-violations run with less friction. The drinking is not a separate “addiction personality”; it is an amplifier of the same externalizing pattern that usually started before the bottle.

2012-202.sentence: IPT deliberately stays outside the room: it works on the role dispute with his actual spouse, not on whatever he's begun to feel about you. That's the whole distinction from psychodynamic work — real relationships get the direct advice and problem-solving; the relationship with the therapist stays out of the conversation.

2012-203.sentence: From the first minutes of life the infant already orients to the human voice over other sounds, so attachment is not a later luxury you “create” with the right toy. Talking, reading, and singing are using a preference that is wired at birth, not waiting for a social smile to prove the baby is ready.

2012-204.sentence: After an SSRI trips a brief mania, the pull is to become the doctor who “unmasked bipolar” and lock in a lifelong label. Hold the countertransference: this episode meets substance-induced mood disorder, not bipolar II, until a spontaneous syndrome shows up off the drug.

2012-205.sentence: When melancholia has emptied the man of speech, food, and thirst, the body is doing the remembering he cannot put into words. ECT is the intervention that reaches that unrepresented state first: it interrupts the somatic freeze so a mind can start to exist again.

2012-206.sentence: ADHD is a developmental claim about a capacity that should show up wherever the child has to hold attention and inhibit impulse. If the trouble lives only in one classroom, you have not yet seen a missing function; you have seen a setting that cannot hold him.

2012-210.sentence: Klein would ask whether the mourner can still keep the dead person as a whole object—loved and missed—rather than a persecuting absence. Cross-cultural rituals that look “too long” or too concrete can be depressive-position repair, not pathology; they widen what counts as ordinary grief.

2012-211.sentence: MBT is built on Bowlby: when a late callback becomes 'she's rejecting me,' the attachment system has hijacked the mind's ability to consider other explanations. The therapist's job isn't to decode the fear, it's to slow the certainty down until the patient can hold more than one possibility again.

2012-212.sentence: Cluster A isolation is Erikson's trust-versus-mistrust left unfinished: other people never became safe enough to approach, so withdrawal is the compromise. Social withdrawal is the signal symptom; catatonia, loose associations, and command voices would mean the task has already collapsed into frank psychosis.

2012-213.sentence: The bilingual schoolroom is a cultural third: a public language and audience the child cannot yet risk a voice inside. Start with graded behavioral exposure that raises tolerance for speaking there; do not open with an SSRI, a benzo, or an Oedipal play hour as if the silence were a private family secret.

2012-215.sentence: Peritraumatic dissociation is the ego stepping out of the scene—numbing affect and reality-testing so the mind does not have to stay inside the crash. That immediate uncoupling, more than ordinary fear or rumination, marks a mind that could not bind the event and raises later PTSD risk.

2012-217.sentence: Validating what this family already does well is the Engagement stage of family psychoeducation: you are recruiting two more people as partners, not installing a protocol on them. If you skip that join and jump to relapse drills, the parents and the 25-year-old with schizophrenia start making a new pattern together—compliance theater instead of a working alliance.

2012-218.sentence: The “hyper,” one-hour sleep, and irritability after 80 mg of prednisone are a steroid storm, not a character you have to interpret first. Gradual taper is the treatment; naming it as mania and piling on quetiapine or valproate can be a defensive enactment—acting instead of removing the cause.

2012-221.sentence: The stomachache and the refusal to sleep alone are the compromise: the child wants the parent nearby and also wants to be a big kid who goes to school. Separation anxiety is that collision in the body—proximity is the wish, independence is the prohibition, and the symptom lets both stay.

2012-225.sentence: Psychological mindedness starts when he can hear the thought “I am a failure as a husband” as his construction, not as a fact the affair proved. CBT’s first useful comment targets that assumption of personal failure, not the marriage history, so he can see his own part without drowning in the parents’ divorce.

2012-227.sentence: A child’s story is co-authored; you do not know the attachment field until you hear the people who feed, soothe, and set the rules. Parental interviews are therefore mandatory—not optional labs or a play hour—because the relationship that holds the child is part of the examination.

2012-228.sentence: Doubling lithium is acting out: she changes the dose instead of saying the bipolar illness still feels unbearable. The diarrhea, tremor, and disorientation are the body answering that bypass—lithium will not be undone by more of itself.

2012-230.sentence: Hopelessness is a verdict: the future has already been tried, found guilty, and denied parole. That inner sentence, not remorse or anxiety, is what the cognitive model treats as the suicide-risk signal.

2012-231.sentence: Discrepancy is a developmental arrival: he can now see the gap between wanting closeness and inviting fury. Brief psychodynamic work uses that newly arrived observing capacity rather than waiting for a full transference reconstruction.

2012-232.sentence: The head-banging is anger at the occupied grandparents and the new baby, turned against the self so attachment can stay clean. The symptom is doing the job of punishing his own body instead of risking the relationship.

2012-235.sentence: Hallucinations on a stimulant are not just a “side effect to watch.” They are the wish for more drive, more focus, more go colliding with a brain that can no longer tell signal from threat. Stop the drug now; the prohibition is physiological, and you do not interpret voices you just chemically turned on.

2012-236.sentence: The bond is not poetry. It is the adult’s body between the infant and danger when the infant cannot yet represent danger in words. What cannot be remembered as “I was kept safe” is later repeated as cling, freeze, or a clinic that suddenly feels like a cliff.

2012-237.sentence: Incorrect treatment is the claim that most often arrives, and it often arrives after you were recruited to be the one who “just sends them home.” Notice the pull to be the brave discharger or the anxious jailer, then document the assessment, the alternatives, and the limit you actually held.

2012-239.sentence: Akathisia is the body shouting what the patient may not yet be able to name. Before you add propranolol or switch the antipsychotic, try one trial comment: “This restlessness started with the medicine, not with your character.” If they can use that, you have a partner; if they only pace, treat the receptor first.

2012-241.sentence: Covert obstructionism is delayed agency: the child never quite got a safe way to say no out loud, so stubbornness and lost forms do the refusing. Name the old DSM type—passive-aggressive—then ask what direct protest would cost this adult if it finally arrived.

2012-242.sentence: Gender, class, and an abusive partner sit in the room as a third: they already limited her choices, so do not import a script that she must be secretly devastated by the abortion. Track what actually predicts later depression—pre-pregnancy depression—rather than moralizing her reported relief.

2012-243.sentence: Integrity is Erikson’s last task: looking back and finding the life, including the misses, still worth having been lived. After sixty-five that verdict is the opposite of despair, not a denial of grief.

2012-244.sentence: Nervios is not a worse object or a sinful self; it is how many Puerto Rican and other Latin American patients locate depression in the nerves—jittery, sleepless, aching. Ask what “nervousness” means in her family before you translate it into emptiness or shame.

2012-245.sentence: Do not read a half-face as conversion until the forehead and the ear have spoken. Equal forehead and perioral weakness plus mastoid pain and hyperacusis is Bell’s palsy—peripheral VII—not a split-off rage parked on the cheek.

2012-246.sentence: A mixed manic/depressed episode puts you both in two weathers at once: racing, irritable, and hopeless in the same hour. Lithium often fails that mix, and the dyad then enacts “nothing works” unless you name the mixed state instead of bargaining for a cleaner mania.

2012-247.sentence: This mind is already running hot: easy fatigue plus feeling keyed up means the ego is burning fuel just to keep worry from spilling. Do not go hunting childhood meaning first; stabilize sleep, tension, and the day's tasks, then decide later whether this person can use any uncovering at all.

2012-248.sentence: The entorhinal cortex is the doorway for new memories; once cells die there, the clock on recent learning does not rewind because someone is motivated. Treatment has to honor that limit: you work with what still encodes, and you do not treat forgetting as resistance.

2012-249.sentence: Simple schizophrenia is the old name for a picture built only of deficit: blunting, withdrawal, no rich inner story to interpret. A trial comment that asks them to see their own part will bounce; you need to test whether any observing ego is left before you treat silence as hidden meaning.

2012-250.sentence: She has already put the baby in the room as a third: “what is best for my baby” is maternal identity speaking, not just a medical preference. Methadone maintenance for the whole pregnancy holds that third without asking her to prove virtue by going cold turkey.

2012-252.sentence: The yelling and hitting after detention can be doing a job: carrying mood, trauma, psychosis, or ADHD that the conduct label is hiding. Evaluating additional psychopathology first treats the outburst as a message, not as the whole person.

2012-253.sentence: At 66 this sits on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair work: looking back and deciding whether the life was livable, or whether it should end. Amitriptyline turns that despair into a sodium-channel problem, so you get the EKG first; you cannot interpret the suicide as meaning until the QRS is not widening.

2012-254.sentence: The family’s alarm at pajamas in the street is a superego scene: public exposure as a moral emergency. Delirium is the opposite of conscience—waxing-and-waning attention and picking at the gown are not guilt, they are an organ failing in real time.

2012-258.sentence: The old affair is already in the room: the patient presents a phantom venereal disease, the spouse says it was years ago and forgiven, and the three of you are living the confession again. That is an enactment of psychotic depression—mood-congruent guilt made into a body crime—not a fresh infection or a new hypochondriacal hobby.

2012-259.sentence: Shame after a binge is the signal that the episode already happened; denial is what kept the hand moving until the plate was empty. Name the loss of control in the room so binge-eating disorder is a pattern you can discuss, not a blackout the patient has to hide.

2012-260.sentence: Jumping at engine noise and canceling drives near the highway is the body still treating every road as the crash site. Sertraline is first-line for that generalized hyperarousal once three months of psychotherapy alone hasn't been enough to settle it.

2012-263.sentence: Absence is not repression of a thought; the 3 Hz spike-and-wave burst blanks awareness for a few seconds of stare and blink. Do not treat the pause as a child "spacing out" on purpose when the EEG names a seizure.

2012-265.sentence: The euphoric closeness MDMA delivers at the party is manufactured, not earned — and the body still sends the bill afterward: mydriasis, hypertension, dehydration, a CPK spike from hours on a flooded system. Treat the crash as pharmacology, not proof the person needs the drug to feel connected to people sober.

2012-267.sentence: Low ceruloplasmin in Wilson disease is a hard stop: the liver and the mind share a deadline you cannot talk past. Impulsivity and lability here are not a character you can hurry into insight; copper has already set a clock the family already watched run out at thirty.

2012-268.sentence: Lorazepam first-line for catatonia—immobility, posturing, echopraxia—treats a developmental capacity that has gone offline: the body can no longer use gesture as thought. You do not start with lithium or a neuroleptic as if mood or psychosis were still the available language; the motor self has to come back online before talk can arrive.

2012-270.sentence: The stage theory was never built from watching children directly — it was reconstructed backward from what adults said on the couch decades later, and every analyst's reconstruction tells a slightly different oral-anal-genital story. A theory assembled from retrospective narratives is hard to validate because there's no independent way to check which version, if any, is right.

2012-271.sentence: Uncontrollable shock empties the animal of a felt sense that effort works—self psychology’s competence pole, the ordinary pride that “I can still do something.” Antidepressants reverse those escape deficits, which is why the paradigm is useful: they restore trying, not just mood labels.

2012-273.sentence: He is trying to keep two attachments alive at once: the parental Colombian object and the new marital one. Integration names that strain—heritage held, not discarded—unlike assimilation (drop the old) or separation (refuse the new).

2012-274.sentence: You will feel recruited to become the skeptic who unmasks a faker; that countertransference belongs more to factitious disorder and malingering. Conversion is the limp that is not produced on purpose—no secondary-gain plot, no hunt for the sick role.

2012-275.sentence: A harsh conscience wants a prohibition: one dinner wine must now be a dementia toxin because the parents had dementia. The data do not license that sermon—if the pattern stays one drink and mood stays remitted, you do not rewrite a lifelong habit into a crime.

2012-278.sentence: Erikson’s intimacy task is mutuality: two people stay related without one using the other. A boundary crossing can still serve the work; a violation is when the clinician’s need (status, sex, money, or a private audience) exploits the patient and isolates them from a safe professional relationship.

2012-279.sentence: Residential care is indicated when home cannot function as a secure base for sobriety—when the people who should hold proximity are the ones offering the drug. Lack of family support is not a character flaw; it means the attachment environment itself is the relapse cue, so the person needs a substitute holding setting.

2012-280.sentence: This laughter is not play or joy; a hypothalamic hamartoma can fire gelastic seizures and, sitting on the tuber cinereum, also drive precocious puberty. The face smiles while the girl feels nothing funny—development has been hijacked at the hypothalamus, not in her mood.

2012-281.sentence: Bilateral placement buys a faster, more robust antidepressant response at the cost of more retrograde amnesia — a trade only the patient can actually weigh. Make that trade explicit before you start, and track orientation and autobiographical memory afterward as carefully as you track mood.

2012-282.sentence: A sixteen-year-old trying on a masochistic heterosexual scene in fantasy is doing ordinary sexual-identity work: the mind rehearses desire before it has to live it. Excitement plus anxiety is the ego sampling a script, not a verdict of future paraphilia or proof of abuse.

2012-283.sentence: Twelve-step facilitation treats showing up at AA as an ego win: the patient already tolerated the social-anxiety spike and still walked in. You shore up that capacity instead of analyzing the strangers, chasing craving, or backing off the meeting.

2012-284.sentence: Asking for a stimulant after four hours of sleep is a wish to override the body’s limit rather than restore the eight-hour baseline. Dyssomnia NOS names that collapse; treating it as ADD would collude with the demand to stay up.

2012-288.sentence: Assaults cluster at change of shift because the holding environment—the staff who know the patient’s state—briefly disappears. Treat handoff like a toddler’s caregiver swap: make the outgoing and incoming minds one continuous object.

2012-289.sentence: Telling the limits of confidentiality at the first visit is conscience put on the calendar, not a speech you give after you have already leaked. The safeguard is the superego made procedural: the rule sits in the room before anyone is tempted to treat privacy as a personal favor.

2012-292.sentence: Hypnosis for IBS works as a borrowed regulator: another person’s voice becomes a temporary secure base for gut arousal the patient cannot dampen alone. The trial signal is not “nice support”; it is a structured other that the enteric nervous system can actually use.

2012-294.sentence: The fencing posture is a frontal-lobe motor signature; you do not call it “behavioral” from a hallway story. Video-EEG is the frame that holds the limit: brief, stereotyped, clustering nocturnal spells stay seizures until the tracing says otherwise.

2012-296.sentence: A 29/30 MMSE can become denial: the number is used to push the engineer’s failing finances and travel planning out of awareness because the score “looks fine.” The limitation is that the MMSE may miss very mild cognitive impairment, so treating the total as reassurance is the defense, not a better screen.

2012-298.sentence: At twenty-seven the Erikson task is intimacy versus isolation, and NF-2—merlin-gene mutation with bilateral vestibular schwannomas—can make hearing loss and ataxia feel like a secret that keeps a partner at arm’s length. The gene names the tumors; the stage names the risk that she pulls back from closeness rather than let someone live with a body that keeps delivering new masses.

2012-299.sentence: Age and cohort sit in the room as a third: many older adults were taught that grief is private and respectable, so standard DBT skills miss the extra target of emotional constriction. When they describe bereavement only in practical terms, you are meeting a generational rule that feeling too much is unseemly, not a failure of mindfulness or distress tolerance.

2013-1.sentence: Financial incentive is not attachment. Attachment would be using the sick role to keep a caregiver close—the “psychological need to feel cared for”—and that points toward factitious illness, not malingering. Name the pending disability check as secondary gain so you do not confuse a bid for money with a bid for a secure base.

2013-2.sentence: Spasmodic torticollis is a cervical dystonia, not a neck that “won’t face” someone; do not interpret the turn until you have treated the circuit. Botulinum toxin is the treatment with the best evidence here, and it works by weakening the overactive muscles rather than by resolving a split between good and bad objects.

2013-3.sentence: Introjection is swallowing the other person whole—taking in a parent’s contempt so it now lives as the patient’s own voice. This mind can use some uncovering: when you show that the phrase is borrowed, you loosen an internalized object instead of only supporting the self-attack.

2013-4.sentence: The school–parent–clinic loop can become an enactment: adults are already living a sexual-danger story instead of talking about ordinary five-year-old curiosity. Peeking and bathroom play among peers, without coercion or distress, is normal sexual development; treat the adults’ panic so the child is not assigned an abuse script he does not have.

2013-5.sentence: Recurrent suicidal behavior in schizophrenia is often acting out: putting a death wish into action rather than holding it in words. Clozapine has the strongest evidence for cutting that behavior, so you treat the impulse at the receptor while you keep naming the wish instead of only managing the aftermath.

2013-6.sentence: Confusion, apathy, and lost tandem gait after gastric bypass can look like collapsed ego strength—poor reality testing and no coping—but the mind is starving for thiamine. Give thiamine for this Wernicke picture before you interpret the “change” as a psychological failure to metabolize loss.

2013-7.sentence: He's not avoiding treatment out of stubbornness — the belief that this suffering is deserved for past deeds is itself a way of making an unbearable feeling make sense. Arguing theology won't reach that; asking what he thinks would need to be true for him to accept help might.

2013-8.sentence: Sensate-focus work—exercises to heighten sensory awareness, not intercourse or vibrators—asks whether they can notice their own tightening and hurry instead of performing. A trial comment lands here: if they can say “we turn touch into a test,” they have enough psychological mindedness to use Masters and Johnson rather than just follow a homework sheet.

2013-13.sentence: Hostility is not a private feeling; it is already being enacted — lived out — in tense interactions and in the vascular bed, where blood pressure tracks the fight. Studying Type A or depression will miss the more consistent finding: anger that is acted rather than thought keeps the pressor system on duty.

2013-14.sentence: Nonmaleficence here is a frame limit, not a personality trait: you do not accept a seriously ill 10-year-old as your patient when your last child work was twenty years ago. Holding that limit — and naming it — protects the child from treatment that would look like care and still be unsafe.

2013-15.sentence: Marked individual differences in executive function first show in the preschool years, when waiting, shifting, and recovering from frustration become visible tasks. That is the developmental window where you can start to see who can hold a plan in mind and who still needs the adult as an external prefrontal cortex.

2013-18.sentence: Trying hard to fall asleep is exactly what wrecks sleep — this patient has turned rest into a task to be accomplished by effort, and that performance mindset is what psychophysiological insomnia actually is.

2013-19.sentence: The rumination is doing a job: it turns sleep into a performance, so the bed becomes a workplace instead of a cue for rest. Stimulus control names that bargain—go to bed only when sleepy, and leave if you are working the insomnia instead of sleeping.

2013-24.sentence: Clarification is the most insight-oriented move because it puts two versions of the self in the same sentence—what is claimed and what is done. That is identity work: the patient has to own the gap rather than take advice, praise, or more story.

2013-26.sentence: The worse the risk-benefit ratio — a decision that could kill or cure — the more rigorously you need to test capacity, not just get a signature; a low-stakes choice earns a lighter touch. That sliding scale is the real ethical point: consent isn't binary, it's calibrated to what's actually at risk of being lost.

2013-28.sentence: An inhibited toddler’s mind startles at novelty; that is a temperament, not a defense you interpret away. Lead with support and graded exposure, not uncovering—this ego needs a safer runway before you ask it to fly.

2013-29.sentence: DID and PTSD are not a one-person museum of alters. The two of you will remake the old danger or the old rescue unless you name it: amnesia and hypervigilance live between people, not only inside states.

2013-35.sentence: One possible bad exam grade isn't a fact yet, but catastrophic thinking treats it like an already-written verdict — fail the test, fail the course, lose the family. Notice that the therapist's question doesn't argue with the fear; it just asks the student to say the whole chain out loud, which is often enough to show how shaky each link is.

2013-37.sentence: Telling this patient that the high ESR and the two-day response to prednisone mean the shoulder pain was real inflammation — not something they caused or imagined — can be what lets them stop hunting for a character flaw and just get treated.

2013-38.sentence: Erikson’s generativity is not a moral exam you fail when the kids leave; the conscience can bless creative community projects as real care for the next generation. A rigid superego that only counts childrearing or career status will keep midlife feeling like dereliction.

2013-41.sentence: Dragons at the desk plus rambling, off-topic answers are a collapse of reality testing, not garden-variety inattention. Early-onset schizophrenia means this ego cannot yet organize thought or filter fear; support structure first, do not interpret the dragons as metaphor.

2013-43.sentence: In the middle of IPT you and the patient keep tightening one agreed link: this supervisor fight, this dip in mood. That is the work of the intermediate phase—strengthening the connection between interpersonal events and symptoms—not restarting the inventory or racing toward goodbye.

2013-47.sentence: It's tempting to jump straight to a schizophrenia diagnosis on a first psychotic break, but confusion and poor memory for recent events should make you pause — that clouded sensorium points toward brief psychotic disorder, not a diagnosis that follows someone for life.

2013-50.sentence: This 15-year-old with death wishes needs supportive structure and FDA-approved escitalopram, not an uncovering hunt for the meaning of every irritable comment. Ask about suicide directly first; insight work waits until the mind can use it without more despair.

2013-51.sentence: Contingency management lets the methadone clinic stay one whole object: take-home doses arrive when attendance and groups are real, and they shrink when they are not. That keeps the patient from splitting the program into the kind dispenser and the cruel rule-maker.

2013-52.sentence: Threatening involuntary stay unless the manic patient “chooses” admission uses closeness as a club and wrecks informed consent. Attachment needs a secure base; here the psychiatrist offered proximity only as a trap, so the signature is not a free yes.

2013-53.sentence: An infant and each caregiver co-build a bond; that is why multiple attachments form and why their strength can differ. The daycare protest is a two-person pattern with that teacher, not proof the child has only one slot and the parents lost it.

2013-54.sentence: Late-life integrity still shows as grace and etiquette with strangers while Alzheimer dementia quietly takes names and ADLs. The social polish is the last hold on “I am still myself,” not evidence that the mind is intact.

2013-56.sentence: Alexithymia is not a missing heart; feelings never become words, so they stay as headache or chest tightness. In Kleinian terms those affects stay unmentalized and get evacuated into the body instead of becoming concern you can think about and repair.

2013-59.sentence: Atomoxetine blocks the norepinephrine transporter rather than releasing dopamine the way stimulants do — which matters most to the family that's scared of handing their kid 'a drug of abuse.' It's the option you reach for when what's driving the refusal is fear of dependence, not the pharmacology itself.

2013-61.sentence: Methadone is holding this woman's ego together: impulse control and affect stay usable because the receptor is not in withdrawal. Pregnancy is already a huge demand on coping; ripping the methadone out (or chasing it with naloxone) would smash that stability for both of them.

2013-64.sentence: Pathological gambling from a dopamine agonist like pramipexole often feels ego-syntonic to the patient — he's just having fun in retirement — while it's the spouse who's left seeing the real damage. That mismatch, patient minimizing and family alarmed, should point you toward the medication before a psychiatric explanation.

2013-65.sentence: A small, apt disclosure lets the patient meet a mixed human object instead of a blank screen or a twin who “has been there too.” You are modeling how a good-enough other survives feeling, which is what builds alliance—not credentials, politics, or shared faith.

2013-67.sentence: Schizophrenia here is not only a broken mind; it is a two-person field collapsing, as the family becomes the last audience while the patient starts relating to cars, the television, and unseen others instead of them. Those flapping, waving arms are the body joining the same withdrawal: movement that no longer answers another person.

2013-70.sentence: Separation anxiety is a collision: the wish to stay glued to the parent meets the demand to go to school, and the mind solves it by flooding with danger-to-family. Generalized anxiety is the usual roommate because that same prohibition against risk then spreads to grades, bodies, and the world.

2013-73.sentence: Caregiver alcohol abuse predicts elder abuse because the helper’s own limit has already failed: intoxication collapses the pause between rage and action. Time and sobriety cannot be rushed in that person, so you do not wait for “insight” before arranging a private safety interview.

2013-76.sentence: The pill, the pediatric visit, the headache: each can function as a feed that keeps the child and parent glued together so school drop-off never has to happen. Name the medicine as optional so it does not become proof that only a body crisis justifies staying home.

2013-78.sentence: When a two-year-old feeds a stuffed animal from a toy cup, it's tempting to read a whole inner narrative into it — but pretend play at this age is really the child discovering that one thing can stand for another, not yet a story with feelings and plot. Resist crediting it with more sophistication than it has.

2013-80.sentence: The binge-purge cycle in bulimia often works to regulate self-esteem without needing to lean on another person; fluoxetine plus CBT is the combination that's actually been studied here. Medication doesn't fix willpower — it can quiet the drive enough that the patient starts using the therapist, not the purge, to feel steady again.

2013-81.sentence: A brief, discussable hug after a death is a boundary crossing: the wish to soothe and be soothed collides with the rule that we do not touch, and you let both sides of that conflict stay in the room. It is not a boundary violation (exploitation) and not an enactment you hide; name the hug in the next session so the drive does not get acted again instead of thought.

2013-83.sentence: Craving wants to be acted on immediately, turned into a drink before it can be thought about. Naltrexone blocking the opioid reward buys enough of a gap that the urge can be talked through in session instead of automatically relapsed on.

2013-85.sentence: Isolated erotomania sits in delusional disorder, so a trial comment about longing or status will not land as metaphor; the patient treats coded interviews as evidence, not as a wish they can look at. Psychological mindedness is exactly what is missing: they cannot see their own part in constructing the romance, only the other person’s alleged love.

2013-86.sentence: Wanting off fluoxetine the moment sildenafil tames the sexual side effect is often denial: the third episode is treated as if it never happened. Keep the fluoxetine while it works; the defense is against needing a maintenance drug, not against the orgasm delay itself.

2013-90.sentence: In acute refeeding for severe anorexia nervosa, starvation is an unrepresented state: hunger, fear, and control live in the body and cannot yet be remembered as a story. Coaching, support, and reinforcement at the meal are the first language; interpretation of family or core beliefs comes after the soma can stay in the room.

2013-93.sentence: Hyperactivity is the piece that most often quiets with age, and that can recruit you into a false transference of “this kid grew out of it.” Your countertransference—relief that they sit still—can hide that impulsivity and inattention are still asking you to be the external brake they never fully internalized.

2013-94.sentence: Dusky competence is not “sounds lawyerly.” The defendant must consult counsel with a rational understanding and hold a factual and rational grasp of the proceedings. A delusion that the judge is an alien agent can leave vocabulary intact while the belief itself is doing the work of making the courtroom unusable as a real legal space.

2013-97.sentence: Hypnotizability and dissociation are really the same underlying talent — the capacity to absorb so completely into an experience that ordinary self-awareness recedes. In dissociative disorder that same absorption gets used defensively, parking unbearable memory and feeling offstage instead of holding them as part of one continuous self.

2013-100.sentence: Child abuse is the one place where staying quiet stops being therapeutic — the confidentiality that usually protects the relationship has to give way to a report, because the alternative is sending the patient back into the same danger alone. That's not a failure of the therapeutic frame; it's the frame doing its job.

2013-101.sentence: Primary process is the mind before the clock: unconscious thoughts that do not keep logical connections, so a supervisor can be a parent and a train at once. You cannot rush that material into secondary process; termination and the hour only work if you let illogic exist long enough to be named rather than tidied.

2013-104.sentence: The plea for a pill after cirrhosis can recruit you into a punitive rescuer—disulfiram as the ‘make it hurt so they stop’ object—or a magical one who will erase drinking with fluoxetine. Acamprosate is the less theatrical choice: you stay the physician who protects a damaged liver instead of acting out the patient’s disappointment as either punishment or a mood-drug shortcut.

2013-105.sentence: In DBT, ‘dialectical’ means holding two truths at once—this pain is real and this behavior cannot continue—and looking for a synthesis rather than picking a side. That is the opposite of an unrepresented split: what cannot be thought as both/and gets repeated as self-harm after rejection until someone helps the patient stand in the middle.

2013-107.sentence: School-age speed of learning rides on prefrontal cortical pruning: unused connections are cut so the remaining circuits can work with more precision. The child’s self still needs your mirroring of real competence—‘you can plan this homework’—because pruning is refinement, not a finished executive self, which is why impulse control still wobbles.

2013-108.sentence: Decentration is an ego gain: the child can now stand outside his own wishes and see two parents as separate people with their own conflict. That frees him from the old magical bargain—‘if I am good they stay’—so sadness and anger can be felt without being used as proof that he caused the divorce.

2013-110.sentence: Envy is the wish; the prohibition is that you must not be the envious one. Projection dumps the impulse on the sibling so the wish stays alive while the conscience stays clean.

2013-114.sentence: Anaclitic depression is Spitz's name for what happens when a needed caregiver is suddenly gone and the infant's capacity to use that person has already formed. The collapse in feeding, sleep, and liveliness is a developmental achievement that then has nowhere to go.

2013-115.sentence: The “3” is already doing a job: it keeps some wish to change alive without forcing a full goodbye to alcohol. Asking why not a 1 pulls that leftover concern into words—liver, a relationship—so the patient hears their own reason instead of yours.

2013-117.sentence: The outbursts show up when a parent says “chores” or “no,” not with siblings, so the fight is a two-person signal, not a free-floating illness. Parent management training has the evidence because it changes the adult’s response—the actual arena—rather than medicating a child who can still play.

2013-119.sentence: Covert sensitization pairs the hot fantasy with an aversive fantasy so the mind supplies its own punishment without a shock box. That is a planned use of undoing: the person rehearses spoiling the urge in imagination so they do not have to act it out.

2013-122.sentence: The coffee-shop job holds two wishes at once: to become the physician the parents already named, and to refuse that career without having to say no. Identity is the task because the depression is the collision of those wishes, not a failure of intimacy or of later generativity.

2013-123.sentence: Phenytoin's classic side effects — gum overgrowth, hirsutism, the ataxic gait — aren't just exam findings; for a 73-year-old, they're daily reminders of losing control over his own body on top of a seizure disorder that already threatened his independence. Ask how he feels about what he sees in the mirror, not just about the nystagmus.

2013-124.sentence: Clomipramine is the most serotonergic TCA and still the pharmacologic standard when OCD washing will not yield. You will be recruited as the one who finally sanitizes the world or as the one who dares leave dirt on the hands; that pull is countertransference, and it is data, not a reason to skip the drug.

2013-125.sentence: The five-mile radius is the fear living in the body because it never became a memory that could be told. Exposure CBT is the treatment that asks the unrepresented panic to happen in graded drives rather than only in the locked-down map of home.

2013-131.sentence: School-age grief has a clock you cannot rush: intense crying and questions about the death are work, not pathology. Unresolved grief shows as a limit that will not close—clinging to parents in separation anxiety or a lasting freeze-out of peers.

2013-133.sentence: Before treating this as health anxiety, work up the reflux and indigestion as possible real gastric disease — a fixed belief about cancer doesn't rule out cancer, and referring for medical evaluation isn't punting the case, it's the responsible first step.

2013-135.sentence: The crack-house is a conditioned stimulus; classical conditioning rings craving before the ego can vote. Walking another block is suppression—pushing the urge aside on purpose—and it fails at the doorway because Pavlov already owns the street.

2013-136.sentence: In the emergency department, ego strength starts as safety, so affect can be tolerated without flooding and reality testing can come back online. Psychosocial interventions that establish safety from further trauma do that work; benzodiazepines, a same-day SSRI, single-session EMDR, and group debriefing do not.

2013-137.sentence: Lithium's protection against suicide doesn't simply track how well it controls mood swings — it seems to blunt impulsivity and aggression more directly, a genuinely different mechanism than mood control. Worth remembering that treating the mood disorder and reducing suicide risk aren't automatically the same intervention.

2013-139.sentence: Involuntary emergency medication is what happens when a patient's own capacity to calm down has broken completely and no amount of talking or proximity can bring them back — someone else's regulation has to substitute for theirs. Documenting the imminent danger is what keeps that intervention honest: the body can't be left unsafe, but psychosis alone doesn't erase the right to consent.

2013-140.sentence: Lithium is both real risk and real lifeline here — teratogenic, but also the one thing that's actually kept her stable through repeated relapses. After a prior NMS, she may experience any antipsychotic as something that nearly killed her, so staying on lithium isn't inertia, it's staying with the treatment she can actually trust.

2013-141.sentence: She parks the terror in her ex-husband—that is projection, putting an inner change onto someone outside—while she still knows the story “sounds crazy.” New replacement of objects, insomnia, and work decline need a medical and neurologic workup first; interpreting the projection as the diagnosis would miss an organic process announcing itself as Capgras-like certainty.

2013-142.sentence: Latency lines up with industry versus inferiority: the school-age child’s job is competence, and the 8-year-old’s falling self-esteem is already an enactment in which adults keep proving he cannot do the work. If the evaluation only catalogues deficits, the clinic joins the same two-person script instead of naming skills, effort, and what still works.

2013-144.sentence: Reality testing and role functioning are still standing—he is in class, with family, in organized sport—so the ego’s crack is impulse control and affect tolerance, not a first mania or PCP break. Exogenous anabolic steroids punch that hole: more gym, more irritability, threats, without needing a new personality story.

2013-147.sentence: Group work can use more therapist transparency and self-disclosure because the here-and-now already has many observers; a brief, real statement can support members who cannot yet use deep uncovering. Keep self-disclosure as technique, not confession: enough presence to regulate the room, not so much that you steal the hour from exploring what the late arrival is doing to the group.

2013-148.sentence: The reason for CBC monitoring on clozapine is neutrophils specifically, not general blood counts — agranulocytosis is silent until it isn't. It's easy to talk yourself out of a required draw because the patient 'looks fine'; that's the countertransference to watch, since skipping the ANC is how a rare but lethal risk gets missed.

2013-149.sentence: Sudden sleep attacks on a dopamine agonist like ropinirole often aren't something the patient can report themselves — they may have no memory of nodding off, so it's the family who catches the near-miss at the wheel. Ask what changed when the agonist started, treat it as a drug effect rather than a character flaw, and address driving safety immediately.

2013-151.sentence: Consent is the frame’s hard stop: you cannot discuss the spouse’s medication questions until the patient authorizes it, no matter how worried the caller sounds. Time and confidentiality cannot be rushed; the first sentence is that you need the patient’s permission, not an invitation to explain the change.

2013-152.sentence: Hallucinations and fluctuating attention in Lewy body dementia can pull staff toward reaching for more antipsychotic to calm things down — which is exactly the wrong move, since these patients are unusually sensitive to EPS from those same drugs. Naming the syndrome up front is what stops that reflex before it causes harm.

2013-154.sentence: If you treat twenty-five-year sadness about a child who died of leukemia as pathology, you and the system are enacting a demand that grief finish on schedule. The living pattern is the pressure to call function-preserving, sleep-intact mourning “complicated” instead of letting it remain a durable bond.

2013-156.sentence: After the snake, the hike itself becomes a poison-pill: exposure is not help, it is proof that danger is coming. Specific phobia is the relationship to the cue—cling to the parents, refuse the trail—not a demand for a systemic treatment of “anxiety.”

2013-157.sentence: The limit you hold is the cannabis history itself: age at first use, how often, and whether it preceded the psychosis—not a polite skip because the teenager (or the family) treats it as ordinary. Confidentiality covers the chart, not the fact; you still name cannabis as the adolescent exposure tied to later schizophrenia.

2013-159.sentence: Paradoxical insomnia is the night doing psychic work: the patient needs the story of under two hours even when latency is ten minutes, sleep lasts seven hours, and efficiency is 90%. The complaint is a misread of rest, not a factitious show for the lab, so you treat the conviction rather than a missing two hours.

2013-160.sentence: Reflecting the pain back — 'this sounds really hard' — instead of jumping to advice or fact-finding about who ended it is what lets the patient feel held rather than interrogated. Asking how they're coping tests something real too: can they still take care of themselves while grieving, or has the loss swamped that capacity?

2013-163.sentence: The teacher-child pair can still hold a “good” version of this student: live explanation lands, and the IQ of 92 is not the problem. Achievement and adaptive scores drop once the work is asked of the child alone, so the learning disability is the split between competence inside a holding relationship and collapse when the page has to stand in for the teacher.

2013-170.sentence: The pair may already be in an enactment: intercourse has become a pass/fail test, she “fails” lubrication, and he presses for completion. Sensate focus breaks that two-person script by taking intercourse off the table so they stop living the old anxious pattern and can notice actual sensation.

2013-171.sentence: Humor here is a defense with extra mental room: the school-age child can hold two meanings at once, see the forbidden or silly second meaning, and laugh it into a safer form. Understanding double meanings in jokes is that new capacity; preschoolers still need language to stay more literal.

2013-172.sentence: You are not being a chauffeur; you stay in traffic until tachycardia and sweating fall so the ego can learn the fear wave is tolerable. Classical conditioning paired traffic with terror; remaining until that arousal fades rebuilds affect tolerance instead of letting avoidance run the day.

2013-173.sentence: A fetish works by displacement — arousal gets attached to something concrete and controllable, an object, instead of to the unpredictability of a whole human person. That's part of why fetishism is defined by that fixed, nonliving focus: a workaround for intimacy that feels safer than the real thing.

2013-174.sentence: A trial comment only lands after lorazepam 2 mg has brought the cocaine hyperarousal down enough that the adolescent can actually think. Psychological mindedness needs a cortex that is not flooded; you do not hunt insight while they are still tachycardic and scanning the room.

2013-176.sentence: Switching from methylphenidate to dextroamphetamine after a real trial isn't a verdict on the child — it's just trying a different stimulant on the same nervous system. Say that out loud, because families often hear a medication switch as 'he needs something stronger,' which can feel like escalating failure rather than ordinary trial and error.

2013-177.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the frame that holds when a helpful impulse wants to outrun the risk: primum non nocere means the first job is not to add injury. Beneficence wants to treat; this principle is the brake that makes you name the harm, the interaction, and the safer option before you act.

2013-179.sentence: Taijin kyofusho locates the danger in what leaks into the other person—gaze, face, odor—as if a bad part of the self will be put into them and injure them. That is projective identification in cultural clothing: the feared scene is not “I will be shamed,” but “I will contaminate you, and then I cannot repair it.”

2013-180.sentence: Supportive work stays in the present so you do not reenact the old scene of an unavailable adult disappearing into the patient’s childhood while the rent and the insomnia go unaddressed. Working primarily now is the technique: you sit in today’s crisis with the patient instead of becoming the next person who talks over it.

2013-182.sentence: Reading disorder is the most common learning problem in special education, and the harder work often isn't the phonics drills — it's helping the child tolerate the shame of a word not decoding without concluding 'I'm stupid' and giving up on the book.

2013-185.sentence: The frame is who holds the meaning: a professional interpreter, not a cultural spokesperson who closes the case. Nervios in Hispanic American communities names stress in the nerves; you still ask what this patient's nerves do, or confidentiality and curiosity both collapse into a group slogan.

2013-189.sentence: A WISC-IV full-scale IQ of 60 is only half of competence; self-esteem in this child lives in what they can actually do at home and school. The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, 2nd ed. (VABS-II) is the mirroring instrument: it asks caregivers whether daily function matches the low score before you call it intellectual disability.

2013-190.sentence: After a graft, the idealized body—the one that did not need a stranger’s organ—is gone, and self-esteem often crashes into guilt about depending on family and pills. That is why major depression, not PTSD or a brief psychosis, is the most common psychiatric illness after transplant: the self cannot yet feel like a whole person again.

2013-191.sentence: The wish is that ECT will wipe out emptiness, rage, and abandonment the way it can lift a melancholic episode. Borderline personality disorder is a negative predictor because the prohibition remains: the machine treats the major depression, not the characterologic storm that will still be there when the seizure is over.

2013-192.sentence: The fights are the couple’s way of repeating what they cannot yet put into words: how they already survive some hours without attacking. Solution-focused homework—“what are you doing differently when you are not arguing”—pulls that unrepresented stretch of peace into speech so they do not have to keep living it only as the next explosion.

2013-193.sentence: Once a preschooler can hold two minds at once, you stop being a mind-reader and become a person they can test, surprise, and recruit. The countertransference shift is the work: you feel less like a container of their thoughts and more like someone whose thoughts they are now tracking.

2013-198.sentence: The tantrums cluster around 'no' because ODD is fundamentally a fight over who gets to hold authority in the relationship, not a mood problem. Ask whether it happens only at home or everywhere — that tells you if he's opposing one particular adult or authority itself.

2013-201.sentence: At eleven, “best friend” means feeling cared about: care has to exist as a named fact, not only as recess or a group project. After trauma, that fact often never gets represented, so need is repeated in the body or dumped into the adult instead of being located in a peer who actually holds the child.

2013-204.sentence: This adult never developed the capacity to weigh a greater-than-50% chance of right-arm paralysis against freedom from seizures, so a guardian’s insistence cannot stand in for a mind that did not arrive. Court order is the frame when someone else is choosing a disabling resection the patient cannot authorize.

2013-209.sentence: A teenager who's still shy with real classmates but curious about naked bodies online hasn't split his world into 'good friends' and 'bad sexuality' — both belong to the same normal, developing interest in sex. That integration is exactly what makes this ordinary curiosity, not abuse, addiction, or confusion about orientation.

2013-211.sentence: Those missing-time splices and the hostile calls she cannot own mark a self that cannot stay in one continuous hour; integration is a capacity that will not be rushed by a new marriage or by your wish for a single narrator. Treat the gaps as a hard limit: you work with whoever is in the room today, and you do not demand that one person remember the old girlfriend’s voicemails before the work has earned that continuity.

2013-212.sentence: Compliance rises when someone can take in a trial comment and see their own part—panic about the kidneys, not “being difficult”—instead of only fighting the diuretic. A good C-L service is psychological-mindedness on the ward: one usable interpretation of the refusal, then the medicine actually gets taken.

2013-213.sentence: The frame here is who holds the limit on suffering: the typical “bad death” fear is dying in pain, not the hospital, delirium, or unfinished life review. Your ethical job is to name that fear plainly and keep analgesia and honesty in the room rather than outsourcing the end to vague reassurance.

2013-214.sentence: It's tempting to read this patient's fluctuating attention as a personality clash you need to manage in the room — but bilateral triphasic waves and a high ammonia say this is a liver-brain storm, not a relationship problem. Treat the delirium as delirium first; the psychology can wait until the ammonia comes down.

2013-215.sentence: School age is Erikson’s industry versus inferiority: the child is building personal worth through competence at reading, games, and making things work. “I am stupid” is that stage speaking; the developmental task is a real skill that can be mastered, not more parental love or a premature identity crisis.

2013-218.sentence: A psychiatrist can teach the public about alcohol problems in general, but diagnosing one named person from a news clip skips the single thing that makes a diagnosis valid: an actual examination. The ethical line isn't about fame or payment — it's that no doctor-patient relationship, and no exam, ever happened.

2013-220.sentence: The abdomen as the typical injury site in pregnant partner violence is a fact that can open insight: the blow is aimed at the pregnancy, not “just another argument bruise.” A trial comment after you see her alone—“it looks like the baby was the target”—tests whether she can use that observation without you diagnosing her partner from the hallway.

2013-221.sentence: Arbitrary inference is concluding with no evidence or against the evidence, and you cannot rush the patient past that habit by arguing the conclusion. The limit is time plus capacity: stay with the missing data until they can tolerate not-knowing, rather than filling the gap with a finished story.

2013-223.sentence: The 13-year-old who asks the same morning questions is asking you to hold the clock and the story, not to become another parent who answers forever. Anxiety is the usual partner of ASD, so you keep confidentiality while you still call school about bullying—the child is not the only informant, and you do not hand the limit to whoever is loudest.

2013-224.sentence: The emergency bay can already be in an enactment: staff treat the obese 26-year-old’s headache as noise while the swollen discs are the finding. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is that two-person pattern—dismiss her body, miss the raised pressure, and risk her vision.

2013-225.sentence: Pinning every surge on coffee or a bad thought is rationalization: the ego invents a cause so the attack is not random. Panic disorder still needs at least some unprovoked attacks that peak in minutes; if a neat trigger covers every episode, you are watching a defense, not the diagnosis.

2013-226.sentence: Speech in the ICU is not ego strength: he can answer a simple question and still cannot hold the facts or the affect of prolonged ventilation. A living will or a durable power of attorney carries the wish when reality testing fails; a DNR or DNI slip is a later order, not the paper that tells the team what he already decided.

2013-229.sentence: Looking to the partner before speaking is not politeness; it is the symptom doing work—keeping the room safe by not naming the threat. Private, concrete questions about domestic violence take that job off the patient’s mouth so the couple’s story cannot keep the violence hidden.

2013-230.sentence: A securely attached toddler seeks contact eagerly because the parent is still a usable base, not a source of poison or demand. Reunion is the “dose”: proximity is taken in, distress metabolizes, and play can start again.

2013-231.sentence: Calling it hypochondriasis first is a defense: denial of the body so nobody has to sit with a real lesion. The most important differential is a medical condition, because ruling that out is what keeps the consult from becoming a shared wish that the abdomen is “only” in the mind.

2013-232.sentence: The apnea test is not a metaphor; it is the limit that says the brainstem no longer drives breathing. Families and teams need that named finding so grief is not asked to do the work of a neurologic exam.

2013-233.sentence: Derealization is the attack doing a job: the room goes unreal so the surge of fear does not have to be fully inhabited. Ask whether it is recognized as an odd inner state; if it is held as fact, you are no longer in a panic attack.

2013-235.sentence: Isolation of affect, intellectualization, and reaction formation keep feeling off the table so the hour stays a problem to solve rather than a relationship that will end. Suitability for uncovering therapy is limited until time, fees, and termination can be felt as losses, not just procedures.

2013-236.sentence: Compulsive sexual behavior is a drive collision: the erotic wish and the prohibition keep repeating as acting instead of as conflict you can talk about. Twelve-step groups hold both sides at once—the craving and the rule—better than diving into psychodynamic work before the enactment is contained.

2013-237.sentence: Peek-a-boo works because object permanence lets the infant keep a picture of the caregiver when the face vanishes. That returning, delighted gaze is early mirroring: the self stays coherent because the other is expected to come back, not gone forever.

2013-238.sentence: When one member names hopelessness and suicide and another immediately feels the same, that is contagion: the suicidal state has jumped bodies instead of staying named as one person's pain. Universalization can still be useful—you are not the only one—but the work is to hold the shared bad feeling without inviting a comparison of methods.

2013-241.sentence: Reserpine and methyldopa carry real histories of triggering depression, and hydrochlorothiazide can drop his sodium again — so picking the wrong drug here doesn't just raise blood pressure risk, it risks confirming his fear that every treatment makes him worse. Atenolol or spironolactone let you treat the hypertension without restaging that old story.

2013-243.sentence: Schizotypal personality already shows the same thin ego functions that fail in schizophrenia: reality testing is leaky enough for odd beliefs and unusual percepts, but not shattered. That family history is the heritable marker that those particular ego muscles—reality testing and the stimulus barrier—run thin in this pedigree.

2013-244.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s first task, trust versus mistrust: hostility is often the last available protest when the room already feels unsafe. Name and validate the affect first so the patient can feel met rather than managed; logic, threats, or a needle only confirm the mistrust.

2013-246.sentence: The psych consult is projective identification: the team parks fever, weight loss, ataxia, and months of memory loss in “depression” so they do not have to hold HIV. Depressive concern is ordering the HIV test and staying with what it means, not splitting the body off as a mood case.

2013-247.sentence: The “defect” is a split-off bad object parked on one feature so the rest of the self can stay clean and lovable. Fluoxetine can quiet the checking enough that the patient can start to see the face as a relationship problem, not a surgical one.

2013-248.sentence: Cape-like loss of pain and temperature will recruit you to become the skeptic who calls it functional and walks away. Syringomyelia is the central-cord lesion that explains that pattern; naming it keeps you from living out the dismissive doctor they already expect.

2013-249.sentence: Your training-superego — the inner examiner — will demand a quick major-depression label and a prescription before you have asked what the illness means. Inquiring what the patient believes explains the symptoms is how you keep conscience from turning into a rigid Western script.

2013-250.sentence: The flattery is projective identification: she lodges an idealized erotic self in you, and you start to feel special as if the fantasy were about your actual person. Consultation is the repair move — you take the projection back instead of acting from that mutual glow.

2013-253.sentence: Valproate is doing two jobs at once: it holds the mother's bipolarity and it quietly writes risk onto the fetal neural tube. Naming that conflict early lets the wish for stability stay in the room without pretending the fetus is not already in the bargain.

2013-254.sentence: The feared object tells you which developmental task never quite arrived: being seen by others versus being trapped without an exit. Social anxiety is a later-arriving self-in-the-gaze problem; agoraphobia is a panic-of-no-escape problem, even if both people avoid the same store.

2013-256.sentence: When a patient answers 'both are round' instead of 'both are fruit,' it's easy to feel a flash of irritation or the urge to over-explain — that reaction is worth noticing before you write the answer off as him just being slow. Abstract reasoning is exactly the capacity being tested, and your own response to a concrete answer is data too.

2013-257.sentence: Conduct disorder on top of ADHD is not extra fidgeting; it is aggression that has never been remembered as pain and so keeps getting enacted as fighting, theft, and rule-breaking. The worse adult prognosis is the unrepresented injury repeating in the body and the relationship instead of becoming a story.

2013-259.sentence: Caregivers keep a self together by feeling useful and competent, not by being forced into one heroic person or an even split. Your job is to shore up that competence—who can dose meds, who can give respite, what actually calms agitation—so the family’s work actually improves the patient’s care.

2013-261.sentence: A prior suicide attempt is the fact you have to hold, not a feeling you can talk away into “hopelessness” or family history. Contain it—keep the raw dread thinkable—by asking method, intent, rescue, and what treatment followed, instead of evacuating the risk into a softer predictor.

2013-262.sentence: Adult partner violence is not a mandated police report the way child abuse is, so you do not seize the frame by calling the cops or ordering him to leave tonight. You hold the limit by listening and mapping safety, threats, and what he wants next—without blaming him or pretending this is rare in gay relationships.

2013-263.sentence: Waxing and waning alertness after sertraline is not “deeper depression” the patient needs insight into; it is delirium until proven otherwise. Check serum electrolytes first, because an SSRI in a 65-year-old often means SIADH hyponatremia, and a sertraline level or DST will not name that.

2013-264.sentence: The hated boss in his head was an unrepresented state: a felt “mean” figure with no room for another mind. Mentalization is noticing the gap—the real voice in the office versus the one inside—so the old scene is no longer only repeated as hatred.

2013-265.sentence: The anxious pulmonary patient will try to make you the instant soother—the one who hands over alprazolam, clonazepam, or propranolol so the dread drops now. Your countertransference is the urge to comply; naming that pull lets you stay the doctor who offers buspirone, a 5-HT1A agonist that calms without stealing respiratory drive.

2013-266.sentence: Left anterior cerebral artery infarction hits the medial frontal lobe and paracentral lobule, so the right leg fails while the hand and face are spared—and the self goes quiet. Abulia is a competence injury: this person needs you to mirror remaining agency, not to treat passivity as consent or as a personality.

2013-268.sentence: Mild pediatric anxiety is doing a job: it keeps the child off the stage and recruits adults to remove the danger. Psychotherapy alone is first-line because the work is to find what the worry is protecting, not to start an SSRI or a benzodiazepine before that meaning has been heard.

2013-270.sentence: An incapacitated patient can't carry the weight of a major medical decision, so it lands on you — and beneficence means resisting the pull to just decide alone because that feels faster. Find the right surrogate and let the patient's own best interests guide the choice, rather than acting as though you alone know best.

2013-272.sentence: CBT for panic leaves a method the patient can still run after termination: cue logs, interoceptive exposure, and walking back into avoided places. Pills do not install that skill, which is why relapse rises after they stop and CBT’s advantage appears at discontinuation.

2013-273.sentence: Selective mutism is avoidant behavior, not opposition or a language lesion: the child splits a safe home object from a dangerous school audience. Silence protects the speaking self rather than handing it to strangers who feel like bad objects.

2013-275.sentence: Low-dose imipramine treats the pain–depression circuit instead of another workup that functions like a moral exam. The preferred act is not more investigation or an opioid; it is a TCA that can quiet both the abdomen and the self-attack that keeps the pain on trial.

2013-278.sentence: Heroin withdrawal (yawning, lacrimation, myalgias, diarrhea) smashes suppression—the ordinary “I can ride this out” lid—so suicidal talk rushes in as a bid to end the body-pain now. Treat the opioid withdrawal first; the death-wish often shrinks once the autonomic storm is named and medicated.

2013-280.sentence: This sits on industry versus inferiority: the young lawyer treats sufficient sleep as slacking on the high-profile case, so the ego never clocks out. Sleep paralysis with a sensed intruder is the body forcing a stop the career-self will not grant; the first treatment is sleep, not prazosin.

2013-282.sentence: The 4-per-second generalized spike-and-wave of childhood absence epilepsy is dumped into the teacher as “this girl will not pay attention”—projective identification, meaning the blank second is put into the adult so the child is not seen as briefly gone. Depressive concern starts when you repair that misread: it is a seizure, not a character flaw.

2013-283.sentence: Buying shares turns you from the person who holds both the hopeful and the predatory parts of the patient into a partner who needs the business to win. Once money and care occupy the same object, the “good doctor who believes in recovery” and the “investor who benefits” cannot be kept apart in one mind.

2013-284.sentence: He's finally responding after failing imipramine, nortriptyline, duloxetine, and selegiline — that hard-won stability is worth protecting from an insurer's blanket rule about bupropion and seizures. Continuing the low, divided SR dose that hasn't caused a seizure is the clinician staying an advocate for what's actually working, not just deferring to policy.

2013-285.sentence: Hematemesis, renal tubular acidosis, CPK 3120, and brain atrophy land in the room as a pair of people deciding whether the story is “mystery medical” or “glue and solvents.” If you skip products the patient does not call drugs, the two of you collude in the same not-naming that kept the inhalant use going.

2013-288.sentence: A contracted missed-visit fee is containment: the rage or shame of the empty hour gets a named rule instead of being dumped as “you don’t care” or “I don’t exist.” The APA stance only holds if you put that container in the contract first, so the feeling can be thought rather than evacuated by a surprise bill.

2013-289.sentence: The ex-girlfriend leaving him is a blow to self-esteem, and the plan to “teach her a lesson” is an attempt to restore a grandiose, competent self by force. Your job is still the Tarasoff duty: inform the police that he poses a potential danger, rather than treating the threat as only a narcissistic rant.

2013-290.sentence: The 13-year-old’s development still depends on a home that does not throw children across rooms; “no medical injury” does not make the rage safe. You tell the 22-year-old that you must report to child protective services, because protection cannot wait for insight into why the story arrived today.

2013-291.sentence: Hypnosis after trauma works when a harsh inner critic can briefly stand down and allow focused attention instead of scanning for danger. In hypnotizable people it can safely decrease pain and stress; it is not a moral shortcut that “makes half of patients worse.”

2013-292.sentence: Recurrent “unexplained” visual loss and old hemiparesis recruit you into the conversion-hysteria role—the doctor who treats the body as a message. Bilateral cortical blindness, spasticity, extensor plantars, and the angiogram/MRI point to sickle cell vaso-occlusion, so you stay the neurologist, not the interpreter of symbols.
