2013-293.sentence: In patients over 65, alcohol dependence is less common, but the same “few drinks” after a fall can be the body repeating unmourned loss without a story attached. The adverse consequences are more serious—falls, drugs, isolation—so you treat the drinking as high-stakes even when the narrative is thin.

2013-296.sentence: Engagement and differentiation running together is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion on a group scale: members need a “we” and also a special seat next to the leader. Competition for time is not failure of bonding; it is the group trying on both belonging and a distinct self at once.

2013-298.sentence: This is countertransference: leftover urgency to save the alcoholic parent is now aimed at this patient, so “we are making progress” is the psychiatrist’s wish, not the work. A trial comment starts with that pull to convince rather than another lecture on quitting.

2013-299.sentence: Duty to other hospitalized patients is the frame after an assault: the ward’s safety limit outranks keeping this admission “therapeutic.” Arrest and transfer say the community of remaining patients holds the boundary, not the assailant’s treatment preference.

2014-2.sentence: Twelve-step facilitation recruits you as sponsor-stand-in: someone who names the disease and then steps aside so a Higher Power can hold what he cannot. Notice the countertransference pull to become the extra self he surrenders to; stay a facilitator of that surrender, not a rival savior.

2014-3.sentence: Right parietal damage leaves the left hemiplegia unrepresented: she cannot remember the limb as hers, so she repeats the loss by handing the arm to you. Anosognosia here is not stubborn denial; the body-self map is gone, and the dyad has to carry the missing half.

2014-5.sentence: Fluoxetine as first-line asks whether her ego can wait through the lag and sit with early activation without bolting. Panic treatment tests affect tolerance: she has to hold weekly attacks while the SSRI slowly restores a margin of control.

2014-7.sentence: The team is already in an enactment: they are living a fight with the entitled patient instead of treating him. Model appealing to that entitlement so staff stop the punish-or-submit loop and still get the labs done.

2014-9.sentence: The first job is the frame: name the rule, protect the staff, and keep treatment possible. Watching, referring, or charging a dollar for each "stupid" is dodge-work; limits are the intervention that stops the abuse from becoming the treatment.

2014-11.sentence: Untreated mania is not a weekend of high self-esteem; the grandiose self can stay inflated for about three months. Counsel the family with that clock so they do not wait for a one-week crash that the untreated episode will not deliver.

2014-13.sentence: Methylphenidate is not a personality transplant; it loans the eight-year-old a bit of prefrontal braking so energy, the short fuse, and homework slips do not have to live only as body-discharge. Video games already hold his attention, so the drug is aimed at the developmental gap between that locked-in play and the classroom demand to sit, wait, and finish.

2014-14.sentence: You asked for guns out of the house after a suicide attempt; the parent said no and you filed with child protective services, which is you holding the safety limit when the family would not. Autonomy is the ethical concept that fights that move: the parent’s claim to keep firearms and decide how they are secured, even when that claim collides with the child’s protection.

2014-15.sentence: The argument left something unsayable, so the throat went mute while a loud cough still proves the cords can close—conversion, not a torn larynx. The symptom is the fight relocated: speech is banned, but the apparatus is intact, which is why this is conversion disorder rather than injury or selective mutism.

2014-16.sentence: Sleep terrors start in childhood: a non-REM surge of terror and frantic movement, not a dream you can interpret at the bedside. There is no insight in the episode itself—eyes open, poorly organized thrashing, amnesia after—so you do not treat it as a REM nightmare or a seizure until the developmental picture fails.

2014-18.sentence: Four weeks is the line where a normal, if miserable, reaction to nearly being robbed — the startle, the replaying memories, the pulling away from friends — is still expected, not a disorder. Past that point the same picture gets called PTSD, which just means the mind hasn't managed to settle the story yet.

2014-20.sentence: The Wisconsin Card Sorting Test asks whether he can shift set after feedback, the same muscle he needs to take in a trial comment about his own impulsivity. A near-perfect MMSE can hide a frontal patient who cannot see his perseveration, so insight is not available to keep his meds safe.

2014-21.sentence: You hold the frame by having him listen to that song again and again with no alcohol until the pairing dies; that is extinction, not a new trick. Disulfiram-nausea or non-alcoholic beer would start a different pairing; they do not unpair the cue.

2014-22.sentence: They dump “declare my spouse the problem” into you as raw heat. You contain it—hold the blame long enough that it becomes thinkable as a fight between them, which is the common move in every couple and family therapy: difficulties named in relational terms.

2014-23.sentence: The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule watches whether joint attention can appear in a structured play hour; you cannot rush a three-year-old into looking with you. Speech and relatedness have a developmental limit you observe, not force, once hearing is already cleared.

2014-24.sentence: If you keep demanding her name as if she is hiding it, you enact the assault’s erasure: two people repeating pressure on a mind that cannot retrieve episodic memory. Driving and fluent speech stay because procedural skill is not the file that went missing.

2014-26.sentence: Sertraline in the gut is not just a side effect; it is the first feed, and nausea can feel like the pill is poisoning you. Name the GI hit before she leaves or the relationship to the medicine ends in the bathroom, not in the next visit.

2014-27.sentence: Do not let olanzapine become a convenient cover: that is denial, pushing the two-day drink-stop out of awareness while the EEG already shows withdrawal delirium. Name the tremor, fever, and inattention as alcohol leaving the body, or the defense will keep you treating the wrong fire.

2014-28.sentence: This man never built a reliable holding environment—the late-arriving capacity to stay in treatment without someone coming to him. Assertive community treatment is that missing developmental function: the team arrives so impulsivity and violence are not left to an exhausted family.

2014-29.sentence: The erection that works alone and fails with his wife is a conscience problem in the marriage bed: desire feels permitted only offstage. Bring her in for behavioral exercises so the couple, not a private guilt, becomes the site of the work.

2014-30.sentence: The sudden vertigo, diplopia, ataxia, and occipital pain during neck cracking is raw body-terror that has to be named before anyone can think. Contain it as vertebral artery dissection—do not evacuate it into “anxiety after chiropractic”—or the dread stays unthinkable and the artery keeps tearing.

2014-31.sentence: A same-sex night or a heterosexual fling is often the adolescent self trying on a version of itself before the self-concept is solid, not a failed gender identity. If parents treat that experiment as a disorder, they pull the mirroring—the admiring, confirming look—the kid still needs while sexual self-esteem is under construction.

2014-32.sentence: CAMS found combination sertraline plus CBT beat either monotherapy for pediatric GAD, separation anxiety, and social phobia. Sertraline can drop the arousal enough that a trial comment in CBT—“notice how your mind just predicted catastrophe”—can actually land instead of bouncing off a flooded nervous system.

2014-34.sentence: Lithium is at its best in acute mania and in maintenance, which is why the “how soon can I stop?” question is not only pharmacokinetic. You are being recruited as either the jailer who will never let the high return or the accomplice who will unlock the door too early; name that pull before you write the taper.

2014-35.sentence: Two doses of mirtazapine, then euphoria and standing on a chair, with no prior mood history, is substance-induced bipolar disorder, not a lifetime Bipolar I sentence. The team’s rush to brand him is a superego move: conscience wanting a hard, moral diagnosis instead of sitting with the more modest fact that a drug flipped the switch.

2014-36.sentence: On a locked unit, the wish to belong and the discharge clock collide every day, so cohesion never has time to form. Turnover is the real impediment: members leave before the group can metabolize either the longing to get close or the fear of it.

2014-37.sentence: New burning pain that makes her clamp down, which then makes the burn worse, can look like a body repeating something she has no words for. Still send her to gynecology first: an unrepresented state is a hypothesis, not a license to skip the exam that would find infection, vestibulitis, or endometriosis.

2014-39.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the first frame rule: do not manufacture a phobia in an 11-month-old to prove classical conditioning. Little Albert could not refuse the pairing of the stimulus and the loud bang, so Watson treated the baby as apparatus rather than a subject with a right not to be harmed.

2014-40.sentence: Amphetamine can flood the ED with persecutory objects: the computers become flashing accusers and a knife is recruited as a hard, external protector. That split is the drug collapsing inner threat into the machines in the room—check the urine before you baptize this as a primary psychotic break.

2014-45.sentence: He used his spouse as a regulator—someone nearby to dump rage into—then broke the hand that reached for her. Naming that the violence is his job to stop protects the attachment system from turning proximity into a license to hit.

2014-49.sentence: Hiding behind confidentiality here is denial: you treat a seven-year bond—and a husband you already know—as if it never existed so you do not have to feel the death. Calling him is ordinary grief work, not a lawsuit dodge or a chart leak; the relationship already left the consulting room.

2014-50.sentence: He and the family were already living one scene: he insisted the house smelled foul, they argued about a smell that was his medial temporal lobe talking. HSV encephalitis makes that two-person story; the T2 temporal signal and the seizure are the same circuit, not a private hallucination you can ignore.

2014-51.sentence: He wants DDAVP so overnight camp can stay a secure base instead of a wet sleeping bag that would push him out of the group. Father’s bedwetting until 12 is attachment data, not a lab cue: the family already knows this body, and desmopressin is a short bridge so he can stay close to peers.

2014-58.sentence: Moderate ID here is not a verdict on insight; she already shows what she can use—self-care with a spotter, a greeter job with a supervisor, second-grade academics. A trial comment stays concrete: “You do better when someone is nearby,” which she can take in, rather than asking her to narrate her own disability.

2014-59.sentence: This patient's real fear is 'am I losing myself,' and the honest answer right now is no — she still drives, cooks, and lives alone despite the memory dip. Naming it MCI instead of dementia respects both the fear and the facts, so you protect the independence she still has instead of handing her a verdict she hasn't earned yet.

2014-63.sentence: You can't argue someone out of a fixed delusion, because the belief was never built from evidence in the first place. Empathizing with the fear behind "they're poisoning my dog" — without confirming or confronting the belief itself — keeps the alliance alive, which does more for this patient than being right ever could.

2014-66.sentence: Projective identification goes a step past plain projection: the disowned feeling isn't just parked in you, it's pushed hard enough that you get recruited to act it out — snapping at the nurse instead of simply noticing you're irritated. That pull to actually perform the feeling, not just receive it, is what separates this from ordinary projection.

2014-67.sentence: Pictures of the nanny keep her as a usable inner object, so the preschooler can miss her instead of erasing her. Avoiding her name is not mercy; it makes the loss unthinkable, and unthinkable losses come back as clinginess, night fears, or sudden tantrums.

2014-70.sentence: The freshman on blotter LSD is recruiting you as the last sane object who can make “things aren’t right” stop. Meet that transferential plea with 20 mg of diazepam and a calm, present person—not isolation in the dark, not hourly haloperidol—because a bad trip is panic clinging to you, not a need to be abandoned or neuroleptically crushed.

2014-71.sentence: An overvalued idea is a stubborn, self-defining conviction—here the “Neanderthal” brow that exams call normal-range—that still yields a millimeter to reality, unlike a delusion. The harsh conscience has found a single facial ridge to prosecute; surgery would only feed that prosecutor, not settle the case.

2014-74.sentence: When only one partner is motivated, one of them is trying to hand you their panic to hold while the other won't pick up their end, so there's no shared container for the work. Affairs, sex problems, co-parenting fights, even old unresolved arguments can still be worked through together; a one-sided project just turns into blame instead of insight.

2014-76.sentence: Frontal-lobe atrophy takes the very capacity this lens needs: the person can no longer see their own part or use a trial comment, because initiative and affect have gone dull. You are not meeting resistance; you are meeting missing cortex, so insight work waits while you name the apathy as illness, not character.

2014-77.sentence: The clock on autism can't be rewound: what makes this diagnosis is that the social differences were there before age three, not that anyone — parent or school — was slow to notice them. IQ, aggression, temperament, and even a parent's lack of worry are red herrings; only the early timeline actually makes the diagnosis.

2014-78.sentence: CBT for insomnia outlasts the pills because it leaves the patient with something they own — skills for handling a sleep-disrupting mind — instead of a nightly prop they have to keep taking. Zolpidem, trazodone, and the rest can quiet a bad night, but the relief disappears the moment the prescription does.

2014-81.sentence: Winnicott’s holding environment is the caregiver’s job of keeping the child safe enough that spontaneity can happen—assertiveness grows from surviving a little frustration, not from never meeting it. The hovering parent who finishes every task is doing the opposite of holding: she is erasing the struggle that would have built a sense of competence.

2014-84.sentence: Parents who still see explosions after a moderate stimulant are recruiting you to be the person who finally “stops the badness,” usually by adding an atypical or swapping to divalproex. That pull is countertransference: you feel pressured to become the punitive or sedating parent. The clinical move is to stay the optimizing doctor and push the long-acting stimulant first.

2014-89.sentence: Asking how rested someone feels after only three or four hours of sleep is the question that separates mania from insomnia: a manic patient feels fueled and ready to go, while an insomniac feels wrung out and desperate for more sleep. The other options ask about the sleep itself; this one asks about the mood underneath it.

2014-91.sentence: Refusing wound care while asking nurses to feed him splits the staff into two objects: the all-bad pain-givers and the all-good feeders. Reward for helping with dressings and calories keeps those functions in one relationship instead of letting him park all the good in the spoon and all the bad in the debridement.

2014-94.sentence: At the curb the three-year-old has acquired a new capacity: he reads the mother's face before he moves. That is social referencing—using the caregiver's expression as a safety signal—not stranger anxiety or object permanence.

2014-98.sentence: The wish to “wake him up” with methylphenidate or bupropion is acting out: doing something stimulating instead of sitting with residual cognitive dullness on clozapine. Fluoxetine is the indicated add-on here—it can lift negative and cognitive complaints and bump clozapine levels—so you stay with the only antipsychotic that already worked rather than chasing speed.

2014-99.sentence: Her lateness-equals-disgust story is transference: she installs a hating you in the five-minute gap. Tactical disclosure—briefly showing your real mind (“I ran late; I’m curious what you imagined”)—is the MBT move that restores two separate minds instead of a Socratic fight about who is right.

2014-101.sentence: Hippocampal tau tangles mean this mind is losing the apparatus that would use insight-oriented uncovering. Name Alzheimer disease, then shift technique toward support, orientation, and caregiver structure—you cannot interpret your way out of neurofibrillary degeneration.

2014-102.sentence: The pair co-authored the monster until one child’s shriek made pretend feel real, and the second child’s ego could not bind the surge. Withdrawal is the relationship saying the affect got too hot—not cheating, not a moral veto on harm themes, just too much anxiety for a four-year-old to stay in the game.

2014-106.sentence: The Santería curse is a live third in the room: faith, homeland, and family sit between you and the suicide risk. Learn from them the expected course of a curse-illness so you treat their map of danger, not a lecture on neurotransmitters.

2014-107.sentence: Empathy means taking in the patient's experience as they actually live it, not imagining how you'd feel in their shoes and handing that back instead. Staying with their inner world rather than substituting your own is what keeps a well-meaning therapist from quietly making the patient's story about themselves.

2014-109.sentence: Following commands during the thrashing means she is still in a two-person field with you, not in a cortical electrical storm that has taken the self offline. The ethical job is to hold that limit without a public unmasking in the bay: treat the events as a communication you will work with later, not as a lie you expose.

2014-110.sentence: Paranoia is what amphetamine psychosis does for the person: it turns a catecholamine flood into a plot, so the terror has an author instead of being formless. That is why you see intense suspiciousness after a stimulant binge, not the alogia and flattening that mark a primary process illness.

2014-111.sentence: Another SSRI that costs him his appetite, GI comfort, and sexual function would be trading one depression for a body he can't bring into a relationship — at thirty, that's a real cost, not a minor side effect. Bupropion treats the depression through a different mechanism than the one that already failed him, without repeating those losses.

2014-113.sentence: Psychological mindedness already arrived; what is late is the capacity to stay inside a good-enough relationship without treating vague inadequacy as a verdict that he must leave. Twelve sessions of brief psychodynamic therapy use that observing ego on the old sense of not-enough, which CBT, IPT, or supportive work would not target as cleanly.

2014-115.sentence: They keep recruiting you as either the scolding parent or the buddy who says drinking is fine. Motivational enhancement therapy holds the ambivalence itself—the two wishes at once—so you do not become either figure.

2014-116.sentence: The adult sibling is still inside the consult frame, even two years later; attraction that feels new is often leftover heat from that triad. APA ethics therefore bars romance with any third party, not only the identified adolescent.

2014-118.sentence: The primary team is already living a two-person pattern: they need psychiatry to turn a worship state into a diagnosis. Worldwide, those ‘taken over’ episodes are usually normal pieces of religious and ritual events, not depersonalization or psychosis.

2014-120.sentence: Cycling through the ED is doing a job: it is asking for a container big enough that the child does not have to leave home. Wraparound services exist to hold that dysregulation in the community and prevent hospitalization or residential placement.

2014-121.sentence: Integrity versus despair is the late-life task here: this attorney still works and still knows the people and animals are not real, so the ego has not given up a coherent self just because macular degeneration stole the visual field. Charles Bonnet is the cortex filling in a blind world; it is not a collapse of reality testing, and that distinction is what keeps this from becoming despair dressed up as psychosis.

2014-122.sentence: When mother answers every question and calls ulcerative colitis "our disease," her conscience has moved into his gut; he is not allowed a private body or a private illness. Enmeshment, in Minuchin's sense, is that sanctioned gap in boundaries: guilt and loyalty replace a child's right to speak for himself.

2014-124.sentence: The 2-year-old with a car next to the toddler with a truck is holding two separate play-worlds side by side; good and bad, mine and yours, are not yet mixed in one shared scene. Parallel play is object relatedness at arm's length: near enough to feel another mind, not yet ready to assign roles or feed the same doll.

2014-125.sentence: Transient psychosis in borderline personality is a mind that cannot hold itself together under abandonment pressure, not a new primary psychotic illness. Uncovering interpretations will shred that mind further; you support, name the stressor, and wait for reality testing to come back before you go deeper.

2014-126.sentence: After the house is gone, hopelessness is the mind saying agency itself has been destroyed, not a buried feeling that needs to be excavated. Structured steps that rebuild self-efficacy, and CBT that challenges the conviction that nothing will ever improve, restore a usable ego before you chase terror or start an SSRI or propranolol for prophylaxis.

2014-131.sentence: Capacity here turns on appreciation: she can name pills and needles, but she cannot take in that oral antibiotics already failed and sepsis is next. Some limits will not wait for family, a proxy, or a better MMSE; the consequence is already in the room.

2014-132.sentence: A June handoff without a real risk assessment is the wish to be done with residency winning out over the duty not to abandon a patient mid-crisis. Naming who's suicidal and what's been tried is how the outgoing resident stays responsible for the patient even after they've stopped being responsible for the chart.

2014-135.sentence: Object constancy is the late Mahler capacity to keep a good-enough picture of the other while you are frustrated, not Piaget permanence and not conservation. When that fails, the session after a vacation becomes splitting: you are all-good one hour and all-bad the next because the mind cannot hold both feelings at once.

2014-139.sentence: When your mind keeps leaving a flat patient, treat the drift as a signal that you have lost your function as a secure base — the person they use to stay regulated in the room. Sit still and scan what you feel toward them before you apologize, take notes, or cut time; that inner check is how you come back into range so they do not have to protest a therapist who already left.

2014-153.sentence: A contingency fee is projective identification built into the payment structure: the attorney's need to win gets planted in you, and your "opinion" quietly becomes an extension of their case instead of your own judgment. Staying on an hourly or flat fee keeps the evaluation yours to revise if the facts don't support the side that hired you.

2014-154.sentence: Keeping quetiapine going forever because the ward is finally quiet is an enactment: staff and physician are living “silence the dangerous elder” instead of reviewing the chemical restraint. OBRA 1987’s every-three-month taper attempt is the formal interruption of that two-person (really two-system) repetition.

2014-155.sentence: Supportive work’s job is to stabilize functioning and strengthen defenses, not to pry at a vertical split the patient cannot stay present for. Insight that asks a fragile mind to watch itself from the other side of that split is how they leave the room without standing up.

2014-156.sentence: Methadone was carrying impulse control and affect tolerance; carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, drops the level, and that borrowed ego strength evaporates into craving and irritability. Treat the interaction as a sudden loss of scaffolding, not as the patient “deciding” to relapse.

2014-157.sentence: Criticism, blame, and hostility are high expressed emotion: the family stops being a secure base and starts being a threat the patient has to monitor. Psychoeducation lowers that heat so proximity can regulate the psychosis again instead of triggering another relapse.

2014-162.sentence: The “younger man” is the third in the marriage: an 80-year-old’s sexual and generational place is under threat, and the children siding with mother seals him out. Delusional disorder (jealous type) keeps identity intact by locating the injury in her betrayal rather than in aging, and the rest of his mind—no hallucinations, intact cognition—stays organized around that one idea.

2014-168.sentence: ADHD plus ODD in a young child is mostly lived in the body and the home–school loop, not stored as thoughts you can interpret. A rewards program built on what the child actually enjoys is how you represent that storm: same clear contingency at home and school, instead of insight or imagery the child cannot yet hold.

2014-169.sentence: When the veteran asks why his brain is stuck on exits and slammed doors, notice the pull to become the one who either dismisses the scanning as 'just PTSD' or joins him in treating the world as permanently unsafe. That is the countertransference: you are being recruited as either a naïve civilian or a fellow sentry, and naming the hypervigilance as an old threat-detector still firing can keep you from enacting either role.

2014-170.sentence: IPSRT treats the relapse as something two people (and a whole household) keep making: late nights, red-eyes, and overnight shifts knock the social zeitgeber off its peg, and the mood follows. Lifestyle regularity is the interpersonal prescription—stable sleep, meals, and social timing—so the relationship stops being the place where the clock gets smashed.

2014-172.sentence: The toddler's language grows from the parent's affect-holding talk—frequent conversation and thinking aloud—more than from drills, because the child is borrowing the adult's words to bind impulse and name feeling. That is ego strength in the making: the parent who narrates the room is lending regulation, not just vocabulary.

2014-174.sentence: The fitness-for-duty eval is already an enactment: the impaired physician who refuses treatment pulls you toward being the secret-keeping colleague, and the system pulls you toward being the cop. You are not bound by usual confidentiality because this is not a treatment frame—if you protect him like a patient, you are living the cover-up instead of naming it.

2014-177.sentence: Alcohol is the most common preventable cause of intellectual disability, and it's often missed because a mother's drinking during pregnancy is exactly the kind of history that gets minimized or left out. A smooth philtrum and thin upper lip are the body's record of something the history alone might never have told you.

2014-178.sentence: Look at the patient and say you, not he: insight starts when they are a subject in the room, not a third-person case the interpreter is reporting on. A trial comment lands only if it is offered to the person, not narrated about them.

2014-181.sentence: Peek-a-boo is the infant playing a forbidden pair of wishes at once: make the face vanish, and keep it. Object permanence is what lets that game stay a game instead of a catastrophe—the object can go, so the wish to send it away does not have to be disowned.

2014-182.sentence: The body is telling the history the chart cannot: hypokalemia, hypochloremia, metabolic alkalosis, and a high amylase with a normal lipase after vomiting, not pancreatitis. Purging is an unrepresented state acted in the gut—what cannot be remembered as hunger, shame, or rage is repeated as emptying.

2014-185.sentence: Insight here is not a clever comment about death wishes; it is whether the family can see their part in leaving a firearm in the house. Reducing gun access is the prevention step that does not wait for the teen to become psychologically minded.

2014-186.sentence: Recent alcohol abuse is the limit that outpatient cutting cannot absorb: intoxication collapses the pause between 'to feel something' and a lethal slip. Admission is not a personality diagnosis; it is the ending of a plan that assumed she could still stop herself sober.

2014-191.sentence: OSA with enuresis, snoring, and large tonsils is fragmenting sleep, so the child cannot hold a good-enough night and looks impulsive by day. Fix the airway first; ADHD as a split-off “bad child” label is the relationship story you do not buy until breathing is restored.

2014-193.sentence: When the group starts risking self-disclosure and questioning your competence, they are recruiting you as the parent who will either collapse or punish. Name that testing—that is transference: an old authority scene lived in the room—rather than proving you are a good leader or slamming the lid back on Forming-level politeness.

2014-195.sentence: Not recognizing the family after the partner's assault is the mind's emergency exit: dissociative amnesia erases the people who make the trauma real. Intact identity, intact cognition, and a normal CT say this is protection by not-knowing, not a left temporal contusion.

2014-198.sentence: After a first break the family will try to make you either the oracle of cure or the prophet of inevitable decline. Emphasizing staying on antipsychotics is the transference job: you become the steady object who holds schizophrenia as treatable, not a verdict of chronic collapse.

2014-200.sentence: Five-year-olds sit on the hinge between initiative and industry: kindergarten asks them to produce, wait, and belong in a group, and home is where leftover baby-need is allowed to leak. The clinginess and regression are not a diagnosis; they are the child parking the leftover of the old stage so the new psychosocial task can start at school.

2014-201.sentence: Anhedonia in melancholia is not just a sad mood; it is a shutdown of wanting, as if pleasure itself had become dangerous or pointless. The symptom empties the day of incentive so the person does not have to risk desire, appetite, or morning hope.

2014-204.sentence: Poor insight after a first schizophrenia diagnosis recruits you into the role of the only one who still believes there is an illness, while the patient lives in a world where the antipsychotic is an insult. Notice the countertransference pull to argue or abandon; that heat is the dyad acting out the lost awareness instead of naming it.

2014-206.sentence: Taijin kyofusho sits at the collision of a wish to be seen and a prohibition against offending the group, so the odor becomes the compromise. Social phobia, body dysmorphic disorder, and somatic delusional disorder are the DSM neighbors because each is a different intensity of that same wish–shame fight.

2014-208.sentence: Playing doctor, naptime masturbation, bathroom peeking, and asking to see a peer’s genitals are thinkable curiosity. Mimicking intercourse is raw, undigested adult sexuality dumped into play—contain it as possible exposure or enactment, not as “just preschool.”

2014-212.sentence: Before you and dermatology lock into treating imaginary lice, ask about recreational alcohol and drugs—stimulants especially—because the infestation fight is already an enactment: two people living the old pursuit-and-refusal instead of naming what is happening. Substance-induced formication is the exit from that two-person repetition; antipsychotic mandates and forced psychiatry only thicken the chase.

2014-213.sentence: Habit reversal therapy trains the child to notice the premonitory urge and swap in a competing movement—suppression used as a skill, not as white-knuckle denial. The tic is not being psychoanalyzed away; the ego is learning a pause between urge and discharge, which is why this is first-line for mild-to-moderate tics before meds.

2014-214.sentence: Lorazepam is the first-line medicine here because catatonia with waxy flexibility is the mind holding two impossible objects at once: the need to act and the terror of acting, frozen as a statue. You do not add an antipsychotic that can worsen catatonia; you give a benzodiazepine that loosens the freeze so the person can rejoin a living relationship with food, meds, and you.

2014-215.sentence: A reflective statement exists to ensure that what the patient said was understood—support first, not challenge, not interpretation, not a hunt for more details. Early in the work this mind can use a mirror more than a probe; if you keep firing questions you raise the uncovering dose past what the interview can metabolize.

2014-216.sentence: Kleine-Levin syndrome can look like laziness or depression to a family watching their son sleep 18 hours a day and eat everything in sight, but the dulled, withdrawn presence between episodes is the illness, not a character problem. Naming it clearly stops the parents from moralizing a neurological event, which matters as much as the medical workup itself.

2014-217.sentence: A double bind is two messages that can't both be honored: Betty's parents praise the college plan and then punish her for its cost, so there's no version of "going" or "not going" that doesn't disappoint them. That's why she looks stuck rather than simply indecisive — every direction she could move gets penalized by the same people who opened the door.

2014-218.sentence: Clozapine is not only an antipsychotic here; it is the one agent shown to cut suicide in schizophrenia, so the “meaning” of the prescription is a concrete bid to keep the person alive. When other atypicals have failed that job, staying on olanzapine or quetiapine can function as a quiet bargain with risk rather than a treatment of it.

2014-219.sentence: This sits on Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair: late life is the work of keeping dignity while accepting real limits, and driving is often the last symbol of adult competence. Consulting state reporting law is how you hold both sides of that stage—you do not steal autonomy by fiat, and you do not abandon the public (or the patient) to a failing ego function.

2014-220.sentence: Inattentive ADHD next to a reading disability is often wrapped in denial: the child (and sometimes the school) treats “I just don’t like reading” as if attention and decoding were intact. Naming ADHD, inattentive type, undercuts that defense so the delay is treated as a brain-and-skill problem, not as laziness or a character flaw.

2014-221.sentence: Modeling is already an enactment in the waiting room: fear shrinks when another child lives the ride as fun, and the phobic child borrows that regulation instead of arguing with the fear. You are not just teaching a learning principle—you are staging a two-person scene where courage is caught by watching, which is why peer demo beats a lecture about bikes.

2014-222.sentence: IPT’s frame is present-tense relationships, not schemas, childhood insight, relaxation drills, or Rogerian reflection—so the limit you hold is “we work the interpersonal problem.” Increasing contacts and strengthening the friendships she already has is the technique that keeps that frame, instead of sliding into CBT, psychodynamic excavation, or nonspecific warmth.

2014-228.sentence: The side effect you must name first in a 78-year-old referred for ECT is cognitive dysfunction, not fractures or dental trauma. Memory gaps after treatment can leave the illness as something that happened to the body while the story of the depression cannot be held in words.

2014-229.sentence: Hope and the wish to be well are still colliding with a hard prohibition: she must now accept that treatment has failed and only dying remains. Validating the grief as a normal reaction treats that collision as work, not as a suicidal plan or a “distorted” thought you need to CBT away.

2014-231.sentence: A well-defined parent–child boundary is the family’s way of knowing who holds authority and who can still speak. That structure lets people see their own part without the kids running the marriage or the parents collapsing into peers.

2014-232.sentence: Directed masturbation, sometimes with a vibrator, treats female orgasmic disorder by taking orgasm out of the couple’s gaze so inhibition can loosen. The defense is often a freeze of excitement under a partner’s eye; practice alone lets sensation return before it has to survive another person.

2014-234.sentence: The church group is a selfobject: it mirrors her as more than a caregiver and props up a self that Alzheimer care is grinding down. Telling her to keep going protects that source of esteem; cheerleading or blaming her frustration would leave her more depleted.

2014-237.sentence: Sublimation is turning an unacceptable feeling into something the world actually values — the child's raw jealousy of a gifted sibling gets rerouted into real skill at martial arts instead of staying as rivalry with no outlet. The jealousy doesn't disappear; it gets used, which is why the child looks less envious once there's somewhere to put the drive to compete.

2014-243.sentence: Those cartoonish, fantastic “hallucinations” of conversion are a defense: the mind stages a childish scene so the fight with the partner never has to be felt as rage or loss. Unlike a psychotic hallucination, the vision is psychologically meaningful theater with intact reality testing—the patient is not reluctant, not multi-modal-psychotic, and not describing a single dry sensory fragment.

2014-245.sentence: Sedating an 85-year-old who is newly, specifically terrified is easier than asking what changed — but a urinalysis for delirium respects that something real broke in her, not just her behavior. Naming a UTI as the culprit treats the confusion as an injury to who she is, instead of a target for a benzodiazepine.

2014-247.sentence: The referring doctor's "special patient who needs really good treatment" is already a demand that you skip an ordinary start and become the extra-good object overnight. Hold the limit: you cannot rush a new therapy into "taking," and that hurry is how splitting between the old psychiatrist and you gets lived instead of named.

2014-249.sentence: Factitious disorder is a conscience bargain: being the patient is the allowed identity, so symptoms are produced to be recognized as ill, not to collect a check. Malingering uses the same conscious deception for external gain; the distinguishing motive is whether the sick role has been sanctioned as the moral solution.

2014-251.sentence: Splitting is doing the work here: this patient can't tolerate ‘we were both partly at fault,’ so the other driver becomes purely bad, and slashing his tires restores a clean, blameless self. That fury at property is not the same as a threat to a person — so Tarasoff's duty to warn was never triggered.

2014-253.sentence: The outbursts and morning stomachaches live in the child–school pair, not only in the parents’ story of a well-behaved home. A release to speak with the teacher is how you get the other person in the pattern, instead of treating the child as a one-person mind.

2014-255.sentence: Saying “Hi Daddy” into a toy phone is symbolic representation: the ego can let one object stand for an absent person. That is affect tolerance in action—the child holds Daddy in mind instead of needing the real body in the room.

2014-256.sentence: Specific phobia is the anxiety disorder that most often starts in childhood, when the mind is still sorting real danger from imagined danger. Binding fear to one object (dogs, dark, needles) is a developmental bargain: one fenced-off threat so the rest of the child’s world can stay usable.

2014-260.sentence: Crushing, snorting, or injecting the prescribed opioid is already an enactment: the two of you are living the old fight—more drug versus more control—instead of talking about pain and fear. Tolerance, late-dose withdrawal, and climbing milligrams are expected physiology; the route change is the relationship going underground.

2014-261.sentence: A subpoena is a demand at the door, not a court order; without the patient's consent you oppose it and hold the frame—the agreed boundary of who hears what. Calling the lawyer or handing the chart to a surrogate still leaks the session and teaches that the room collapses when the system knocks.

2014-267.sentence: Avoidant personality wants the relationship and still cannot take the last step; schizoid personality does not want it, so there is nothing to wait for. Termination thinking helps here: desire is present, but the capacity to bear rejection cannot be rushed, and the work is staying at that limit without calling the stall indifference.

2014-268.sentence: Copropraxia is an intrusive obscene gesture thrown off by chronic tics — not a message about you, your gender, or the room. Read it as an insult and you've invented an audience that isn't there; the tic disorder is the only relationship actually happening, so chart it as copropraxia, not an act aimed at you.

2014-270.sentence: A consult that arrives soaked in ‘IV drug use’ and a sad backstory can recruit you into treating a mood before you've ruled out a body falling apart. The real message here is a spinal epidural abscess — fever, percussion tenderness, paraparesis, saddle anesthesia, incontinence — and accepting the ‘depression’ frame instead of examining the spine is a trap, not a diagnosis.

2014-271.sentence: The frame here is honesty: you do not “protect” a dying child by keeping the diagnosis off the table. Silence leaves him alone with what he already senses, and it steals the last bit of autonomy he has left.

2014-273.sentence: Believing every lawyer is a demon isn't just a symptom to note — it is the wall that keeps this patient from ever letting counsel in. That inability to work with an attorney, not the delusion's content alone, is what fails Dusky's second prong and makes him incompetent to stand trial.

2014-277.sentence: Hypnotizability is not a trait you infer from gender, ethnicity, WAIS-IV IQ, or the MMPI-2; it tracks the capacity to engage imagination, which is how a person lets another mind become a temporary secure base. In hypnosis the voice of the clinician is used the way an attached child uses a caregiver: to regulate attention and body state from the outside until the inner scene can hold.

2014-278.sentence: Nocturnal pins-and-needles that shake out of the hand is carpal tunnel until proven otherwise, and the countertransference trap is letting yourself be recruited as the doctor who treats it as anxiety or “neuropathy.” That recruitment is the old medical-psych split: you become the dismissive listener while the median nerve keeps waking her.

2014-279.sentence: Rerouting the commute away from the usual bar is stimulus control, a CBT relapse-prevention move that outsources conscience to the map so the patient is not left alone with a brittle “just don’t drink” command. The superego here is too thin to win a nightly stare-down with the tavern; changing the route is the ethical work done in geography instead of guilt.

2014-280.sentence: Federal 42 CFR Part 2 holds substance use treatment records to a stricter confidentiality bar than suicidality, homicidality, psychosis, or ECT notes, because the law treats SUD shame as a special risk of exposure. That extra legal conscience exists so a subpoena cannot casually turn treatment into public punishment.

2014-281.sentence: Asking the enrolled MS patient’s spouse to join as a healthy control threatens voluntarism: free, uncoerced yes, not autonomy, capacity, or the information sheet. In the room you are being recruited as the kindly researcher who “just needs one more control,” while the spouse is pressured into the loyal-partner role and cannot easily refuse.

2014-282.sentence: Mood is the one MSE heading that lives in the patient’s words (“I feel empty”); affect, appearance, insight, and even much of thought content you infer from what you see and hear. After trauma, the named mood can be a thin label over what the body is still repeating, so quote the report and separately describe the observed affect.

2014-283.sentence: Normalization names the collision without forcing a confession: the wish to discharge tension (scream, hit) and the prohibition against harming a partner sit in the same sentence. By saying stressed people sometimes do things they did not intend, you give the suicidal patient and spouse a way to report intimate-partner violence without first having to own the forbidden impulse as uniquely theirs.

2014-287.sentence: This patient can already hold a trial comment: the chest burning might be benign, and still the mind snaps back to a missed infarct. CBT has the best evidence because it uses that sliver of psychological mindedness—seeing one's own catastrophic appraisal as a move, not as a coronary—rather than more reassurance or fewer cardiology visits.

2014-292.sentence: Marginalization is the cultural third in the room: no live allegiance to the native culture and no real uptake of the host, so there is no group ego to borrow when despair hits. That nowhere-identity is why suicide, alcohol, and other substances cluster here—not because someone “chose” the wrong customs, but because no we remains to metabolize shame.

2014-296.sentence: An alcohol blackout is anterograde amnesia while the person stays awake and talking—the superego, the inner judge, often treats that gap as a moral loophole rather than a memory failure. The conscience then either pummels him for what he cannot recall or quietly licenses the next binge because 'I wasn't really there.

2014-298.sentence: Declining the Facebook request protects the frame: fee, time, and a one-way window, not a mutual social feed. Ego strength in the psychiatrist is the capacity to tolerate the patient's disappointment without collapsing into friend-mode or hiding behind 'privacy' as the only reason.

2014-300.sentence: Kohlberg's highest stage judges action by universal ethical principles, not by the social contract or keeping order. The frame question is who holds the limit when principle and institutional rule collide—you still name the law, but you do not pretend Stage 4 is the ceiling.

2015-1.sentence: Nonmaleficence is the frame holding the limit when the ICU wants a drug and the heart cannot take it: you refuse the antipsychotic because QT prolongation plus bradycardia is already a harm waiting to happen. The team’s urgency can pull you into doing something; the ethic is to stay still until a safer plan exists.

2015-2.sentence: If you and the patient spend the hour proving alters, you are already in an enactment: living the hidden-self drama instead of talking about what is missing. Track the amnesia—the extensive inability to recall personal information—because that gap is the illness, not the performance of other personalities.

2015-3.sentence: Reaching for methylphenidate or modafinil is acting out: swapping one chemical booster for another so the deadline never has to meet withdrawal. Cut caffeine by 25% weekly and the ego stays in charge—he still works, and the dependence comes down on a schedule instead of a crash.

2015-4.sentence: The Eye opener on CAGE is the drink as a morning feed: alcohol has become the first object that proves the body cannot start the day. That is not a hangover tip; it is the relationship announcing that the bottle now holds the wake-up function.

2015-6.sentence: Nihilistic delusions in late-onset psychotic depression capture insight: if the bowels have stopped and the self is already rotting, there is no “I am depressed” left to work with. A trial comment about mood will bounce; you treat the delusion and the not-eating first, then see whether a mind that can look at itself returns.

2015-7.sentence: Tic severity usually crests in school years and starts to ease in adolescence, so the nine-year-old’s worsening is still on the typical clock, not a signal that time has run out. Hold the parents’ panic without rushing a med jump: the developmental limit here is that you cannot force the tic course to finish early, only contain the year until adolescence does some of the work.

2015-8.sentence: The finding that keeps showing up is the therapeutic alliance, not the diploma or the fancier manual. That alliance is Bion’s container: you take in the resident’s (and the patient’s) raw dread that nothing is working and give it back as a thinkable problem—stay in the relationship—rather than evacuating the feeling by switching therapies.

2015-12.sentence: In chronic PTSD with childhood-abuse dissociation, hypnosis is for volitional control of leaving the body, not for burying, rewriting, or amnestizing the abuse. Unrepresented trauma returns as lost time and dangerous driving; the work is to put a hand on the switch so the body does not have to repeat what cannot yet be remembered as a story.

2015-13.sentence: Do not treat this as a wish colliding with a prohibition. The malar rash, proteinuria, fever, pancytopenia, and pleural effusions name lupus cerebritis, and the visual-plus-auditory hallucinations with disorientation and one-of-three recall are a failing sensorium, not a neurotic compromise. Interpreting “persecution” as drive conflict here would miss the brain on fire.

2015-14.sentence: Pseudocyesis puts gender and the cultural demand to become a mother in the room as a third: her body produces amenorrhea, nausea, breast fullness, and a swollen belly as if that script were already true. The negative pregnancy test and empty ultrasound do not end the conviction because the identity stake is “I am supposed to be pregnant,” not a lab result.

2015-16.sentence: The suicidality is doing work: it marks the pain of a lifelong female identification colliding with a body that still has male genitals despite breast implants. That is gender dysphoria, not schizophrenia, transvestic disorder, or body dysmorphic nitpicking of a single feature.

2015-17.sentence: Sensate focusing is homework that rebuilds a childhood capacity: curious touch without a performance goal. By banning breasts and genitals at first, you let the couple recover exploratory play before intercourse became a pass/fail exam.

2015-18.sentence: The family and the patient are now a two-person persecution system: they experience a hostile, withdrawn elder, and the patient experiences alien thought insertion and control. A MOCA of 28/30 and an MRI with only age-related involution keep this as late-life schizophrenia, not a dementia the relatives can carry alone.

2015-20.sentence: Ages one to three are Freud’s anal window: the child wants it now, and the parent has to teach delay of gratification around toileting and “by myself.” That tug-of-war is how a toddler first learns a mind can wait, not a trauma to erase.

2015-23.sentence: Race on the form tracks visible physical categories; ethnicity is the thicker mix of language, religion, nation, and family practice—Haitian, Catholic, Creole, not just “Black.” Keep both, or you flatten a person into a checkbox and miss how they actually live.

2015-26.sentence: They asked you to manage suicidal ideation; your job is to hold that request and still name the real emergency: serotonin syndrome from linezolid plus sertraline (lithium and fever just muddy the picture). The frame is who sets the agenda—you do not treat the consult question while the MAOI-like antibiotic and the SSRI keep cooking the patient.

2015-27.sentence: A delusion of reference means the TV is not just on; it is aimed at them, so there is no leftover "maybe I am reading myself into this." You cannot trial-comment that until they can stand a sliver of ownership; right now the message lives entirely outside, in the news anchor.

2015-28.sentence: Disulfiram works when someone else actually watches the swallow—classically the partner—so the pill is not left to a lonely good intention that evaporates by evening. The partner holds both sides of the object: care that wants you sober and a limit that will not let you sneak the drink and the tablet apart.

2015-29.sentence: Intellectual disability is the comorbidity you plan around in autism, not a side note, because it sets how much the mind can use interpretation versus structure. You support function, language, and safety; you do not uncover conflict as if this were a neurotic child who just needs insight.

2015-30.sentence: Circumstantial speech still lands the job description; the long detour through the boss and coworkers is the cost of getting there. The extra stories buy time so a simple question does not feel like a demand to be pinned down in one clean sentence.

2015-32.sentence: Parents often have insight only into the loud half of combined ADHD—the oppositional-defiant fights—and none into the child’s own anxious part. A trial comment that names both comorbidities (“the arguing we see, and the worry he may not show”) tests whether they can use that second piece, not just the behavior chart.

2015-35.sentence: Mid-adolescence has a sexual timetable you cannot rush: a typically developing 15-year-old boy’s masturbatory fantasy is of explicit sexual acts, not the romantic stories or partner-response scenes of later years. The parent’s wish to end that rawness is a wish to terminate a phase that still has time left on the clock.

2015-36.sentence: The wish is to treat; the prohibition is that this is not your patient. What distinguishes the forensic exam from a general psychiatric evaluation is maintenance of confidentiality—you do not keep the usual clinical seal, because the evaluee was never in a treatment relationship with you.

2015-37.sentence: Each escape from the grocery aisle is negative reinforcement: the panic drop rewards flight, so the self never has to stay present while anxiety peaks. In self-psychology terms she is protecting a shaky sense of competence—better to be the person who “handles it by leaving” than to risk a public collapse that would shatter self-esteem.

2015-41.sentence: The biggest risk here is a biological parent with bipolar disorder, not race difference, open adoption, or infant placement. The parents’ worry about those other stories is a defense—displacement—so they do not have to sit with genetic loading they cannot adopt away.

2015-43.sentence: The frame here is not “is alprazolam allowed.” It is who holds the limit after a new PCP refused to keep writing it without a psychiatrist in the room. A past misuse history of other drugs or alcohol is the finding that turns as-needed alprazolam from a treatment contract into a substance you may be asked to become the new supplier for.

2015-45.sentence: The breakup ripped away the person she was using as a secure base, and the sertraline-overdose thought was a protest at that sudden loss of proximity. Seeing her the next day keeps you as a temporary base after she has already calmed, agreed to stay with family, and allowed you to speak with them—without turning the call into a late-night dose change.

2015-46.sentence: This child’s ego can handle school, friends, and play dates at home; what it cannot tolerate is distance from the attachment figures. Separation anxiety is the diagnosis because the feared catastrophe is getting lost or kidnapped—being away—not a global worry machine or a social-evaluation fear.

2015-49.sentence: When the child can hold one caregiver who is both feeding and frustrating, Klein calls that the depressive position: concern for a whole person replaces the split into all-good and all-bad. Repair becomes possible because the “bad” object is no longer a separate enemy you have to evacuate.

2015-50.sentence: Reality testing is intact here: culturally shared spirit-visions are not the same as a mind that cannot tell inner from outer. Ego strength is the schoolwork collapse—treat the function that failed, not the gift the family can still use.

2015-53.sentence: What predicts adult relating is the parent’s capacity to perceive and think about the child’s intentions—mentalization, not infant temperament or sibling drama. Uncovering “why I pick the same partner” only helps if that mind can still use another person as a thinking partner; otherwise stay supportive.

2015-54.sentence: The mother is splitting the parental pair: you may evaluate ADHD with her consent, but treatment without the father would enact her all-good/all-bad custody story. Ask for the divorce decree so you are not recruited as the good object who erases the other parent.

2015-55.sentence: The shrinking-body panic is not just vanity; it is a Kleinian dump of a hated small, weak self into the mirror so the patient can stay identified with a hard, inflated body. Anabolic-androgenic steroid abuse keeps that split going: the muscles are a paranoid-schizoid fortress against the soft, shrinking object he cannot yet mourn or repair.

2015-58.sentence: On a medical floor, “I’m fine” can be a symptom that keeps the ward moving and keeps terror off the chart. The Joint Commission’s primary risk factor—lack of proper assessment for suicide risk—means the missed ask is doing work: it protects staff from knowing how close the patient is.

2015-63.sentence: “Tell me more about how all this started” keeps the story in one room so the patient does not dissociate—leave without leaving the chair—into why-questions, shame, or a mid-life-crisis label. Open invitation holds both the affair and the repair in awareness; closed or moralizing probes push half the material offline.

2015-65.sentence: Exploitativeness in narcissistic personality is a limit problem: other people are treated as extensions, so endings and “no” never quite arrive. The work is not to rush empathy they do not have yet, but to hold time and refusal until using staff and family stops being the only way to feel whole.

2015-69.sentence: In this Southeast Asian dhat picture, nocturnal ejaculation is not remembered as ordinary sexuality; it is lived as a leak of vital essence through semen. What cannot be represented as ordinary desire or loss is repeated in the body as fatigue, abdominal pain, and weight loss.

2015-73.sentence: The commitment hearing can feel like two minds in one room: the frightened, dangerous patient you just saw, and the citizen whose liberty you are asking a judge to take. Clear and convincing evidence is the legal wall that keeps you from evacuating your own anxiety by overselling danger—or from splitting off the risk and understating it.

2015-74.sentence: You are holding two objects at once: the cold spouse in the story and the you who ended last hour before the patient finished. An interpretation names that they are one relationship in two rooms, so the patient can hate and need the same person without splitting you into “good listener” and “dismissive other.”

2015-76.sentence: After a sudden maternal death, the surviving parent and the school-aged children will co-create the next attachment field—silence, over-caretaking, or honest mourning. Ensuring psychosocial supports keeps that field from collapsing into one isolated dyad that has to carry the whole loss.

2015-77.sentence: Calling you by mother’s name is a parapraxis: the unconscious used a slip instead of a sentence. How far you unpack it depends on this ego—if the childhood was brutal, name the slip lightly and stay supportive; if the patient can play with it, the slip is already doing the uncovering.

2015-78.sentence: Transient global amnesia drops a family into a few hours of a parent who is present but not registering anything — repeated questions, no new memories, then a full return to normal with no memory of the gap itself. Naming the syndrome, and that recurrence is rare, turns the family's raw fear of ‘stroke’ or ‘losing her’ into something they can actually hold onto.

2015-79.sentence: Schizotypal oddness (auras, crystals, the surgeon’s “aura”) is not a phase you can talk someone out of in a consult; it is a lifelong temperament that has already set the limit on how close people get. Your job is to respect that ceiling: treat the appendicitis, do not try to force intimacy or “normalize” the magical thinking overnight.

2015-81.sentence: Midlife friendship loosens the childhood rule that your secure base has to be the same age as you. The fifteen-years-younger confidante can still be the person she turns to for regulation; proximity of soul matters more than proximity of birth year.

2015-82.sentence: Optic neuritis that remits in six weeks is a test of ego strength: can this person tolerate a body that suddenly fails, then seems fine, while MS still waits in the wings? Name the risk plainly so they can plan, not so they panic; reality testing includes holding a future diagnosis without collapsing now.

2015-84.sentence: Morning-coherent, afternoon-disorganized speech is the ward already enacting sundowning: the system “forgets” at 4 p.m. what it knew at 10 a.m. Treat the fluctuation as the diagnosis talking, not as two different patients, and do not argue with the afternoon exam as if it were a character change.

2015-85.sentence: The cough is nothing, and he still makes you the aggressor: that is splitting, holding you as all-bad so the good-you cannot exist in the same hour. Transference-focused psychotherapy names that pattern out loud instead of soothing it or arguing about your throat.

2015-86.sentence: Paroxetine is the SSRI most likely to put a serotonergic brake on ejaculation, so the tablet becomes a demand that he last longer for someone else. He slips it in at the door because needing a pill for sex can feel like proof he is defective, not just a 5-HT reuptake effect.

2015-87.sentence: The protective factor is not 50/50 custody or same-gender parenting; it is cessation of conflict between the divorced parents. You hold that limit: the child is not the mediator, the audience, or the courier for the fight.

2015-91.sentence: An accurate interpretation is a good object they did not invent, and that can stir Kleinian envy—the wish to spoil what the therapist just did well. Getting worse is the attack: they stay in the paranoid-schizoid position (split, all-bad, no repair) rather than feel depressive concern, which is ordinary guilt and a wish to make it right.

2015-96.sentence: The frozen house is a two-person (really four-person) pattern: Dad’s need for quiet and the kids’ fear of harming him lock together. A strategic task—a real visiting schedule—changes the dance without a speech about feelings; friends can come at agreed hours so guilt and protection stop running the clock.

2015-97.sentence: An acutely psychotic mind already cannot use uncovering; risperidone-driven akathisia makes it worse by flooding the body with restlessness that will be read as danger. Treat the motor side effect with propranolol 10 mg three times daily first, then support and contain—do not interpret or push the dose.

2015-100.sentence: If the patient cannot even register “apple, table, penny,” you do not have a partner for uncovering work. Technique follows that finding: support, simplify, and treat the sensorium before you ask this mind to remember or interpret.

2015-102.sentence: Attachment does not require bruises to break; emotional neglect still removes the person who should have been the secure base. Every form of early life stress, not only physical or sexual abuse, independently predicts adult psychiatric illness, so take the ‘it wasn’t that bad’ story as a clue, not a clearance.

2015-103.sentence: Beneficence is the ethical name for a two-person rescue: delirium has dropped him out of a peer conversation, so you and he briefly become a caretaker-and-cared-for pair. Overriding the refusal is not you being paternal alone; it is the two of you living a temporary parent–child setup until capacity returns and autonomy can re-enter the room.

2015-105.sentence: Reality testing is the ego function that failed: a man who believes he is a wizard with diplomatic immunity cannot appraise the actual courtroom. Competency to stand trial needs that function intact so he can understand the charges and work with counsel, not negotiate from a delusional embassy.

2015-107.sentence: Prader–Willi hyperphagia pulls the family into a kitchen-policing war: lock the pantry, chase the forage, ride the tantrum. That is an enactment—you and the parents are living a food-control struggle instead of naming the sequence (neonatal hypotonia, then insatiable seeking) and treating the 15q11–13 paternal-deletion physiology.

2015-108.sentence: The TAT’s person-by-a-window is a blank enough other that she will cast someone—often you—into the scene. Who she makes that figure be is a transference rehearsal, and the feeling the story leaves in you is the countertransference sample.

2015-109.sentence: Intercourse with a stuffed animal is not curiosity; it is a script the child cannot put into words, so the body and play stage what memory cannot hold. Watch for other unrepresented material—night terrors, sudden freeze, or sexualized play that looks rehearsed rather than exploratory.

2015-110.sentence: Seasonal depression pulls her inward just as she is trying to make a new attachment, so light therapy is a secure-base intervention: it restores circadian proximity to the sun without putting a fetus in the middle of a medication decision. When winter darkness isolates her from her husband, timed bright light can re-regulate the pair before they lose each other as co-regulators.

2015-111.sentence: Twenty minutes of dying-feeling panic is more affect than this ego can bind, so lorazepam buys minutes of impulse control and reality testing while the cortex comes back online. Fluoxetine is the long game; you do not ask a flooded ego to wait six weeks for containment.

2015-112.sentence: Homework and holidays keep him a father, not a visitor, which is the supportive structure this child’s mind can actually use after the family frame broke. Uncovering his grief or making him her companion loads her with adult affect she cannot metabolize.

2015-113.sentence: Postpartum psychosis is often bipolar bursting into the mother–infant pair, so two people are suddenly living inside one person’s mood episode. Treat the bipolar diathesis fast; the infant cannot wait while you sort whether this is “just” depression or trauma.

2015-114.sentence: The attack is projective identification in action: unbearable rage is forced into you so you feel the danger he cannot think. Call law enforcement first; you cannot interpret a split until the room is safe and the projection is no longer landing on your body.

2015-115.sentence: Interferon is a good object that can flip into a persecutor: it treats hepatitis C and can also deepen depression into suicidal ideation. You keep both faces of the drug in one mind so hepatology does not split the consult into “just start it” versus “psych said never.”

2015-116.sentence: The fight over med times, food delivery, and who is “abusing” him is an autonomy-versus-shame crisis, not a failed capacity exam. Name that he is hard to work with and plan the behavior so the team can hold limits without shaming him into another lawsuit threat.

2015-117.sentence: “I’m being left out again” is an automatic thought: a snap appraisal that arrives before a core belief even speaks. You catch it at the surface so a roommate’s phone call does not have to become a lifelong story of exile.

2015-118.sentence: Toddlerhood is when “no” first has to mean something, and limit setting is that parental task. Attachment already happened; now the child needs an ending to the impulse, not more stimulation or instruction.

2015-121.sentence: Calling this what it is—coercive—rather than dressing it up as friendly encouragement is what keeps it ethical: you're using real leverage, not hiding it. It's justified here because you believe that letting a recently suicidal, manic patient go home unmedicated risks losing him to the very crisis he was just hospitalized for.

2015-122.sentence: A holding environment is the parent's reliable presence that lets the infant protest, settle, and come back—attachment as a secure base, not a lecture. When you recreate that predictability in treatment, the patient can use you to regulate instead of scattering every time the hour ends.

2015-123.sentence: You two still have a conversation even when Broca's area has wrecked speech: the patient can close the eyes on request because comprehension is relatively spared. The interpersonal task is to wait, not fill the silence, so the pair of you do not turn a language lesion into a false story that the person 'doesn't understand.

2015-125.sentence: Histrionic lability treats the pill, the compliment, and the appointment as proof that someone is still watching. The relationship task is not to feed the flourish or withhold it as punishment, but to notice that the feeling is intense, shallow, and gone the moment the audience leaves.

2015-126.sentence: The calm after 'dumped me' is isolation of affect, a defense that parks the feeling so the story can be told. Confrontation here is not a fight; it is you naming that split so the patient can look at the gap instead of living only in the words.

2015-128.sentence: "Why a 3 and not a 0?" gets the patient to generate his own reasons for change instead of borrowing yours—and a reason he comes up with himself is the one that survives after he leaves your office. Push him toward a 5 or a 10 instead, and you've quietly taken the wheel he's the only one who can actually drive.

2015-129.sentence: This patient already fired one doctor for not taking his dread seriously—so another workup for stomach cancer just repeats that pattern instead of breaking it. The real task is staying with the fear itself, ordinary gurgling and all, until it can be talked about instead of tested away.

2015-131.sentence: Simply asking the patient how the hour felt outperforms almost everything else you can bring to the room—more than technique, more than a precisely accurate transference interpretation, more than matching backgrounds. It works because it makes the patient's own read on the treatment the thing you actually track, instead of assuming you already know.

2015-132.sentence: Split treatment lets everyone pretend the pill and the psychotherapy live in different people, so liability can be sliced 50/50 or limited to the script. The symptom of the arrangement is that dodge; the prescribing psychiatrist still keeps full responsibility for the patient's care.

2015-134.sentence: The vomit is not a random habit; it is the ritual that empties the unbearable fullness so she never has to sit with it. Holding her after the meal until that dysphoria fades is extinction: the escape response is blocked until the urge dies on its own, so abdominal fullness stops predicting a purge.

2015-135.sentence: "I am sorry" with no relief at having survived is the real risk marker here—she hasn't yet let herself feel glad the attempt failed. Inpatient care buys time for that feeling to catch up, so some wish to keep living has a chance to surface before she's alone with the impulse again.

2015-137.sentence: He already knows each click buys a brief lift against loneliness, so this mind can use that insight; you do not need a deep excavation of childhood before you name the loop. Operant conditioning is the technique-level truth: the purchase is positively reinforced, and therapy works by weakening that payoff rather than uncovering a hidden conflict first.

2015-139.sentence: After one choking panic at the table, this teen treats food as a threat and the parents as the people who might shove calories back at them. Specific phobia here is also a bid for a safer base: stay near the family by shrinking the meal, not by saying the eating itself now feels like it could kill them.

2015-141.sentence: Creutzfeldt-Jakob with myoclonus and spongiform microvacuolation of glia and dendrites is not a mind that can use uncovering; the cortex is vanishing week by week. Stay supportive: name the course, protect the family from wild interpretation, and do not hunt for hidden meaning in a brain that is dissolving.

2015-142.sentence: Her ego is already using a bilingual friend as extra reality-testing against a husband who may be the source of the bruises. Start with the professional interpreter and that friend, keep him in the parking lot, and do not ask her limited English or his presence to carry the truth.

2015-143.sentence: Stopping your pretend 911 call is the child using you as a secure base to check: the dollhouse fire is symbol, not catastrophe. That pause marks preoperational into concrete operational—two people can now share that it is play and still stay regulated.

2015-148.sentence: Split treatment tempts you to forget you are half of a pair. Your job is to evaluate and prescribe while keeping regular contact with the therapist; a trial comment is, “If we never talk, we will each treat a different patient.”

2015-150.sentence: Ego strength is whether feeling can be held without flooding or breaking reality. In ataque de nervios the affect spills as shouting, crying, trembling, and rising heat, yet it still maps to an anxiety disorder: impulse and affect overflow, reality testing holds.

2015-152.sentence: Bilateral parotid sialadenosis is the body advertising self-induced vomiting while the interview still says 'I barely eat.' Two people are making that pattern: the patient hides the purge and you, if you blame weight gain or refeeding, join the hide instead of naming the vomit.

2015-153.sentence: Habituation is what you are after: anxiety after the doorknob falls on its own when washing is blocked. Attachment-wise the ritual was a homemade caregiver; you become the secure base that stays nearby so the patient can sit with contamination without fleeing into the sink.

2015-154.sentence: Reactive attachment disorder is the child who will not use you: little smile, no comfort-seeking, unexplained irritability after a string of foster homes. If someone then reaches for a pill as the 'feed' that will make bonding happen, the medicine becomes proof of need rather than a relationship the child still cannot risk.

2015-158.sentence: A Facebook friend request is evacuation: the patient dumps leftover need into your personal page so it does not have to be thought in the room. Containment means you take that raw leftover, turn it into words about the frame, and bring it back next session instead of clicking Accept or Ignore.

2015-163.sentence: Gut-directed hypnosis works when someone can take the raw belly panic of irritable bowel syndrome and hold it long enough for it to become a thought instead of a spasm. That is containing: you metabolize the nameless dread so the bowel does not have to evacuate it as pain and urgency.

2015-165.sentence: A trial comment the day after the crane collapse is that numbness, flash images, and a sleepless night are a human stress reaction, not proof he is breaking. Psychological mindedness starts here: he can use that naming to reach coworkers and family instead of swallowing critical-incident debriefing, a benzo, or early trauma-focused CBT.

2015-166.sentence: Hoarding disorder lives in a broken frame: the home has no usable rooms, neighbors call police, and still the patient holds the limit that every pile is worth keeping if only there were time. You hold the other limit—safety, egress, and that insight without sorting is not treatment.

2015-168.sentence: Graduated vaginal dilators treat genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder by letting her approach the feared sensation in measured doses rather than freeze or flee. That is undoing in the service of mastery: each larger size rewrites the reflex that said penetration equals injury.

2015-169.sentence: Two failed antipsychotics and a patient talking about suicide isn't the moment to reach for a third drug out of habit—that just repeats the pattern that already isn't working. Clozapine is worth the extra monitoring here because it's the one option that can actually interrupt both the psychosis and the despair it's feeding.

2015-170.sentence: Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development is the strip just beyond what the infant can do alone, where a parent’s toy or prompt still makes sense. Stimulation that sits there builds a new capacity; toys dumped below reflex or far above grasp leave development stuck.

2015-173.sentence: Voluntary pizza money is a two-person (really many-person) bargain: each resident can silently let someone else pay. A meeting that includes every club member makes the free-rider problem a shared conversation, which is why that strategy beats a private ask, a single collector, a guilt pitch, or a threat.

2015-175.sentence: TMS lets the patient keep a waking mind while current is applied to cortex, so the treatment does not require the surrender of consciousness that anesthesia for ECT demands. For someone whose depression already feels like a loss of control, that intact awareness is the real advantage: they can accept stimulation without handing the body over to a procedure they cannot watch.

2015-177.sentence: Voices arguing about the patient in the third person are Schneider's first-rank finding: the mind is no longer the sole speaker of the self. Culturally, that is a live third in the room—an alien chorus that comments on him as if he were already an object of public debate rather than a private subject.

2015-180.sentence: The tics are visible, so you can feel recruited into the worried-watcher role, scanning every blink and bark. The school failure is usually ADHD riding along with Tourette, and that quieter inattention is what is actually costing him grades while you are still watching the movements.

2015-185.sentence: First same-sex attraction in early adolescence is the symptom doing the work of naming a desire that was already there. It reassures him that coming out at fifty-five is a late announcement, not a late onset.

2015-186.sentence: Skipping informed consent for depot antipsychotic dumps the decision into the patient as if they had already agreed. Repair is naming autonomy out loud: risks, benefits, and alternatives, instead of leaving the split in the syringe.
