2015-187.sentence: The last usable self is not speech or limbs; it is lid opening and vertical gaze after a basilar occlusion. Goals-of-care talk that skips that channel treats a still-present person as already gone.

2015-189.sentence: Purging is evacuation of something felt as intolerable, and the body keeps the ledger: hypokalemia flattens T waves and raises U waves. The EKG is not a side show; it is the relationship with the bad stuff written on the heart.

2015-190.sentence: Missed social cues in autism are not a child refusing your frame or testing a limit. You hold the assessment differently: you do not interpret inattention as defiance, because the social-cue channel never came online the usual way.

2015-191.sentence: Apathy that cannot organize a clock is not the same as sadness that will not try. If clock drawing fails, a trial comment about their part in the emptiness will bounce; the executive gear for self-observation is what is broken.

2015-192.sentence: Using after a clean screen is acting out: feeling gets discharged as a behavior instead of being named. Contingency management puts the $20 and the three-negative lockout outside the patient so the impulse does not have to be held by will alone.

2015-194.sentence: Right now the part of him that would call for help before acting isn't reliably available—no supports, a pattern of impulsivity, and a specific lethal plan mean he can't yet be trusted to reach for a phone instead of the pills. Inpatient hospitalization holds that safety until he can be counted on to use an outpatient plan instead.

2015-196.sentence: Shared (integrated) care means the pediatrician, psychiatrist, and psychologist stay in one circuit around the child's asthma, ADHD, and oppositional behavior. That circuit is a secure base: the family uses nearby adults to regulate, instead of being bounced between offices like a separation they have to protest.

2015-198.sentence: Erikson's midlife task, ages 40–60, is generativity: feeling useful by protecting the next generation, not integrity-versus-despair. With a 55-year-old who feels useless after the last child leaves, stay supportive and concrete about contribution; this is not a mind asking you to uncover every old wish.

2015-202.sentence: Winnicott’s good-enough parent is attuned enough that the child can feel her own drives, not a perfect mirror and not a Kohut selfobject. Technique follows prognosis: this mother needs support that “snapping once” is ordinary failure, not an uncovering hunt for the moment she “ruined” him.

2015-203.sentence: Malpractice still needs harm: this patient found a new psychiatrist and did well, so the best defense is no appreciably bad outcome, not the signed letter or the 30-day pill bottle. The two of you made a clumsy last session together; the court still asks whether that relational mess injured him.

2015-205.sentence: The clean syringe is a feed, not a demand that he stop wanting heroin. You stay in the relationship by reducing HIV and hepatitis risk first, so the clinic is not experienced as a poison that only loves him if he is abstinent.

2015-210.sentence: The wish is to discharge rage through the wrist; the prohibition is to call it nothing. Confrontation names that collision without interpreting why: the cut was not lethal, and it still says he is not doing well.

2015-211.sentence: The toddler is discovering a body that can generate pleasure, not announcing trauma. Your job is mirroring: you reflect that this is ordinary toddler competence so the parent can keep a sturdy, non-shaming self around the child’s genital curiosity.

2015-212.sentence: Habit reversal asks the child to notice the premonitory urge and swap in a competing response, so you become the coach who names the tic instead of the audience that flinches. Watch the countertransference of wanting to suppress or look away; that urge in you is what the kid already expects from every classroom.

2015-213.sentence: Paranoid personality lives the unremembered injury as if it is happening again in every memo and peer review. What cannot be thought as old betrayal is repeated in the doctor–hospital dyad as certainty that administration is exploiting him.

2015-217.sentence: The first one to three years after arrival is the real limit: the immigrant’s hope of a new life meets a country that will not instantly confer language, work, or belonging. Demoralization there is a time problem, not a character problem—you cannot rush the ego’s adaptation any more than you can rush mourning.

2015-218.sentence: Her wish to taper fast isn't really about the pharmacology—it's guilt, the urge to purge the 'poison' out of her body as fast as possible so she can feel like a good mother again. The actual protective move runs against that urge: staying on the current dose, because withdrawal risks the baby far more than the methadone does.

2015-219.sentence: Cognitive impairment—anterograde and retrograde memory trouble—is what most often stops ECT, because memory is how the self stays continuous. When recall frays, the person feels less like a subject and more like a collection of gaps, so families refuse even when mood would improve.

2015-220.sentence: Topiramate (carbonic anhydrase inhibition, acidosis, stones) recruits you into the ED as the doctor who “should have seen this coming.” Name that countertransference so you treat the hematuria and the missed risk, not just your guilt.

2015-221.sentence: M’Naughten asks only whether, at the moment, he knew the act was wrong—the law’s stand-in for a working conscience, or superego. A combat flashback that wiped that knowledge (and left no memory) is what the defense must show; PTSD, hyperarousal, or a DSM label will not do.

2015-223.sentence: Empathic validation names the affect first—here, humiliation—so the patient feels held rather than analyzed. Avoiding coworkers after the staff meeting is doing protective work: it keeps the shame from being restaged in the hallway before either of you has put words to it.

2015-224.sentence: Separation anxiety and worry that the surviving parent will get sick are age-typical grief in an eight-year-old, not a new attachment diagnosis. The cling is nameless dread looking for a container: a mind that can take in the raw fear and return it as thinkable mourning instead of letting the child evacuate it as panic.

2015-227.sentence: Social anxiety disorder here is fear of scrutiny: the messy signature feels like a public stain, so cash for a car becomes the workaround. What cannot be thought as “just handwriting” gets repeated in the body of daily life—avoid the pen, avoid the audience.

2015-230.sentence: Binge-purge is a drive collision: the wish to take food in meets the prohibition that it must not stay, and the body acts both sides. Fluoxetine is the drug with evidence here; it does not settle the wish versus the rule, but it can quiet the binge-purge enough that the fight is no longer only in the bathroom.

2015-233.sentence: Twenty minutes are already gone, and the remaining hour cannot be spent on martinis, the marital fight, or lateness while forearm cutting is on the table. DBT's hierarchy holds that limit: self-injurious behavior is the first target, and you do not rush past it to work on anything that can wait.

2015-234.sentence: Four weeks at clozapine 200 mg with partial gain and good tolerability is still a trial in progress, not a failed case that needs aripiprazole, divalproex, quetiapine, or depot risperidone. A useful comment to the team is that the urge to add or switch is their impatience, not evidence the patient has used the clozapine trial yet.

2015-239.sentence: Psychoanalytic work is after the part that left without leaving the chair: unconscious conflict kept out of awareness by a split, not just better coping. Other therapies can improve relationships and alliance; this one is specific because it tries to bring that sequestered conflict into the room so it can be known.

2015-240.sentence: Nightly trauma dreams are a two-person problem once she is in treatment: sertraline and therapy hold the day, but the nights still replay the assault. Adding prazosin—an alpha-1 blocker used for PTSD nightmares—is you joining her against nocturnal hyperarousal rather than leaving her to face the flashbacks alone.

2015-241.sentence: Alzheimer disease first shreds the autobiographical memory that lets this person keep a spouse or child inside as a secure base—the inner map of “someone is there.” Once that map fails, language and tool-use go next, so the family becomes the only remaining regulator; the cling and the panic are attachment, not mere “confusion.”

2015-242.sentence: Observed methadone is the good object—the clinic that keeps him alive—while disulfiram is the deliberately bad object that will punish a drink with an acetaldehyde crash. Giving both at the window, with consent, lets one relationship hold craving and consequence instead of splitting them into “kind clinic” versus “kicked-out drunk.”

2015-244.sentence: The family’s hush after his myocardial infarction is the symptom, not a waiting room: silence is how they keep a feared truth (death, blame, who will carry what) out of the air. Naming the inability to talk as one of the family’s problems puts that mute pact on the table instead of filling it with a lecture or deputizing a spokesperson.

2015-245.sentence: The mute, posturing body is dumping terror into the team, who then reach for haloperidol as if they could kill the badness—classic projective identification, the other person is made to feel and act the split-off state. Lorazepam is the repair: it loosens the freeze so concern and speech can return, instead of answering the projection with a neuroleptic that can deepen catatonia.

2015-248.sentence: Impaired prosody means the music of speech is off: stress, pitch, and melody do not carry feeling the way grammar still does. A trial comment lands only if they can hear how you said it; if they cannot, you name the flat or sing-song delivery itself rather than expecting them to infer their part from your tone.

2015-250.sentence: Triangulation parks the bad object—Dad's dangerous drinking—in the 15-year-old so Mother never has to hold both love and complaint in one adult relationship. The boy is asked to be the safe messenger; that splits the couple's conflict across a child instead of keeping good and bad in the marriage.

2015-251.sentence: Urgent-but-not-emergency distress has to have somewhere to go—if your voicemail is silent about that, a patient in crisis may escalate straight to 911 or the ED because those can feel like the only options left. Naming your covering clinician gives them a real middle path, so a bad week doesn't have to become an emergency just because you're unreachable.

2015-253.sentence: A threat of court and commitment is already a technique choice: you have moved from negotiation to force, so this 18-year-old cannot use uncovering or a real yes. Support the frame by naming the legal limit plainly and offering what is still optional (who visits, meds discussion, safety plan) rather than dressing coercion as “voluntary insight.”

2015-256.sentence: “I’ll stay a girl even if I wear blue or cut my hair” is gender constancy: the self-label holds when clothes and hair change. That is a developmental achievement, not an enactment with you; do not treat the insistence as a fight about the clinic’s rules.

2015-257.sentence: Mute, not eating, psychotic depression in a 70-year-old is ego collapse, not a dissociative split you wait out in the chair. ECT is the next step because this mind cannot use words, TMS, VNS, or DBS while starvation and psychosis are running the show.

2015-258.sentence: Rorschach and TAT are for what the patient cannot say on a structured interview: unrepresented, odd linkages leak onto an inkblot as subtle thought disorder. They do not screen cognition, certify developmental level, or cancel uncooperativeness; they catch psychotic process that has no words yet.

2015-260.sentence: Contempt and stonewalling are the divorce already happening in the chairs, not a later outcome. That is an enactment: they live “you are worthless / I am gone” instead of saying the smaller hurt.

2015-261.sentence: He splits the field into the saved and “the devil’s workers,” so mixed, ordinary people cannot exist. Hold schizophreniform: about two months of psychosis is still inside one-to-six months, not a finished schizophrenia story.

2015-262.sentence: A history of violent behavior is the finding that sets the limit, not how hot the 2 a.m. rage feels. You hold the frame: past acts decide dangerousness more than tonight’s anger, the gun at home, or your own fear.

2015-265.sentence: The endometriosis is already named and treated; what cannot be rushed is her capacity to live with leftover pain without converting it into a cancer emergency. Illness anxiety would be fear without the symptom; here the body is loud, and the work is to hold time—hours of research, daily calls—until worry can wait instead of demanding a new treatment tonight.

2015-267.sentence: Bonding is the parent's selfobject need: she wants to feel like a competent, loving mother, and she is measuring that against an imagined instant rush. Attachment is the infant's side; what she needs mirrored is that her tie can grow after the critical-period myth, not that she failed at first sight.

2015-268.sentence: The wish is to erase the crash with a pill—prazosin, propranolol, escitalopram—so nobody has to approach the memory. Trauma-focused CBT is the collision with the prohibition: the child must revisit the story in words, not bury the drive to forget under a first-line medication that pediatric PTSD does not have.

2015-269.sentence: The mentor cannot be remembered as a teacher anymore; dementia repeats the old hierarchy in the body of the admission, and you feel it as discomfort instead of a narrative. Finish urgent care, then transfer: if you stay, the unrepresented dual relationship will be acted in the dyad rather than named and ended.

2015-270.sentence: Social learning is ego at work: she copies mother's clothes because that is the available model, not because hormones or a triangular oedipal plot required it. Dress-up and 'I am a girl' are practice in identifying with a real person, which is ordinary coping with a new gender role at three and a half.

2015-271.sentence: The daughter’s call is not only a risk question; it is proximity-seeking after you put quetiapine 50 mg into her 82-year-old parent—she is using you as a secure base to metabolize the black-box fear. Name the real trade-off in that same attachment language: atypical antipsychotics raise mortality, and you will stay close enough to weigh that harm against the agitation you were asked to contain.

2015-272.sentence: An overvalued idea lives in the marriage, not only in one skull: he keeps assigning adultery to her, and she is now cast as the one who must disprove a charge that he already admits has no evidence. The interpersonal move is the half-open door—he concedes he might be wrong—so the couple stays locked in interrogation instead of grief, jealousy, or a clean delusion that would end the debate.

2015-275.sentence: The scale is undoing: he tries to cancel the pancreatic-cancer identification with his dead parent by proving, ounce by ounce, that he is not wasting away. Avoiding the annual physical is the paired defense—keep the feared confirmation out of the room—so illness anxiety stays a private ritual instead of a diagnosis he would have to hear.

2015-276.sentence: When the family asks you to “declare” Father incompetent, the enactment has already started: they want you to live the takeover with them instead of sending the question to a judge. You assess capacity; a judicial hearing decides competency—stay in that role or you become the extra relative with a prescription pad.

2015-277.sentence: Reciprocal inhibition works on a simple rule: anxiety and pleasure can't fully occupy the mind at the same moment, so deliberately calling up a pleasurable image while standing at the party crowds out some of the space the fear would otherwise take over. She isn't avoiding the anxiety—she's just refusing to let it be the only thing in the room.

2015-279.sentence: Motivational enhancement therapy treats readiness as a limit you do not rush: empathy, discrepancy, no argument, roll with resistance, support self-efficacy. You end the fantasy that confrontation can terminate ambivalence on your timetable; change starts when he can hold the gap between his drinking and his values.

2015-280.sentence: Testing an automatic thought like 'I am worthless' works because it treats the thought as a hypothesis to check against evidence, not a verdict to accept—the same shift a patient makes when a harsh self-judgment stops feeling like fact and starts feeling like one more thing to examine. That's the real engine of cognitive therapy: not comfort, but evidence.

2015-283.sentence: American Indian and Alaska Native suicide rates are not a demographic footnote; they walk in as a cultural third—colonization, poverty, and intergenerational loss sitting between you and this patient. Use that knowledge to widen the safety plan (kin, tribe, IHS, elders), not to flatten the person into a category.

2015-285.sentence: The child's ego learned to hold fear with a small dog in a quiet room; that is a narrow window of affect tolerance, not a cured phobia. A large dog at a birthday party is a new context and a bigger stimulus, so renewal of clinically significant fear is expected until exposure is practiced more broadly.

2015-289.sentence: Depersonalization is the psyche’s way of getting out of a body that still holds what cannot be remembered as a story. The person does not recall the trauma; they watch themselves from the hallway so the unrepresented state never has to arrive as “I was there.”

2015-291.sentence: The bilateral sixth-nerve palsies and that CSF (protein 223, glucose 25, mixed cells) are Mycobacterium tuberculosis announcing itself in a man whose drinking has already thinned his body’s defenses. The syndrome is doing the work his history would not: forcing a stop, a hospital, and a name for years of self-erasure.

2015-292.sentence: The cake binge isn't hunger — it's what happens when the restriction cracks faster than she can put words to what's building, so it gets acted out through her body instead of felt or named. The hours of exercise afterward aren't really about calories; they're an attempt to punish that loss of control back into order, which is why the cycle repeats instead of resolving anything.

2015-294.sentence: Tetrabenazine depletes vesicular dopamine (VMAT2) when guanfacine and antipsychotics have already failed, and the family will recruit you as the last adult who can finally stop the tics. Notice the countertransference pull to become the magic fixer; prescribe the drug, but do not become the tic-suppressing parent they are handing you.

2015-296.sentence: A 16-year-old on probation still needs a parental coalition that can hold one set of expectations; that developmental capacity lives in the parents first, not in a more “egalitarian” family meeting. Structural work is the late arrival of hierarchy: both parents define rules they can actually back, so the adolescent is not left to organize himself around two competing grown-ups.

2015-297.sentence: Point tenderness at T5 plus a nipple-level sensory cut and new incontinence is spinal epidural abscess until proven otherwise—do not let a heroin history become a sanctioned gap in urgency. The team’s conscience fails here when “this is just withdrawal” or “they did this to themselves” delays the scan; that is a moral loophole, not a neurologic differential.

2015-298.sentence: Frequent hospitalizations after adequate antipsychotic trials are an evacuation: the unthinkable chaos of missed meds and lost follow-up gets dumped into the ED instead of being held. Assertive community treatment is the container that goes to the patient, so the raw disorganization can be metabolized in the community rather than only in a hospital bed.

2015-300.sentence: Two attendings deadlocked over depression versus delirium freeze the clock; residents and nurses will not speak while the hierarchy still pretends it does not need them. Leaders have to say, out loud, that they need help and value other opinions—otherwise the conflict never becomes thinkable and the workup of delirium stays stalled.

2016-1.sentence: The steep-road detour is already a private rule about what they will not enter, and the clinic should not quietly adopt that same detour by treating every panic as an emergency to be routed around. Keep the hour pointed at that one avoided stretch so the fear stays locatable instead of turning the frame into endless accommodation.

2016-2.sentence: Those inner figures of self and other are what get parked on staff when the patient flips from idealizing to devaluing. The flip is a change of which mental representation is on stage, not a random mood.

2016-3.sentence: The cousin's Mexico trip is a defense: they leave your mania questions by sliding onto someone else's story and never return. Tangentiality here is not only a thought-form; it keeps their own impulsivity off the table.

2016-5.sentence: Using a banana as a phone is a small competence win: the child can make the world fit an inner picture and feel effective. Symbolic play is the self practicing “I can make meaning” without needing the object to already be the thing.

2016-8.sentence: A three-year-old’s sense of herself as female is not a solo milestone; it is named, mirrored, and used between her and the people who dress, bathe, and talk about her. Tying laces or copying a square can wait; this identity is already a two-person fact in the room.

2016-9.sentence: In a school-age child with tics, major depression is the comorbidity that is still uncommon; ADHD, OCD-spectrum worry, and learning trouble are the ones that usually ride along. Do not dig for a hidden depressive narrative the child’s mind has not yet organized; screen those neighbors and stay supportive until adolescence, when mood disorders actually catch up.

2016-12.sentence: Pramipexole, the D3-preferring agonist, can dump an unrepresented urge into the room as compulsive gambling the Parkinson patient does not experience as a remembered wish. The spouse is left living the wreckage in the bank account; treat the drug, not a sudden character flaw.

2016-13.sentence: An interpersonal psychodynamic group lives on ordinary transference: people try you on as parent, rival, or longed-for friend and then talk about it. Antisocial personality disorder tends to recruit you and the other members into exploitation or legal-risk suspicion instead, so the room becomes a hunt rather than a place to notice who you are being asked to become.

2016-15.sentence: The old medical wish is to lead, diagnose, and decide; recovery principles put a prohibition on that grab for control. Collaborating in partnership with consumers to support their goals is how you hold the collision: you keep your expertise without discharging the wish to be the one who knows.

2016-16.sentence: A suicidal crisis does not wait for insight, media guidelines, or a school screen to ripen. Restricting access to lethal methods is the limit you can actually hold: you buy time when the capacity to stay alive cannot be rushed.

2016-17.sentence: Wanting to end things the moment a relationship starts costing her something is exactly the test Erikson called intimacy versus isolation — can she stay fused to someone else's life change without dissolving, or does cutting the tie feel safer than that risk. The move itself isn't the real crisis; whether she can stay coupled through it is.

2016-19.sentence: Case management's real win in addiction treatment is retention — simply keeping someone in the room long enough that they might eventually recognize their own part in things. Chase reduced use or lower HIV rates as the proof of success instead, and you'll call the intervention a failure long before that slower work of just staying engaged has had time to matter.

2016-22.sentence: A patient punching or shouting in their sleep can look like buried rage finally breaking through, but in REM sleep behavior disorder it's the opposite of meaning — the muscle atonia that's supposed to lock the body out of the dream has failed, so the dream gets acted instead of just dreamed. Treat it as a neurologic warning sign, often years ahead of Parkinsonism, not a window into what the patient secretly wants.

2016-23.sentence: “Worst headache of my life” recruits you as the doctor who must not miss the bleed, and a normal CT tempts a countertransference of premature reassurance. Lumbar puncture is staying in that role: you look for xanthochromia instead of becoming the person who waves the danger away.

2016-24.sentence: When reality testing is thin and splitting is still how good and bad get sorted, uncovering therapy asks for an integration the ego can't yet manage — it will just flood the patient instead of helping them. Supportive therapy is the holding environment instead: you lend structure and impulse control from outside until the relationship can stay in one piece on its own.

2016-27.sentence: At forty-three the Erikson task is generativity: staying reliably present without a heroic new consult. Regular visits with an actual exam give a holding schedule so the lump, bloating, and chest pain do not have to escalate to keep the doctor from leaving.

2016-28.sentence: DSM names cannot be dropped into a rural clinic and expected to finish the work; local culture sets a hard limit on how far those labels travel. You do not end the idiom—“thinking too much,” spirits—by replacing it with a faster Western diagnosis.

2016-31.sentence: A hypersensitive infant has thin affect tolerance: ordinary sound and touch hit like threat, so startle and crying are the only available regulators. That is not “being difficult”; it is a nervous system that cannot yet hold stimulation long enough to settle, so the adult’s job is to shrink the world until the baby can use it.

2016-34.sentence: It's tempting to read new rigidity in a patient over 70 as decline or a personality change rather than a drug effect — but the same antipsychotic dose that was fine at 40 is already a heavy dopamine-receptor occupancy in an aging brain with less receptor reserve to spare. Ask what changed in the med list before you ask what changed in the person.

2016-36.sentence: Dissociative identity disorder asks you to hold the frame for more than one occupant: travel amnesia, lost job skills, childhood gaps, out-of-body watching, sudden feeling, and a child’s voice are switches, not “poor memory.” Confidentiality and time still belong to one treatment; you do not let an alter, or your curiosity, rewrite who consented or how long the hour lasts.

2016-37.sentence: The urine-tampering already answers the insight question: they can plan and hide the production of illness, so they are not lost in a delusion. A trial comment is something like, “Part of you needs to be a patient here,” because factitious disorder is intentional falsification of medical or psychological signs without the obvious payout that would make it malingering.

2016-38.sentence: Fear of becoming his father arrived before any dementia did, so the adult capacity you are counting on is still intact: he can use foresight instead of waiting for damage. Primary prevention is that move—tighten blood pressure, diabetes, and lipids now, while cognition is still normal, rather than screening for early disease or rehabbing a stroke that has not happened.

2016-39.sentence: Those headaches, dizziness, and gut symptoms may be carrying the migration story he cannot yet put into a Western word like depression. “What do you think is causing your symptoms?” lets the symptom keep its meaning—neurasthenia, family strain, shame about work—before you translate it into a DSM checklist.

2016-44.sentence: IPT opens on the quality of social connections because withdrawal after a role transition is often the working defense: isolation keeps the grief from being shared and therefore from being felt. You map who is still in the room with the patient so that defense has less cover, not so you can interpret childhood or the unconscious.

2016-47.sentence: Chronotherapy for circadian rhythm sleep disorder is a prescribed clock, and the delayed-phase student often treats that clock as a demand to defy or a feed that finally organizes the day. You are not handing a hypnotic; you are asking them to take in an outside rhythm—light and wake time—as something that can set them rather than as poison.

2016-49.sentence: Mood reactivity is a two-person sign: the low mood is not sealed inside her; another person’s warmth can still lift it. Lead-limb hypersomnia and binge-weight gain sit next to that interpersonal brightness, so the depression is organized around contact and rejection, not a one-person vegetative lock.

2016-50.sentence: She needs you as a mirroring other who can still see her as a patient, not as a damages calculator. The ethical limit is clinical presentation only—impairment ratings, causation, and dollar disability would collapse that selfobject function into a courtroom verdict on her worth.

2016-53.sentence: “What brought you to the hospital today?” is a container: you hold the unshaped mess long enough for it to become a sentence. Closed questions evacuate the dread into yes/no pellets; this open-ended prompt asks the patient to think the arrival instead of dump it.

2016-59.sentence: Clouded sensorium is the ED’s way of saying the medical process is already in the room with you, not waiting for labs. Calling it “psych” while attention waxes and wanes is the enactment: the system repeats the split between mind and body instead of treating the delirium in front of you.

2016-62.sentence: Socratic questioning is a mirroring move: you treat her as someone who can think, not as someone who needs your reassurance. An automatic thought like “I bombed it, so I’m worthless” loses its grip when she finds the hole in it herself, and that finding is a self-esteem event.

2016-63.sentence: The false-belief marble test is a container in miniature: the child has to hold the doll’s wrong idea as a thought, not as the actual marble. Fail that, and the other person’s mind is not a mind—it is just the world, unmetabolized.

2016-67.sentence: Recent heavy drinking is not just a risk factor on a list; alcohol is already in the relationship as feed and poison at once, numbing the body while thinning the ego’s shock absorbers. When the crash comes, that same bottle has already taught the mind that safety lives outside the self, so the trauma sticks instead of being metabolized.

2016-69.sentence: Early first intercourse that then tracks with more partners is not only epidemiology; it can be a paranoid-schizoid solution, using bodies to evacuate anxiety instead of holding one person with mixed feelings. The developmental task is depressive concern: staying with one relationship long enough to care what it costs the other person.

2016-71.sentence: Graded task assignments treat the garage as a developmental load the ego cannot yet carry whole, so you lend the missing capacity in small, sequenced pieces. You are not cheerleading motivation; you are building the child’s-eye skill of starting when the whole job still feels like too much mother to take in at once.

2016-74.sentence: Social anxiety here is a mirroring wound: the stutter already taught the self that other eyes will not reflect competence, so the promotion and the restaurant feel like public proof of being inept. The solid marriage shows the need is not for a holding partner but for an audience that can still admire skill.

2016-78.sentence: Hoarding most often rides with major depression, so the pile is not a solo ritual but a two-person bargain: keep the stuff and we never have to face the deadness between us. The distress at discarding is interpersonal—someone would have to stay present while the object, and the mood, leave.

2016-83.sentence: Rationalization is a story that makes embezzling sound like bookkeeping: the company still profits, so nothing was taken. Insight starts when they can hear that sentence as a cover, not as an audit.

2016-86.sentence: Step one—admitting powerlessness over the addiction—is not piety; it is saying out loud a state that has lived only as using, blackout, and the body repeating what cannot yet be remembered as a story. Until that unrepresented helplessness is spoken, the twelve-step program has nothing to work on but another enactment of control.

2016-87.sentence: Care managers win in primary-care depression because they sit in the collision between the wish to be well and the prohibition against needing more than a ten-minute visit. Guidelines and CME stay on the shelf; a person who calls, tracks PHQ-9s, and pulls the patient back is the compromise formation that actually treats.

2016-89.sentence: Winnicott’s mirroring is the parent’s face giving the infant their own feeling back, so a self can begin to exist as something seen rather than only raw affect. Holding keeps the body safe; mirroring is the developmental move that arrives when the parent is attuned most of the time and shows it.

2016-90.sentence: Mental health court increasing engagement in community treatment is the system stepping out of the usual jail-and-drop enactment: the two-person repetition of “you’re dangerous / you’re abandoned.” Diversion names the illness in a courtroom so the defendant and the clinic can stay in a treatment relationship instead of another booking.

2016-91.sentence: Wanting the psychiatrist parked in the clinic is a kind of denial: it treats proximity as if it were the treatment, so nobody has to feel how much care actually falls through the cracks. Collaborative care works when a non-physician care manager holds that anxiety and coordinates the work, instead of pretending co-location undoes the split.

2016-92.sentence: A tic shows leftover ego strength: the patient can briefly suppress the jerk, which is impulse control, then the urge wins and relief follows. That premonitory urge-and-relief loop is not myoclonus (no warning) and not a compulsion (no feared thought the ego is bargaining with).

2016-94.sentence: Split treatment is a two-person pattern: psychiatrist and unaffiliated therapist each quietly assign the other the job of knowing how suicidal the patient is. After the job loss, that unsaid bargain is an enactment—living the disconnect instead of sharing the condition—and the law treats both as having a duty to know.

2016-95.sentence: After TBI, the tablet is not a gadget so much as a borrowed secure base: an external mind that holds appointments when the injured one cannot. Monthly sessions are proximity on purpose—the therapist stays close while the patient learns to use that object to self-regulate, which is cognitive rehabilitation, not cheerleading.

2016-100.sentence: Organizational culture theory says the unit runs on shared meaning and 'how we do things here,' not on the seclusion protocol you posted. A trial comment to staff—'we treat the policy as the outsider and protect the old ritual'—tests whether they can see their own part instead of only blaming the written rule.

2016-102.sentence: An advance directive is the frame written while the 60-year-old with early bipolar-related cognitive change is still lucid: who speaks, and what care is refused, when mania or incapacity arrives. Guardianship, conservatorship, guardian ad litem, and a representative payee are later substitutions by the court or the system; they are not the patient's own prior consent.

2016-103.sentence: Telephone consultation is part of the DBT frame, not a favor you grant when you feel generous. You hold the limit by teaching skills in the crisis call instead of becoming the after-hours soother.

2016-105.sentence: Frotteurism is touching or rubbing a nonconsenting person for sexual arousal; here the “exam” is the cover for the act. A wish for genital contact collides with the prohibition of the professional role, so the contact is staged as an accident of knees and a stool.

2016-106.sentence: Financial stress is a real risk factor for child abuse, not a moral footnote. When money panic cannot be contained—held long enough to become thinkable—it can be evacuated into the child as hitting, screaming, or neglect.

2016-107.sentence: School age is industry versus inferiority: the self wants a mirror that says “you can do this,” not a pep talk about identity. When competence is not recognized, irritability and school refusal are often the self collapsing, not a primary mood disorder.

2016-109.sentence: A personal feed is not a secure base; it is your private life, and the patient cannot use it to regulate without collapsing you into a friend. A separate professional account keeps proximity available (hours, policies, psychoeducation) without inviting them into your vacation photos, which is the attachment version of a locked office door.

2016-111.sentence: Calling later-life desire 'over anyway' is often suppression: the person knows the wish is still there and parks it to avoid shame or a limp erection. A majority of middle-aged and older adults stay sexually active, so the work is naming the wish instead of using age as a polite gag.

2016-120.sentence: Adolescence is the phase that packages idealism with a sense of invulnerability, which is why a 16-year-old can floor it drunk and mean it when they say nothing bad would happen. Drive conflict is the collision: the wish to feel omnipotent and unbound runs into a still-thin prohibition against death, so the risky act is the compromise, not a random lapse in judgment.

2016-121.sentence: When a postpartum woman cannot remember or think the terror of harming the infant, the unrepresented state shows up as a poison delusion and a demand to leave—the body and the dyad act it instead of naming it. That is why you treat this as an infanticide emergency: the baby is already inside the unthinkable scene, not a metaphor you can interpret from the doorway.

2016-122.sentence: She is recruiting you as the doctor who will not add another pill—watch the countertransference wish to be the kind, non-pharma one who hands her an “natural” out. You can still name SAMe honestly: it has some evidence in depression, and your job is not to become either the withholding MD or the supplement pal.

2016-123.sentence: The APA rule is a hard superego: no sexual relationship with current or former patients, period—not after discharge, not after “consent,” not after a clean termination. The flirtatious text is the moment conscience either holds or invents a sanctioned gap (“treatment is over, so it is private life”).

2016-127.sentence: Slower visual processing in this healthy 75-year-old is a real limit, not a moral failing, and the adult child's push to take the keys can land as a collapse of the parent's competence, the feeling of being able and seen as able. Name the aging fact first so you can still offer a mirroring response: you see the parent's wish to stay a capable driver, and you also see the accidents.

2016-132.sentence: Same-sex groupings regardless of activity are the dominant playground pattern in third and fourth grade, so a 9-year-old who only plays with boys is often developmentally on script. A trial comment that invites insight: I wonder if the worry is more about our wish for mixed-sex ease than about what his mind can actually do with peers right now.

2016-133.sentence: The frame of hospice is not only morphine and a new bed; it is a planned rupture of the old holding environment—home, spouse, the chair by the window. Name the feared loss of the loved ones, or the consult becomes a polite discussion of pain while the real goodbye stays unspoken.

2016-135.sentence: She is not hiding the grief; she is using suppression—she keeps the tears in the room and still thinks about adoption. That is the defense of a phase-of-life problem: the wish stays conscious, so you do not need to diagnose a disorder to make the sadness legitimate.

2016-141.sentence: When he can say the nausea is from the drug and he wants out, that is usable insight: he sees his body and his wish as his own, not only his wife's. A trial comment is to treat that statement as competent dissent—proxy consent started the trial; his present mind ends it.

2016-142.sentence: Binge-purge anorexia leans on acting out: the impulse is discharged into a binge, a purge, or a weekend stimulant rather than held as a feeling. Substance use rides the same discharge channel; restriction more often uses denial and control, while this subtype uses the body and the bottle to evacuate the conflict.

2016-143.sentence: She wants you as the couples pill: the same good object who already feeds her individual work, now prescribed to the marriage. Impartiality is the dose limit—if you swallow that request you become her proof, not a third who can hear both of them.

2016-144.sentence: A year of shoplifting, sugar cravings, and hoarding easily reads as a personality gone bad, but this is frontotemporal dementia taking away the inhibition that used to hold those impulses in check — it's the same person, minus the brakes. SPECT can show the frontal hypoperfusion behind that loss of restraint, which is why you image before you moralize.

2016-145.sentence: The psychoeducation hour can become an enactment: you and the room are already living a medicalizing script instead of talking about fear of the person. Naming mental illness a brain disease does not buy more tolerant attitudes; it can keep the public one step further from relationship.

2016-146.sentence: Jail is forced separation from every usual attachment figure, so suicide is the protest when there is no secure base left. Federal courts therefore require a suicide prevention program as the institution's duty of proximity, not optional counseling or a forensic specialist on staff.

2016-149.sentence: In the prison clinic the pair is never only two people; the institution is in the room with you. Imminent plans to escape or create disorder break confidentiality here in a way HIV status, inmate threats, and old crime details do not.

2016-150.sentence: In DBT the cutting, rage, or crisis call is treated as a behavior that already has a job, not as a riddle to interpret. The therapist uses contingencies and skills to replace that job, rather than holding the feeling until its meaning arrives.

2016-151.sentence: This sits on Erikson's initiative-versus-guilt years: a four-and-a-half-year-old is supposed to invent a world, not yet police it. The dinner-table monkey is practice at taking the lead in play; worry more if the child cannot leave the companion when reality needs them.

2016-152.sentence: In group CBT the pain is allowed to stay real; the work is to stop organizing a whole life around waiting for it to vanish. Functioning despite pain means the symptom can be a fact without remaining the only story the person is allowed to tell.

2016-155.sentence: A just-turned-two-year-old who can kick a ball is using what this mind can actually do; asking for a copied circle or a tricycle is asking for a later ego. Support the parent with that milestone instead of interpreting delay they have not shown.

2016-156.sentence: The long recap of who broke the rules is school-age ego strength: the child is using story and the rulebook to bind impulse instead of hitting. Latency lives on that identification with the grown-up order; it is coping, not just tattling.

2016-157.sentence: Asking what they think is causing the pain invites them to use you as a secure base: a person they can stay near while they put a private theory into words. Homesickness and “what are you hiding” close that distance; the explanatory-model question keeps attachment available for regulation instead of turning the visit into a test of loyalty to the workup.

2016-158.sentence: Mild intellectual disability hits later-emerging social cognition harder than color names or a practiced bedtime script, so peer cues fail first. Treat that as a developmental mismatch, not willfulness: the child can do the household routine and still miss the glance that says “we’re joking now.”

2016-162.sentence: Localized amnesia—blanking a whole stretch of time, not a category of facts or one’s entire autobiography—is the usual bargain after trauma: the relationship-event is gone, the rest of the self stays. Reconstruct that interval with another person at a tolerable pace; forcing the missing hours recreates the original overrun.

2016-164.sentence: In a job-loss flood you lend ego strength: affect tolerance and a bit of structure so the patient can stand the hour without more uncovering. Supportive therapy is that loan; psychoanalysis and IPT wait until impulse control and reality testing can hold the work.

2016-167.sentence: The gait–incontinence–cognition triad tempts denial: call it Alzheimer and stop looking. Enlarged ventricles name NPH, a shunt-possible hydrocephalus, so the defense to name is premature foreclosure, not more cortical-atrophy storytelling.

2016-168.sentence: It's easy for a team to quietly treat a dementia diagnosis as proof of incompetence, repeating that assumption in the chart instead of actually testing capacity for the decision at hand. The law does the opposite — it presumes competence until a court says otherwise, so your job is to evaluate this specific decision, not rubber-stamp the team's shortcut.

2016-174.sentence: Illness anxiety lives in the idea of disease, not in a felt symptom; after the acquaintance’s death the tumor cannot be remembered as someone else’s story, so it is repeated as hours of searching and a demand for PET. The unrepresented loss shows up in the dyad as “prove I am not dying,” while the body stays neurologically quiet.

2016-175.sentence: Multisystemic therapy puts helpers in the home and neighborhood so the teenager’s delinquent wish—to rule, steal, or blow up—meets a live prohibition that is not another locked ward. The conflict stays in the family and street where it is already being lived, instead of being evacuated into a hospital that only repeats the same fight.

2016-177.sentence: The sandwich generation—teen applying to college and a father with new dementia—dumps two raw claims into one mind before they can be thought. If nobody helps him hold both, the insomnia is nameless dread leaking out as nights that will not metabolize the stretch.

2016-178.sentence: Extinction means you withdraw the attention that was the stimulus, so the scream-to-get-staff-over response weakens—not punish, not reinforce by rushing in. Attachment-wise, the patient is using proximity as regulation; if you vanish the rush without a plan, expect protest before the scream dies down.

2016-182.sentence: Death from abuse peaks from birth to three years because the pair is not two people yet: the infant cannot protest, flee, or recruit a third, so the caregiver's rage has nowhere to go but the body. The changing story in the PICU is the relationship still being written by one person; your job is to stop that two-person script from finishing.

2016-183.sentence: Little Hans's horse phobia is attachment work in costume: the boy keeps the father close by fearing a stand-in he can avoid, so he never has to lose the real secure base. The symptom is a clumsy proximity strategy, not a random animal fear; he regulates distance to dad by putting the danger on the street.

2016-184.sentence: Kin selection says the childless aunt is not failing to reproduce; she is feeding her own genes through nieces and nephews, so the devotion is an investment, not a leftover life. The meaning of the altruism is inclusive fitness: her care is the family line's way of staying alive when she has no child of her own.

2016-187.sentence: Shaping is why you don't demand the whole behavior at once — you reward each small approximation toward it, like praising a child for just tolerating the toothbrush near her lips before she'll ever accept the full routine, so the skill grows without ever being demanded whole.

2016-188.sentence: The family's panic after dense retrograde amnesia is a raw evacuation: they want the ECT out of the room so they do not have to think. You contain that dread—hold it long enough to make it thinkable—and then space the treatments farther apart so memory can recover without abandoning an effective course.

2016-191.sentence: Finding the ball under the blanket is the same trick that later lets a baby tolerate you leaving the room — object permanence is the cognitive floor underneath secure attachment, the proof that 'gone' can still mean 'exists, just hidden.'

2016-192.sentence: Gender-affirming surgery often relieves dysphoria and suicidality, but it isn't a cure-all — general health problems rise afterward, so real psychological relief shouldn't be a reason to stop watching the body too.

2016-194.sentence: Salivating to the smell of dinner is an unconditioned response: the body already knew how to drool before anyone paired a bell with food. The junior resident needs that distinction so exposure is not sold as inventing a new reflex, only as teaching the learned CS–CR pair to fade.

2016-198.sentence: The developmental task of midlife isn't a new resume or reinvented intimacy — it's letting yourself actually feel that your time is finite and death is real, and then deciding what's worth doing with what's left.

2016-202.sentence: Self-help groups set goals that ignore intragroup dynamics, so they stay supportive: same problem, shared hope, no excavation of how members use one another. Your process group can uncover those uses; AA-style meetings cannot, and promising personality change there overloads a mind that only asked for a room of peers.

2016-206.sentence: Fear of abandonment in borderline personality disorder is often a vertical split: one self stays in the chair while another self already lives in the empty room after you leave. The frantic clinging is not only neediness; it is an attempt to keep both selves in the same body when the bond feels about to vanish.

2016-207.sentence: A year of outbursts despite real outpatient work means this patient’s ego cannot yet hold affect, impulses, and daily change in an unstructured week. Partial hospitalization adds scaffolding—hours of structure without a locked unit—so affect tolerance can grow before you ask the self to manage it alone again.

2016-208.sentence: Patients register attunement by whether your eyes seem to meet theirs, not by whether you're actually looking at their face somewhere else on the screen — so parking the webcam next to their image closes that small, felt gap in presence.

2016-212.sentence: Pramipexole works for restless legs by topping up dopamine tone, but that same boost can quietly unlock impulse-control problems — new gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive spending — so ask about those at follow-up, not just about the crawling legs.

2016-215.sentence: A perceived sense of community works against isolation, the defense of sitting in the room without belonging. When members feel a we, they stop treating leadership as someone else's job and identify with the group instead of waiting to be empowered from above.

2016-218.sentence: An MMSE of 21/30 is mild cognitive impairment, not “normal aging,” and that number only arrives because a daughter who lives with her father could not keep carrying the forgetting alone. The score is a two-person event: her protest makes the deficit visible before you recode it as ordinary old age.

2016-223.sentence: Unresponsive caregiving is doing the real work here: the infant learns that protest will not bring a mind, so insecure attachment becomes the cheapest way to stay near a caregiver who does not answer. Poor-quality daycare only bites when that home pattern is already in place; the extra hours are not the meaning of the insecurity.

2016-225.sentence: Clozapine's edge with comorbid addiction fits the self-medication hypothesis — patients often lean on cannabis and alcohol to blunt psychotic terror and emptiness that other antipsychotics don't touch, so when clozapine actually quiets that suffering, the need for the substance drops with it.

2016-226.sentence: Kant’s gift is not a therapy technique but the ethics that decide how much uncovering you are allowed to do: treat the person as an end, not a means to your formulation. Autonomy and duty set the ceiling on interpretation; you do not strip defenses just because the history of psychiatry is interesting.

2016-232.sentence: In school-age kids, self-regulation—managing affect, attention, and impulse—tracks competent social life better than athletics, looks, or SES. That is attachment work on the playground: the child who can use an inner brake (and later a grown-up as a secure base) can stay near peers without exploding or vanishing.

2016-234.sentence: In mania, the bright clothes aren't incidental — grandiosity and disinhibited energy show up on the body before the patient even opens her mouth, which is why appearance and mood, not retardation or poverty of thought, are what point you to the diagnosis.

2016-235.sentence: Ordinary grief and a wife's felt 'presence' aren't pathology — but depressive symptoms that show up early, right after the loss, are what actually predict impairment, so the skill is telling normal longing from a superimposed depression instead of managing either one reflexively.

2016-238.sentence: Erikson’s integrity-versus-despair task at 75 is finding meaning in what he has done, not inventing new hobbies or saving the world. He is recruiting you as the last witness who will either confirm the life added up or sit in the despair with him—watch the countertransference urge to cheerlead or close the chart.

2016-239.sentence: Neglect is the most prevalent maltreatment, and the team’s hunger for bruises or a sexual-abuse story is a sanctioned gap: conscience lights up for commission and goes quiet for omission. Your job is to keep the superego honest—failure to feed and supervise this 6-year-old is already the crime, even when the exam is “only” malnutrition and no one is holding a stick.

2016-241.sentence: Velocardiofacial syndrome means this baseline psychosis isn't new — it's part of the same genetic story as the heart defect and cleft palate his whole life, so before starting an antipsychotic, find out whether the family will hear it as finally getting help or as one more intervention on a body that's already been through enough.

2016-242.sentence: The ventromedial hypothalamus is the satiety brake; a craniopharyngioma can cut it, and bingeing plus sixty pounds in four months is the body without an ending. You cannot interpret that hunger into stopping, and you cannot rush a limit that tissue no longer supplies.

2016-249.sentence: In dementia, aggression is often the last available language for pain that can no longer be put into words — so before restraints, imaging, or a PRN benzo, do the pain assessment and let the real complaint get heard instead of just managed.

2016-250.sentence: Wariness at first contact is often a boundary, not a delusion, and you cannot rush trust across a cultural gap. Say that doctors and patients of different backgrounds sometimes misunderstand each other and ask if he has been concerned about that, rather than labeling him paranoid or hunting for strange beliefs.

2016-252.sentence: Cutting smoking in half after three months isn't a broken promise to correct — praise the real progress, because shame in the room is more likely to end the work than to speed it up.

2016-253.sentence: Teenagers don't organize their choices around a heart attack forty years away — they organize around how they look right now, so a warning about bad breath and yellowing teeth lands because it threatens the self-image they actually care about this week.

2016-254.sentence: Impairment often lives as an unrepresented state: what the physician cannot remember or say is repeated in late notes, missed pages, and a ward that starts covering. The administrative psychiatrist is not bound by the usual parameters of confidentiality because the institution has to put words to what the body and the schedule have already been acting out.

2016-256.sentence: One cooked meal a week is a small competence experience: she gets to feel effective in her own kitchen instead of waiting for a mirrored “you’re ready” that never quite arrives. Behavioral activation here is self-psychological, not just a schedule—it rebuilds esteem through a doable act after symptoms are gone and the self still feels too thin for the “real world.”

2016-257.sentence: An illusion is a wish and a fear colliding on a real stimulus: the IV pole is actually there, and the mind conscripts it into a person at the bedside. Name the finding—misinterpretation of genuine sensory input—so you do not confuse this drive-laden rewrite of the room with a hallucination born of no object at all.

2016-258.sentence: School-based care works because it puts a clinician where the adolescent already is, so help does not require a separate trip that feels like abandonment of the only secure base they have—school itself. The advantage is improved access for youth who otherwise never arrive: proximity is the treatment, not a nicer office across town.

2016-260.sentence: The failure here isn't a lack of trying — the once-automatic motor sequence for dressing is gone, so encouragement or physically walking him through it can't fix what praxis, not motivation, has lost.

2016-261.sentence: Saying "Because girls don't have wee wees" is containment: you take the boy's raw astonishment and hand it back as a thinkable fact. Delay or scolding evacuates the question and leaves him with nameless dread about bodies instead of a name.

2016-262.sentence: Countertransference here is a limit on a new hour: your old sister-feelings arrive before the alliance has time to exist. You cannot rush them out; you name them privately so you do not live the old relationship instead of ending that impulse in the chair.

2016-268.sentence: The live third in the room is not diagnosis or the drug pamphlet; it is the court and the hospital’s power to hold or release him. Bargain-discharge for swallowing the antipsychotic strips voluntariness, the consent element that was missing, and turns “informed choice” into a class-and-custody deal.

2016-271.sentence: Deployment is a third party in the family: the military’s schedule, not the child’s wishes, decides who is home. That institutional absence is why anxiety symptoms rise in the kids during the tour and stay up after reunion, not only on the day dad leaves.

2016-273.sentence: He wants you as an exclusive good object who hides him; the officers want you as their informant. HIPAA lets you tell them he is ready for discharge without his consent, so you have to hold both the patient’s trust and the legal demand in one relationship instead of splitting them.

2016-274.sentence: He is recruiting you as the one adult who already understands the campus world, so the farm family can stay the ones who will not. Name it acculturation difficulty: two cultures are arguing inside him, and your warmth can become a stand-in for leaving home rather than a place to think about telling them.

2016-277.sentence: The so-called panic is doing a job: it yanks her home before delay can mean her dying mother is gone. Separation anxiety here is not random fear of crowds; it is a last-ditch way to stay glued to the only person she has ever leaned on.

2016-280.sentence: Dendritic spines are the little handshake between two neurons: they change number and shape when two sides of a synapse keep meeting. Therapy and antidepressants work there because the relationship, not a lone cell body, is what remolds the contact.

2016-282.sentence: ICU “psychosis” is usually delirium: the ego’s reality testing and sleep–wake scaffolding have collapsed under medical insult. Agitation and ceiling-tile spies are not new schizophrenia; they are what a mind does when it can no longer hold a coherent day.

2016-284.sentence: The fire-setting is already an enactment in the room: he is inviting you to chase, contain, or get scorched instead of naming the rising tension. Pyromania is the diagnosis because the excitement-then-relief cycle around fire is the point, not the stolen hardware or the broken curfew.

2016-285.sentence: Your report can split the defendant into mad versus bad and feel as if you have left the witness chair for the verdict. Insanity stays a finding by the jury: you describe mind, they decide whether he lacked the required state of mind.

2016-286.sentence: Before you push a depressed new mother back toward friends, map who actually functions as her secure base. The initial phase of IPT is collecting information about significant relationships so you know whom she uses to regulate, not yet reconnecting or rewriting expectations.

2016-289.sentence: The referral for “seizures” recruits you to become the epilepsy doctor, and the few bilateral jerks after collapse can hook that countertransference—your urge to treat a spell as a complex partial seizure. Stay with the collar, pallor, and faintness: carotid sinus syncope is mechanical hypersensitivity, not a performance you have to interpret as conversion.

2016-290.sentence: Retirement stirs a wish to stay mentally potent and a prohibition against becoming the sedentary man who “doesn’t bother”—so the news story arrives as both hope and self-reproach. Name that collision and still give the evidence: late-life physical activity, even newly adopted, is more likely than not to aid cognition.

2016-292.sentence: The friend’s omega-3 tip is an evacuation: raw dread of becoming the sibling with Alzheimer disease is handed to you as a pill request so no one has to think it. Contain that—hold the feeling until it is thinkable—and say the studies do not show omega-3s prevent cognitive decline, even if they may have other benefits.

2016-293.sentence: Kohut’s self psychology is the school that says a child’s sense of worth is built from parental empathy—mirroring that says “I see you,” plus room to idealize and feel competent. Without that, the self stays hungry for admiration and shatters at a slight; that is a selfobject need, not merely a defense.

2016-294.sentence: Fewer than a third of people remit on their first SSRI in STAR*D — worth saying out loud to a discouraged patient, so a non-response reads as one data point in a sequence, not proof she's untreatable.

2016-295.sentence: Your own anxiety about discharging someone who's still visibly depressed can tempt you to leave 'suicidal ideation' on the chart after it's actually resolved — that's misrepresenting the record to manage your own worry, not the patient's real risk.

2016-296.sentence: Hand-feeding has become the feed that proves he still needs to be a patient, not a tool that helps a burn body heal. A reward for self-feeding puts the spoon back in his hand so care is earned function, not family as the only nourishment.

2016-297.sentence: The parent who names the wish to stay out and still takes privileges is the one holding the frame: curfew is the fee for belonging, not a mood. Grounding for a month with no talk, or sliding the hour later, either drops the limit or drops the relationship.

2017-1.sentence: Quality of social support is the real holding environment after a spouse dies: other people carry the grief so the treatment hour does not have to become a substitute marriage. Your ethical job is to find who still shows up and to refuse the quiet invitation to fill the empty chair yourself.

2017-3.sentence: Calling one-to-two-minute chewing spells with amnesia a 'dissociative state' is denial: it keeps a seizure in the safer category of mind so nobody has to say brain. Complex partial seizures will not yield to interpretation; they are uninterruptible automatisms, and a normal MRI does not talk them out of existence.

2017-4.sentence: The opening jab tests whether your ego can hold heat without counterattacking, taking a history detour, or proving you are the good doctor. Saying you are sorry they felt unheard and asking them to describe it is affect tolerance in action: you stay with the rupture long enough for an alliance to form.

2017-6.sentence: Her breezy 'sure, no problem' already recruits you: she offers a perfect patient and you are invited to believe her so neither of you feels how hard a year without self-harm actually is. DBT answers by naming that the commitment would be extremely difficult, so the two of you hold the limit together instead of colluding with a wish.

2017-8.sentence: She is holding two versions of herself that will not sit in one room: the administrative-assistant life as all-bad 'settling,' and the unlived graduate degree as the only good object. Ego integrity, Erikson's last crisis, asks her to keep both the missed path and the real decades in one mind instead of letting despair split the whole story.

2017-11.sentence: The old clinic used professional omnipotence—the defense of acting as if only we can know—to keep families out of the plan. System of care names that defense and undoes it: families sit at the table as decision-makers, not as visitors to the expert's room.

2017-14.sentence: The fluctuation in Lewy body dementia isn't a good day followed by someone giving up — it's the same illness leaking in and out of a stable baseline, so the bad hours need to be read as pathology, not as him not trying.

2017-15.sentence: Attachment here is staying with the body instead of abandoning the patient to “functional” when they develop foot drop. Weakness of ankle inversion (tibialis posterior, L5) is the finding that keeps you as a secure base: it localizes a radiculopathy and stops you from using psychology to regulate your own uncertainty.

2017-17.sentence: Walking into a first AA meeting with social anxiety is a near-dissociation: the person can leave the room without leaving the chair, splitting off into analysis or mindfulness to avoid the group. Twelve-step facilitation names the one thing that keeps them present—“you went to the meeting; it will get easier”—so the vertical split does not become the treatment.

2017-20.sentence: Her relief about the abortion is real and doesn't need to be second-guessed — but it doesn't cancel her risk either; a history of depression from before the pregnancy predicts what happens next far better than how she feels about the procedure right now.

2017-22.sentence: Childhood sexual abuse is an established risk for bulimia because the binge-purge can recruit you as the one who either looks away or takes over the body again. Watch the countertransference urge to police food or to go numb; that is the old pair trying to staff the room.

2017-25.sentence: A disorganized patient asking “are you a real psychiatrist?” is testing whether you can hold the limit of who you actually are. Naming that you are a resident—a physician in specialty training—ends the scramble to be more, less, or someone else, and that honesty is what makes the interview thinkable.

2017-26.sentence: Fear is one of the first raw affects an infant can have before envy, shame, pride, or guilt exist as ideas. Containment is the caregiver taking that nameless dread—terror without a word—and giving it shape so the baby can think “something is dangerous” instead of only evacuating panic.

2017-28.sentence: This isn't 'healthier eating' — it's splitting in action: control becomes all-good, and hunger, weight loss, and her parents' worry all get dumped into 'bad,' so there's no room left to feel conflicted about what starving is actually doing to her.

2017-30.sentence: The fourth question about a presentation font is not curiosity; it is evacuation of a belief that “I cannot be trusted to make a good decision.” Roomates (and you) get recruited as containers for that nameless incompetence until someone names the dread instead of answering the font again.

2017-32.sentence: Orbitofrontal injury can leave a person who still talks fluently but cannot use a trial comment—cannot see their own crude joke, the spend, the odd euphoria as theirs. Psychological mindedness is not IQ; it is frontal enough restraint to notice, “I just did that,” and this lesion takes that noticing offline.

2017-34.sentence: She walks around the garbage can, so the visual system is working; conversion is the mind borrowing blindness as a solution when a conflict cannot be spoken. The “pill” she is asking for is not an ophthalmology drug—it is someone to take the symptom as communication rather than as a lesion to cut out.

2017-35.sentence: Daily sumatriptan is the habit to stop first; that is medication-overuse headache, not a new migraine genotype. Denial is working here: she still calls them “chronic migraines” and keeps dosing the abortive, so the drug can stay the problem she does not have to name.

2017-36.sentence: The move that actually cuts completed inpatient suicide is taking down hanging anchors, not a no-suicide contract or more 1:1s. The unit is already in an enactment: after a near-miss, staff want a ritual of watching or locking that soothes anxiety while the ligature points stay in the ceiling.

2017-40.sentence: A registry tracks the whole panel, not only the patients who show up hurting, so the clinic faces the wish to rescue and the prohibition against endless individual heroics. The conflict lives in the list itself: you want to hold every case, and the population method says you must count them instead of devouring them one by one.

2017-45.sentence: The pre-movement potential means the cortex prepared the jerk — some agency is already there — but naming that to the patient without implying they're faking it, without forcing them to 'own' it, is the real skill in delivering this diagnosis.

2017-47.sentence: Cognitive theory puts negative evaluations of self at the center of depression; that schema is the patient’s private fee schedule—“worthless” is what they charge themselves every hour. Your job is to hold time and the frame while those verdicts get tested, not to argue the patient into a refund.

2017-48.sentence: Cutting clozapine to stop pillow-soaking sialorrhea is an enactment: the ward repeats the patient’s shame by discarding the thing that works. Glycopyrrolate treats the drool so the two of you can stay with the needed antipsychotic instead of living the rejection.

2017-51.sentence: The dip in sharing from two to three is not the child becoming mean; it is two people renegotiating who owns the toy now that the toddler has a felt autonomous self. Parents who keep insisting on “be nice” are still playing the old we-are-one game, and the child is answering with mine.

2017-52.sentence: Cognitive impairment is the victim factor that tracks elder abuse most reliably because the mind can go missing while the body stays in the chair, and bruises then have no witness inside. The overwhelmed daughter is left with a person who is there and not there, which is why the risk sits in dementia more than in race, income, or extra diagnoses.

2017-54.sentence: Parents worrying that missed shoe-tying at four is a problem are often anxious about being good-enough parents, not accurately assessing the child — a kid who already runs, kicks a ball, rides a tricycle, and zips her own coat is allowed to still be working on laces.

2017-55.sentence: The team arguing for day hospital, groups, or family psychoed is already in an enactment: they keep asking a high-utilizer with schizophrenia to come to them, which is the same miss-and-readmit loop they hate. Assertive community care is the two-person correction—staff go out, hold housing and meds, and stop repeating the door.

2017-57.sentence: When a charming patient wrecks your thinking, the first move is supervision: borrow another mind before you act. Changing the hour, transferring her, or confessing the crush treats the attraction like a fact you must manage alone instead of a signal you cannot yet metabolize.

2017-58.sentence: Learned helplessness is a limit: after inescapable shock, the animal stops trying because agency itself feels gone, and you cannot talk or wait that capacity back. Antidepressants reverse those behavioral deficits; they restore the possibility of ending the trial, not the memory of having been trapped.

2017-59.sentence: Flailing arms and a tonic 'fencing' posture look like a psychological performance, which is exactly the trap — hypermotor frontal lobe seizures are the seizure type most often mistaken for something psychogenic, so let the video-EEG overrule that impression until it says otherwise.

2017-61.sentence: The Patient Health Questionnaire is a support-level instrument: it names the depression so the clinic can track it without asking the patient to uncover why they are sad. Recommend it when the mind, and the setting, can use a five-minute map more than an hour of interpretation.

2017-63.sentence: Childhood physical abuse is the most common backdrop for DID because the child cannot use the caregiver as a secure base and must split to stay near the person who hurts them. Dissociation here is proximity management: stay attached by leaving the self that was hit.

2017-66.sentence: Innate feelings, not chromosome complement or parental mirroring, are the stronger source of gender identity, so the family’s enactment—living the assigned gender instead of talking about the felt one—cannot write over that inner sense. The work is to stop repeating the assignment in the room and hear the identity that was already there.

2017-68.sentence: First panic in late adolescence often arrives as a body that screams “heart attack” because the mind has no usable story for the surge. What cannot be represented as feeling or memory gets repeated as palpitations, chest tightness, and dying-fear that peaks in minutes—unrepresented affect using the autonomic system as its only language.

2017-71.sentence: Capacity for mental health court is not insight that bipolar “caused” the break-in, and it is not waving away counsel. What cannot stay in words—the fact that opting in means waiving certain constitutional rights—will get enacted as a nod in court if you never ask him to say the waiver out loud.

2017-74.sentence: Six to eight years from first mood symptoms to a diagnosis is enough time to miss Erikson’s identity work in late adolescence and then stall intimacy in the twenties. The delay is not just untreated illness; it is years of a self that never got a name for what was happening, so role and closeness get built around unexplained shutdowns.

2017-76.sentence: Latency (roughly 6–11) is when sexual curiosity goes quiet and the child’s energy pours into same-sex teams, skill, and school—here, basketball as the main job. Teasing girls while playing mostly with boys is the expected social map of that stage, not a failed genital arrival.

2017-77.sentence: SPECT is the test that can split Alzheimer-type from frontotemporal patterns by showing where blood flow has dropped, not just where the MRI looks thin. Think of the frontal hypoperfusion of FTD as a hole in the superego—the inner brake and social conscience—so disinhibition is not “personality” so much as a missing judge.

2017-79.sentence: HIPAA already lets you and the PCP share what you need to treat this shared patient. The hallway freeze is often isolation of affect: you turn the person into a legal object so you do not have to feel the ordinary anxiety of being a real teammate.

2017-81.sentence: Parental criminality is the risk factor that should change how you hear the fighting and lying. The child is still in a developmental window where the parent's act is the curriculum, so he practices the attachment figure's lawlessness as his working model of how people get what they want.

2017-82.sentence: It's tempting to treat new rigidity and confusion in an agitated, hallucinating elderly patient as just needing something to calm them down, but reaching for a high-potency antipsychotic like haloperidol in dementia with Lewy bodies is exactly the reflex that unmasks the diagnosis, provoking severe parkinsonism and worsening delirium instead of calm.

2017-84.sentence: A one-time consult becomes treatment when you write a prescription and then keep talking symptoms and side effects on the phone. The pill is already a feed: once you have been the person who supplies and titrates it, walking away without a handoff is abandonment, not 'just a consult.

2017-85.sentence: Exposure only works inside a firm frame: same safe setting, enough time, no improvising mid-session. That frame is what lets the medial prefrontal cortex lay down new inhibitory learning over the old fear memory instead of just restimulating it.

2017-88.sentence: Beneficence here is containment: you hold the overdose and the wish to leave until the suicide can be thought instead of acted. You do not evacuate the raw dread back onto the street because the patient demanded autonomy in the moment.

2017-90.sentence: Family psychoeducation is not a lecture to the identified patient; it is two (or more) people agreeing to stop the relapse dance together. The joint task is concrete: help the family encourage medication adherence rather than chase ambitious goals or ignore substances.

2017-92.sentence: Ego strength is uneven here: impulse control and affect tolerance hold at school, then collapse at home when a parent sets a limit and rage, threats, and all-night curfew-breaking appear. That home-only pattern is oppositional defiant disorder, not conduct disorder—the ego can still spare strangers, property, and the classroom; it just cannot metabolize parental authority without a tantrum.

2017-94.sentence: It's tempting to reach for estrogen because she's a 58-year-old woman, as if her flattened, slowed-down presentation were just menopause, but the finding that should actually drive the choice is psychomotor retardation, and liothyronine is the augmentation with real evidence for that picture, not for her age or sex.

2017-95.sentence: Insurance pushback is a real test of whether you'll let a reviewer's cost calculus override the clinical judgment you already made; admitting the patient and appealing the denial is what it looks like to actually stand behind your own risk assessment instead of quietly downgrading the plan because someone with a spreadsheet pushed back.

2017-97.sentence: Washing for three hours is a Kleinian evacuation: he tries to push a persecutory “contaminated” bit of self into the sink so it cannot stay inside him. Exposure and response prevention asks him to keep that badness in mind without the ritual, which is how he moves from paranoid-schizoid panic toward ordinary depressive concern—and a chance to repair rather than purge.

2017-98.sentence: When PTSD comes on quickly after one clear event, the person can still hold it as 'something that happened to me' rather than 'this is who I am,' and that intact before-and-after story is part of why rapid-onset PTSD carries a better prognosis than the slow-building kind layered onto a hard childhood, where the trauma feels like identity rather than injury.
