2017-99.sentence: IDEA eligibility is a legal frame, not a favor you write because grades are poor or a parent is desperate. You hold the limit: special education requires a documented disability that actually blocks progress—not a failed grade, a psychiatrist’s name on the chart, or a pill.

2017-101.sentence: Occasional masochistic heterosexual fantasies at sixteen are homework, not a diagnosis: she is trying on intensity to find what belongs to her. Excitement plus anxiety is the developmental signal that she is sorting a pattern, not announcing a paraphilia, a hidden assault, or a secret orientation.

2017-102.sentence: The ward may treat the opioids and the delirium as acting out—behavior used to discharge feeling instead of naming an illness. Order urine porphobilinogen anyway: acute intermittent porphyria hides behind that “drug-seeking” story with the same belly, weakness, and confusion.

2017-106.sentence: Risperidone or aripiprazole can quiet aggressiveness; they will not grow a secure base or buy gaze, prosody, or pragmatic talk. Parents are asking medicine to do attachment work—keep the child close enough to regulate without demanding a social self the drug cannot install.

2017-108.sentence: A tissue and a walk to the elevator can be a crossing the conscience can own; sex, money, or secrecy is a violation because it exploits. The superego test is simple: did you use the patient, or did you stay a clinician who can still say no.

2017-112.sentence: Fluoxetine can strip hydrocodone of its analgesic punch by inhibiting CYP2D6, so the patient loses the O-demethylated active metabolite and the pain comes roaring back. That is a self-esteem injury, not automatically drug-seeking: the person who felt competent and soothed by a working analgesic now feels failed by the medicine and by you.

2017-113.sentence: The first move is to name the jurisdiction’s insanity test—M’Naghten, ALI, or whatever this court actually uses—before you interview anyone. That is the collision of a wish (to exonerate, to heal) and a prohibition (you do not get to invent the legal question); the standard is the frame that keeps the evaluation from becoming a rescue fantasy.

2017-116.sentence: The frame of an intake is that you hold the limit: you do not argue the neighbors’ wiring, endorse it, or promise it will melt. You name the feeling the delusion carries so the patient is met as a person, not recruited into a debate that would collapse the interview.

2017-119.sentence: Sexual violence produces the highest PTSD rates of any trauma type because it isn't just an injury, it's a violation of the basic trust that closeness with another person is safe, which cuts deeper than an impersonal disaster like a flood or a crash.

2017-122.sentence: Neuroticism is not a solo trait sitting in her head; it is a two-person loop: her catastrophizing meets your next workup, and together you keep minting new somatic complaints. Name the dance early or the clinic becomes the other half of the personality risk factor.

2017-125.sentence: Piaget mapped when a mind can construct how the world works—not when it can walk, detach, or repress. The four-year-old who thinks the tall glass holds “more” juice has not yet grown conservation; that capacity arrives later, and you wait for it instead of arguing with preoperational logic.

2017-126.sentence: Abstract reasoning is the ego’s later-arriving skill of moving from proverb to instance and back—grass greener, apple and orange. If it never quite arrived, you stop asking for metaphor and speak in concrete, same-level examples.

2017-131.sentence: Dry at four, wet again at six is secondary enuresis: the night symptom arrived after a secure-enough stretch. That timing often marks a hit to the attachment system—loss, a new sibling, a shaken base—rather than the genetic deep-sleep pattern Dad and the uncles had.

2017-133.sentence: The Beck Depression Inventory asks the patient to rate herself; that only works if she has enough observing ego—the part that can look at feeling instead of just being flooded by it. If she cannot name sadness without collapsing or blanking, skip uncovering and start with a clinician-rated scale plus support until that observing function is stronger.

2017-135.sentence: The teen’s one-word answers are often suppression: he knows more than he will say and holds it out of the hour. Parental interviews are how you get the history his defense will not give you, not a courtesy add-on.

2017-137.sentence: Erikson’s identity diffusion is a lack of continuity of self across relationships over time; it can feel like dissociation, a vertical split where she leaves without leaving the chair. One self shows up for one person, another for the next, so no single “I” holds.

2017-139.sentence: OCD that starts in childhood shows up before a kid has fully learned that a scary thought is just a thought, not a fact to act on, so instead of settling into one clean adult illness it tangles up with the developing mind itself, dragging ADHD, tics, and anxiety along with it, which is why childhood-onset OCD carries a heavier comorbidity burden than the adult-onset kind.

2017-141.sentence: Motivational interviewing does not argue, prescribe, or sell change; it holds the gap between drinking through the kids’ events and wanting to be a present father until that contradiction is thinkable. That is containment: you metabolize the raw shame into a named discrepancy instead of evacuating it with a lecture.

2017-145.sentence: She is recruiting you the way she now recruits her mother: someone who will bless the newlywed choices so she does not have to own them. That is transference, not dependent personality—her earlier out-of-state college move already showed she can decide alone; the phase-of-life stress is what collapsed her back into seeking parental approval.

2017-146.sentence: You may forcibly give antipsychotics in jail for emergency danger, for symptoms that threaten safety, or to restore competency to stand trial—not to extract a confession and not because a forensic psychiatrist or a benefit–risk note says so. The frame is the court, not the dyad: you are treating so he can face the charge, which is a legal use of the body, not a clinical alliance.

2017-147.sentence: Ask how he would describe the problem to a family member or friend; that pulls the complaint into his own idiom instead of your guess about “his people” or spirituality. The wish to be understood collides with your unfamiliarity; the question lets him name the conflict rather than you filling it with a cultural stereotype.

2017-151.sentence: His complaint of slowness is also a recruitment: he is handing you the role of the person who will either certify him as demented or hold the line that he is still himself. Notice your countertransference—the urge to rush, finish his sentences, or over-reassure—because information processing speed is what actually slows after 65, and your impatience can become the proof he came in fearing.

2017-152.sentence: Transference is not a trivia term; it is the old relationship walking into the room and using you as the stand-in. Name it as reenacted feeling in the pair of you, not as her being “difficult,” so the wary please-don’t-abandon-me intensity can be talked about instead of lived.

2017-154.sentence: The preference for the human voice at birth is not a cute extra; it is the newborn’s first job—finding a speaker and locking on. Talking to the baby is already doing something: it offers a living object before words mean anything.

2017-157.sentence: When a patient says a drink calms the tremor, that's diagnostically useful for essential tremor, but it's also worth asking whether alcohol has quietly become how they manage a shaky hand in public, since 'a drink helps' can slide from clinical sign into self-medication before anyone names it.

2017-159.sentence: Parents of a child with autism often hear 'highly heritable' as a verdict that they caused it; your job in that conversation isn't to hand them a clean genetic explanation or a guarantee about the next pregnancy, but to hold their fear of having 'passed something on' without confirming it as blame.

2017-160.sentence: Thanking her for saying she cursed, then working on alternatives, is mirroring: you reflect a mother who can still be competent, not a monster. If you only dump your anger or rush to CPS talk, you shatter the idealizing/self-esteem need that brought the confession.

2017-164.sentence: Piaget maps the lone scientist and leaves conscience out of the lab: guilt, shame, and the wish to please never get a stage. That is why his model cannot explain a withdrawn adolescent whose thinking is intact and whose learning is still frozen by a harsh inner judge.

2017-165.sentence: Physicians who die by suicide are less likely than other completers to have been on an antidepressant; the white-coat identity recruits you into being the one who never needs the pill. That transference is lethal when it also lives in the treating doctor, who under-prescribes rather than sit with a colleague as a patient.

2017-166.sentence: Once complex partial seizures quiet, the mind can park the old storm in a paranoid story that the neurologist means harm—interictal psychosis, not a new personality. The symptom is doing the seizure's old job: keeping danger outside the self after months of control.

2017-167.sentence: At five she is not mixing parade with circus fantasy; she is using the circus to build a category of big public shows that might include clowns. That is categorical thought arriving on time: yesterday's experience becomes today's working class, not a failure of reality testing.

2017-170.sentence: Duration of untreated psychosis is a limit you cannot rush away: first-generation immigrant status often stretches the time before anyone names the break, so language, stigma, and access keep the person in raw experience longer. Shorter DUP is the clinic’s time-boundary; longer DUP here is not “worse character,” it is delayed recognition that the illness has already started.

2017-171.sentence: Two-word phrases (“more milk”) are the toddler’s first container: a raw want gets held in a tiny sentence instead of only a scream. If the two-year-old cannot yet combine words, the feeling stays closer to Bion’s nameless dread—evacuated as noise rather than thinkable speech strangers could even half-understand.

2017-175.sentence: It's easy to hear three ED visits for chest pain and a brother's fatal MI and assume this is health anxiety, but exertional pain relieved by rest is a real cardiac red flag, and treating it as reassurance-seeking risks missing the very thing he's most afraid of.

2017-178.sentence: The hour in the bathroom is attachment work gone solitary: the mirror is being used as a regulating other, a secure base that never answers back. Body dysmorphic disorder, not excoriation disorder, means the protest is “look at this ruined face,” not “I cannot stop picking.”

2017-179.sentence: A visible hockey-crooked nose plus “I want to look normal again” is ego strength: reality testing is intact, affect is contained, and the wish is repair, not a new self. Quality of life often rises after that kind of surgery because the ego is not being asked to metabolize a phantom defect.

2017-182.sentence: Before you say a word to de-escalate, check your own body: are you between the patient and the door, close enough to be grabbed, squared up like you're bracing for a fight? Awareness of positioning, yours and theirs, is the first intervention, before any sentence about calming down or consequences.

2017-185.sentence: When this five-year-old turns mother’s gentle help into fear and aggression, she is using a defense: she treats comfort as danger so she does not have to need anyone. That is not autism’s social-communication pattern and not PTSD’s re-experiencing; reactive attachment after neglectful foster care is the child refusing consolation because depending once already failed.

2017-188.sentence: Industry versus inferiority is the work of latency: make something, get good at it, and let peers and a father see the competence. Ego strength here is that he can take pride in the basketball cards instead of collapsing into inferiority when the parents ding his grades.

2017-191.sentence: Bioequivalence means the same rate and extent of absorption, not an identical pill, and when a patient insists 'the generic doesn't work the same,' that's not always pharmacology talking; sometimes it's the unsettling feeling of losing a familiar object, which can produce real symptoms even when the blood levels match.

2017-192.sentence: Head injuries, especially abusive head trauma, are the leading cause of child maltreatment deaths—ahead of burns, starvation, or retroperitoneal bleeds. In that consult you are recruited to become either the adult who will not see the head or the one who must carry the rage; name that countertransference before you write.

2017-194.sentence: Constricted affect means the feeling is still there, just narrowed, sad with a minimal smile but some normal inflection in the voice. That flicker of range is the opening: unlike a truly flat, shut-down presentation, there's still enough here for a gentle comment about how she's feeling to actually land.

2017-195.sentence: The real limit on videoconference telepsychiatry is not the rural patient; it is physician dissatisfaction with a thinner frame. You cannot rush a clinician into a new ending of the old office ritual if they still experience the screen as a loss of the work.

2017-198.sentence: It's easy for a dramatic self-harm presentation to become the whole story a team reacts to, but no eye contact, flat affect, monotone speech, and stereotyped posturing didn't start three days ago; autism spectrum disorder was hiding in plain sight under the crisis everyone rushed to manage.

2017-199.sentence: At two to three the tantrum is acting out: the child discharges frustration in the body instead of holding it. A good-enough attachment lets the toddler borrow the parent's calm so waiting can start to replace the meltdown.

2017-202.sentence: After a shooting, the family's 'does his depression mean the guns go?' is already an enactment: panic is being lived as a blanket ban instead of thought as risk. The APA position—restrict firearms for people with increased violence risk, not for a diagnosis or a past hospitalization—keeps you from joining that scene.

2017-206.sentence: Clozapine is the only atypical that has consistently beaten typicals for treatment-resistant psychosis—the two of you, and the family, are not shopping for a ‘stronger’ brand. The relational move is to stop the search for a magic pill and share the hard work: agranulocytosis monitoring, weekly labs, and staying in the room when hope and disappointment keep trading places.

2017-207.sentence: The necessaries doctrine says we treat because prison takes away the person’s power to seek care—an imposed separation from the usual secure base of choosing a doctor. When the charge nurse says ‘he’s a prisoner,’ you answer that deprivation of access, not worthiness, is why the SSRI and weekly therapy are required, same as in the community.

2017-208.sentence: The nightly glass of wine is not a secret dementia engine in this story; it has been a stable, moderate ritual that never needed to be the symptom. Advise her to keep the pattern if it does not change—parental dementia plus aging is not a reason to turn a long-held dinner habit into a new self-punishment.

2017-209.sentence: Gray matter volume actually peaks in late childhood, right before the pruning of adolescence begins, so the academic 'wall' some kids hit around puberty isn't a kid who suddenly stopped trying, it's a brain being remodeled, and it helps to say that to a worried parent instead of letting effort take the blame.

2017-210.sentence: It's tempting to reach for opioids when severe pain doesn't show up on an MRI, as if unexplained meant not real, but classic trigeminal neuralgia is a specific, treatable nerve syndrome, and carbamazepine treats the actual cause instead of just chasing the pain with narcotics.

2017-211.sentence: Hyponatremia with mild confusion and lethargy is a support-first mind: the ego is metabolically soggy, so you correct sodium and water, not chase an unconscious conflict. Uncovering talk lands as more noise until the BMP is normal and thirst is no longer running the interview.

2017-212.sentence: The five-month-old’s gurgle-wave-kick and the mother’s tickle are how a good object gets built: mother is taken in as someone who answers excitement with pleasure, not as a temperament trait sitting inside the baby alone. Attachment here is a two-person holding of good feeling, not a one-person setting on a dimmer switch.

2017-213.sentence: A single day-long workshop dumps the algorithm into the CMHC as if staff should swallow a perfect object and feel grateful; leftover hatred of the change then has nowhere to go. Return visits after a focused workshop let you take in their projected incompetence and resistance—projective identification, meaning they put the “this will fail” feeling into you—and hand it back as problem-solving instead of abandonment.

2017-215.sentence: Asking 'when did you first notice you were thinking about cutting' is a behavioral chain question, not an accusation; it treats the urge as a sequence you can map and interrupt, instead of asking 'why would you do that,' which just puts her in the dock and shuts down disclosure.

2017-217.sentence: Opposite-gender clothes and play at six often sit in a still-plastic developmental window, not a finished identity. Gender dysphoria that starts prepuberty most often remits on its own by adulthood, so the work is to hold the child through latency without treating play as destiny.

2017-219.sentence: When a parent recruits you as the judge of a seven-year-old 'loner,' notice the pull to become either the harsh critic or the reassuring grandparent. School age is about peers and group play, so your job is to name that task without joining the parent's panic or dismissing it.

2017-221.sentence: Depersonalization is a vertical split: the person leaves without leaving the chair, watching a body that no longer feels like theirs. Name it apart from derealization (the world goes unreal) so the patient can locate the cut inside the self, not in the room.

2017-222.sentence: PTSD risk is not only the crash; it is the old relational weather the person already lived in. Prior childhood adversity means the nervous system learned, with actual other people, that help does not come—so the new trauma lands on a two-person template already built for terror.

2017-225.sentence: Taking the flowers is a boundary crossing: you bent the usual no-gifts rule so she could enter the room, then you keep the frame by documenting it and thinking about it. A violation would have been becoming her friend; here the limit still belongs to you, and the gift is allowed to mean “I can risk being known.”

2017-226.sentence: Selective abstraction is already happening between you: she hands you a stack of glowing evaluations and you are invited to live only inside the one mild note about questions. That is an enactment—the two of you repeating her habit of treating one blot as the whole self instead of naming the filter.

2017-227.sentence: He is using intellectualization: a confusing surge of arousal around male friends gets turned into a courtroom question—“am I gay?”—so the feeling never has to stay in the body. You answer the facts (these feelings are common at fourteen; preference is still consolidating) so the defense can loosen without you assigning him a lifelong verdict.

2017-229.sentence: The paraphrase is the mirroring the speaker just earned: a partner who can repeat the specific behavior and the feeling back, without fixing it yet, tells the self it was heard accurately. Jumping to change, confession, or brainstorming would skip that reflection and leave one person feeling incompetent in the room.

2017-231.sentence: When pro-inflammatory cytokines rise with a rheumatoid flare, the mind has less spare capacity for uncovering work; support and treating the immune load come first. Insight-heavy technique during that inflammatory window asks a metabolically taxed ego to do more than it can hold.

2017-232.sentence: A 3½-year-old who walks in on the shower and asks why Dad’s penis is “fat” is using age-typical curiosity, not a collapse of impulse control or reality testing. The father’s alarm is the ego under strain; the boy’s is handling genital difference with ordinary preschool interest.

2017-237.sentence: Contamination is the paranoid-schizoid version of OCD: dirt is not just dirt; it is a persecutor that must be kept out. Washing is an attempt to evacuate that projected badness from the skin rather than to mourn ordinary mess and stay in the depressive position, where concern and repair replace endless purification.

2017-240.sentence: Rapprochement is the toddler crisis of needing the parent and hating that need; in this adult it returns as closeness that feels like a crime. A harsh superego—conscience after abuse—treats intimacy as disloyalty or danger, so she cuts the tie before guilt and terror can be named in the room.

2017-248.sentence: It's tempting for both of you to file a change in rigidity under 'his depression,' but andropause has a specific vascular-hormonal signature distinct from mood, and naming it plainly keeps a physical change in aging androgen levels from quietly becoming evidence of failure or decline.

2017-249.sentence: Wraparound is an individualized, family-driven and youth-guided team—not a court, not 24/7 ACT, not a peds–psychiatry handshake. After serial placements, the family becomes the secure base again: the kid uses a known caregiver to regulate, and the team exists to keep that proximity from being taken over by the system.

2017-252.sentence: In precontemplation, 'Have you heard about the health benefits of quitting?' offers a small mirror of competence: he can take in a fact without being told he is reckless or ready. Scare lines, pep talks, and quit-date questions puncture self-esteem; curiosity about benefit leaves his ideal self intact long enough to listen.

2017-253.sentence: Three documented bursts of aggression toward ED patients are not a private lapse; they are evacuation, dumping raw, unthinkable affect into whoever is in the room. Sending the colleague to the physician health program is the institution doing what Bion called containing: holding that heat long enough for it to become thinkable instead of living in the next patient's body.

2017-254.sentence: The sexual-side-effect veto is doing work: it protects a last intact piece of potency so the antidepressant cannot take that too. Escitalopram is the listed agent least likely to induce treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction, so you can treat the depression without stripping the function that still feels like self.

2017-255.sentence: Adaptive mourning is a developmental capacity, and it arrives only if someone lets the child put loss into words. Rapid remarriage, a stoic surviving parent, parentification, or a push for closure all stall that capacity; opportunities to express the loss let it come online.

2017-257.sentence: A dying 34-year-old with under three weeks will recruit you as the last person who can still do something fast, and that pull is countertransference you should name, not act out as heroic delay. Methylphenidate is the treatment that matches the time left; sertraline, duloxetine, or mirtazapine would leave you and the patient waiting for an antidepressant that will not arrive.

2017-258.sentence: Losing identity after 'walking away from something horrible,' with a clean EEG, urine, and scan, is the mind splitting off a bad object so the self does not have to hold both. Dissociative amnesia is that split in action: the person stays, the intolerable relationship is gone from memory.

2017-275.sentence: The family dragged her in, so the first limit is whose hour this is: she stays if she wants the chair, not if they want a less embarrassing daughter. Avoidant personality disorder lives on the certainty of humiliation; a predictable fee and a closed door are the first proof you will not join the critics.

2017-280.sentence: A slot machine runs on a variable-ratio schedule, and that unpredictability is exactly why it produces the strongest, most extinction-resistant behavior of any reinforcement pattern — the brain never learns "not yet," so the next pull always feels like the one that pays. That's not a willpower problem; it's very effective training.

2017-283.sentence: His comprehension is intact — he can follow every word you say — but he has almost no way to answer back, which makes the silence feel unbearable for both of you. Resist the urge to fill it for him; rescuing him too fast quietly tells him the struggle itself is the problem.

2017-284.sentence: Erikson's tasks keep moving if one parent still supplies a reliable world: trust, industry, and later identity do not require a second spouse at the table. Remarriage is not a developmental rescue; stable parental functioning and money are what keep the child from stalling on the stage they are actually in.

2017-286.sentence: Illness anxiety disorder fixes on one feared diagnosis and interrogates it relentlessly, while somatic symptom disorder spreads the anxiety across many bodily complaints at once. The difference isn't how sick someone feels — it's whether the fear has a single target or floods everywhere.

2017-289.sentence: A trial comment is: “When I leave, it is as if a piece of you walks out with me.” If they can use that, they see the rage as loss of a self-object—another person doing a needed function for the self—not as you being a careless doctor.

2017-292.sentence: Starting an SSRI here isn't declaring the cancer has broken her spirit — it's recognizing that suffering doesn't have to clear a full diagnostic bar to deserve treatment. Waiting for her to "earn" the label of depression by getting worse only adds a second illness on top of the first.

2017-294.sentence: Ten percent is a real risk, not a prophecy — hand him that number as a reason to watch for early signs, not as proof he's already becoming his sibling. How you deliver a genetic-risk statistic changes whether it lands as useful information or as a sentence.

2017-296.sentence: The argument already replayed in the body: complete right-arm 'paralysis' after a fight invites you into a two-person debate about who is right. The face-hand drop answers a different question—if the falling hand still protects the face, the pair of you are living a conversion scene, not a clean corticospinal lesion.

2017-297.sentence: A prior puerperal psychosis is a vertical split waiting to reopen: after delivery the mind can leave ordinary reality without leaving the bed. Age, parity, and a hard labor matter less than that last postpartum break plus bipolar I—plan sleep, meds, and watchers around that history, not around the delivery note.

2017-299.sentence: The thank-you is doing work: it keeps you as a usable good object so the marriage can stay improved. Supportive technique accepts that gift—'I'm glad our work has helped'—instead of interpreting the credit or assigning homework that asks for more ego than this patient has.

2018-4.sentence: Peek-a-boo only works once object permanence is in place: the parent can vanish and still be expected back. That is a limit you cannot rush—an infant who cannot hold the hidden other cannot yet use an ending, only a disappearance.

2018-7.sentence: That dread of being seen as inadequate isn't a passing worry — it's a schema, an old rule so automatic she never actually gets to think "is this really necessary?" before she's already back at her desk. Your question is a chance to slow that rule down long enough for her to notice it's running the show.

2018-8.sentence: Confidentiality worries keep adolescents from walking into school-based mental health care because the building itself is full of people who already know them — a teacher in the hallway, a friend at lunch. When kids can't trust the visit will stay private, the safest move is simply not to show up.

2018-9.sentence: Supportive psychotherapy names the goal as better ego functioning and self-esteem because this patient cannot yet stand a wish and a prohibition colliding in full view. You lend ego—structure, praise, reality testing—so drive and guilt do not tear through when memory work or exposure would only flood.

2018-12.sentence: Selective abstraction is why she can walk off a stage the whole house cheered for and remember only the half-second she stumbled — the mind keeps the one flaw and discards everything that contradicts it. Until she can let the performance actually end as a whole, no amount of applause will feel like enough.

2018-13.sentence: A mental health court is a container: it holds the raw mess of psychosis-plus-trespass so the system can think instead of dump the person into jail. When the court cannot metabolize nameless dread about “the crazy offender,” it evacuates him into incarceration.

2018-14.sentence: Isolation of affect, intellectualization, and reaction formation keep the self from needing a mirroring other; the obsessive-compulsive patient feels competent by staying dry and precise. Warmth would feel like a leak in self-esteem, so the story of the divorce stays brilliant and bloodless.

2018-17.sentence: Watching someone flush, vomit, and crash their blood pressure after drinking on disulfiram can pull you toward "he brought this on himself" — that's old shame about addiction talking, not a clinical read. Treat the reaction as a medical emergency first and notice the judgment separately, so it doesn't quietly shape the care he gets.

2018-18.sentence: The Strange Situation isn't measuring how upset the toddler gets at separation — it's measuring what happens at reunion: can the child use the parent to settle back down, or does the protest continue with no way back to calm. That reunion response is the actual window into the attachment bond.

2018-21.sentence: Integrity versus despair in later life is whether this man can accept a longer male refractory period as ordinary aging rather than as proof that desire is over. Name that change plainly: the wait between orgasms lengthens; libido, sperm count, and testosterone are not the story you need to tell.

2018-22.sentence: Intimacy in a psychodynamic group is whole-object relating: members can hold good and bad in the same person instead of splitting the room into allies and enemies. That is the working group, after engagement and subgrouping, when people risk real disclosure and still stay in relationship.

2018-23.sentence: Laughing while children torment a cat isn't cruelty exactly — it's the loss of the capacity to feel for someone else's pain, the empathy that normally stops us before we'd enjoy it. That blunting, with memory still intact, is what points to frontotemporal dementia rather than Alzheimer disease.

2018-25.sentence: A block used as a train means this 22-month-old can already hold “as if,” not just bang and mouth. That symbolic capacity is what later lets play and words carry feeling; until it is there, you stay more supportive and concrete than interpretive.

2018-27.sentence: Primary process is unconscious thought that ignores logic, time, and contradiction—wish and image first. You listen for it in dreams and free association so you do not “correct” it as if it were a toddler’s attempt to control feeling or a map of attachment figures.

2018-28.sentence: Behavioral inhibition is temperament: this child withdraws from novelty and will be the one most at risk for later anxiety. Mirror the wariness without shaming it, and stay a calm idealizable presence so the toddler can borrow courage instead of collapsing into “I am defective.”

2018-29.sentence: A reporter asking you to diagnose a candidate you've never met is asking you to resolve their own anxiety about that person, not to practice medicine. The Goldwater Rule is the refusal of that role: no professional opinion without an actual evaluation, however tempting the question feels.

2018-30.sentence: Untreated depression during pregnancy is the strongest risk factor for postpartum depression—stronger than hormones, SES, or marital strain. Treat now: the same depleted mind will be the infant’s first regulator, and you do not wait for delivery to start that work.

2018-34.sentence: A positive Hoover sign (pressure under the “paralyzed” heel when they lift the good leg) means the pathway still works and the mind is converting exam-week conflict into a limp, not faking it. Early on, support the function and do not interpret the conflict hard; this ego is using a body story because it cannot yet use words, so uncovering the graduate-school fight can wait until the leg is walking.

2018-36.sentence: At twenty-three, the real task isn't reconciling his parents' disappointment — it's identity: can he actually choose the coffee shop or medicine as his own decision, instead of living out the physician they never became. Until he can own that choice, he's not deferred, he's stuck between two lives that were never fully his.

2018-37.sentence: The listener treated a voice on the radio like a doctor who already knew him, and that's a real (if understandable) leap — but the law doesn't follow it. Without an actual doctor-patient relationship, there's no one to sue for the four-milligram binge; a public comment and a friend with pills don't add up to malpractice.

2018-40.sentence: Starting low and going slow with an antidepressant in a teenager isn't excess caution — it's what actually lowers the risk of early activation and suicidal thinking. Frequent early follow-up gives the family something to hold onto besides fear, so they don't swing between refusing all medication and rushing the dose.

2018-41.sentence: The request to restore competence so the inmate can be executed recruits you into the executioner-healer: treat just enough psychosis to make death legally tidy. Your countertransference may be to “help” or to prove you are not soft; the AMA line is the interpretation—decline that restoration role unless a commutation is already in place.

2018-47.sentence: Acknowledge the patient's fear without agreeing the plot is true; that is the trial comment you can make when insight is not available. Confrontation, buddy-talk, and locked-on eye contact all ask for a mind that can still look at itself—this one cannot yet.

2018-48.sentence: Regular periods don't rule out anorexia nervosa — restriction, fear of weight gain, and a body that's dangerously underweight still make the diagnosis, menses or not. When a patient can't hold her own safety in mind, holding the line on weight and medical risk becomes your job, not a debate to win with her.

2018-51.sentence: At sixteen the job is identity versus role confusion: finding a self that can stand with peers and still be yours. Texting the same friends and a romantic partner, plus looking up sexual health, is how this kid is doing that work, so the likely outcome is continued socialization in the current peer group, not a collapse of individuation.

2018-52.sentence: One week after the crash, nightmares, insomnia, dizziness, pain, and fear of driving are the nervous system replaying what it cannot yet file as a finished story. That is acute stress disorder, not PTSD: the unrepresented impact is still happening in the body before a month has passed.

2018-56.sentence: A harsh conscience often treats needing people as a moral failure, so the widower may hear 'stay independent' as the good path. Remaining in contact with friends is the healthier ethic: connection is not a lapse of character.

2018-60.sentence: Her inner critic treats an imperfect note or shared slide as a crime, so highlighting and rewriting become atonement. Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder is that rigid conscience running the rotation: duty-hour violations and doing the group project alone feel safer than depending on peers.

2018-61.sentence: When a borderline patient misreads every pause as abandonment, they are recruiting you to become the mind that can hold both of you—the one who can still think “what is she feeling?” while they cannot. Mentalization theory is that capacity: using your own and the other person’s inner states as the explanation for the blow-up, instead of treating the blow-up as a fact about who they are.

2018-64.sentence: High hypnotizability means the self can loosen its edges on command—attention, body, and “I” slide apart more easily than in schizophrenia or ADHD. In a dissociative disorder that same talent for absorption is already the illness: the person can leave the self so completely that memory and continuity do not hold.

2018-66.sentence: A covering doctor who expects every long-term benzodiazepine to “creep up” is treating a fear as if it were a fact the body will enact. The finding is the opposite: most patients on chronic benzos, including a stable clonazepam, keep the same dose over time.

2018-68.sentence: Envy at the end of year two is a two-person emotion: the toddler can now hold “me” next to “the baby being held” and feel the gap. That grab for the toy is the dyad teaching comparison, not a plot to manipulate Mom.

2018-74.sentence: Keeping the still-suicidal patient in hospital is the duty to treat, not the duty to cooperate with utilization review. Object relations here is simple: you stay the holding object while managed care becomes the abandoning one, and you do not split the patient out to please the payer.

2018-79.sentence: A two-year-old who prefers trucks and boys' clothes is trying on roles, not leaving her body or her sex. She still says she is a girl, so the work is with the parents' panic, not a diagnosis of a split in the child.

2018-80.sentence: Serial 7s asks whether this ICU patient can still hold a sequence in mind, which is the self staying assembled. When attention collapses, the self fragments: nurses become bank clerks and the night never ends.

2018-85.sentence: When a 19-year-old is finally in the genital stage—libido up, parents down, a more adult self coming online—he will try to recruit you as either the parent he is leaving or the lover he is approaching. Notice who you become in the room: overprotective advisor or excited accomplice both tell you which old bond he has not finished renegotiating.

2018-89.sentence: Depersonalization/derealization is the ego thinning out: she keeps reality testing (she knows she is not a robot) but loses affect tolerance and ownership of thought and body. “Head full of cotton” and out-of-body spells mean the observing ego is still there while the experiencing self has gone offline—that is why it is not DID, PTSD, or BPD as the first call.

2018-92.sentence: The commercial panel arrives as a conscience-soother: if you order pharmacogenomics, you have done the thorough, guilt-free thing. Your job is to keep a working superego—promise of utility is not the same as replicated outcome data—so you do not buy moral cover for a test that still lacks that evidence.

2018-94.sentence: The five-minute curbside is doing work for everyone: the PCP gets an expert voice, you get to feel helpful, and the patient never has to become yours. Keep that meaning honest by leaving direction and prescribing with the PCP, so the consult stays advice rather than a stealth treatment relationship.

2018-99.sentence: Erikson’s school-age task is industry versus inferiority: the child needs to feel personally worth something because he can do something, not because he is loved or looks right. When a nine-year-old quits every imperfect task, he is stuck in inferiority; the work is to restore competence as the currency of self-esteem, not to soothe him back into earlier attachment.

2018-100.sentence: Buying a stake in a patient’s startup is a boundary violation: money and treatment become the same relationship, and you can no longer hold the frame. Dual roles (small-town pharmacist, a holiday scarf, a sliding fee, talking about erotic transference) can be managed; becoming her investor cannot.

2018-102.sentence: Delayed ejaculation tracks the aging body: fast sensory fibers drop out and sex steroids fall, so climax—the ending—takes longer or does not arrive. That is a limit you cannot rush; naming the physiology keeps you from treating time itself as a character flaw or an SSRI until you have checked both.

2018-106.sentence: A baby doesn't have just one attachment figure — he forms bonds with anyone who shows up reliably, even if the intensity differs and mom stays the first choice when he's distressed. Dad's daytime hours aren't a consolation prize; they're building a second real relationship the baby can actually use.

2018-111.sentence: The consent ritual can become an enactment: the team performs autonomy while the patient still feels like a subject being processed. Belmont’s respect for persons is the brake on that repetition—informed consent only if the person is treated as an end, not a means.

2018-115.sentence: The request to assay sertraline in milk and infant blood is often less about pharmacokinetics than about whether she can bear being a mother who needs a pill. A trial comment—“You want numbers so you are not the one deciding it is safe to treat yourself”—tests whether she can see her guilt instead of outsourcing it to the lab.

2018-118.sentence: When mammillary bodies and the dorsal (mediodorsal) thalamus die from thiamine loss, the past cannot be laid down, so the mouth fills the gap with confabulation. What cannot be remembered gets repeated as a story invented on the spot, in the body and in the interview.

2018-119.sentence: CBT for persistent voices and delusions does not erase the drive; it asks what wish or threat the belief is carrying. The work is to let the forbidden idea be examined instead of lived as persecution.

2018-122.sentence: The family is not only asking for a pamphlet; they are asking you not to leave them holding the psychosis alone. Pointing them to the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) names a third party that can absorb their rage, grief, and lobbying energy so you do not become the only parent in the room.

2018-128.sentence: Histrionic attention-seeking is proximity work: the other person has to stay visually locked on or the attachment system reads it as abandonment. Theatrical affect and provocative dress are not vanity first; they are a loud bid to use you as an external regulator when inner continuity is thin.

2018-129.sentence: Competency to stand trial lives in present ego strength: can this person still reality-test the charge and tolerate enough affect to work with counsel. Intent at the theft, Miranda, and treatment consent are other legal questions; here you are asking whether the observing ego can sit in a room with a lawyer without falling apart.

2018-136.sentence: When a patient isn't responding to a normal risperidone dose despite taking it, it's easy to read that as "he must not really be taking it" — but multiple wild-type CYP450 alleles can burn through the drug before it ever gets a chance to work. Check the metabolism before you assume the nonadherence.

2018-137.sentence: No two-word phrases by two years old is a reason to test the child's hearing, not a verdict on how the family talks at home. It's easy to let assumptions about language or background explain away a delay that a simple hearing test would actually catch.

2018-140.sentence: After a disaster the child’s wish is to stay glued to the parent; the prohibition is “you have to go back to life.” Peer support is the compromise that holds both: other kids let the wish for attachment live without turning the parent into the only safe object, which is why peers beat relocation, counseling access, or media validation as protection against post-traumatic symptoms.

2018-141.sentence: What you cannot remember about failing to get your alcoholic parent to quit is being repeated in this room: you lean, they stall, and the body of the treatment is the old scene. Countertransference is that leftover urgency—not the patient’s resistance—and it is why you insist “we are making progress” when the only change is your pulse.

2018-143.sentence: The dying patient’s conscience is already working overtime; a sudden move can feel like abandonment they “deserve.” An identified care person is the external ego that keeps the handoff moral and practical, which is why that person predicts a better transition more than older age, a non-cancer diagnosis, or a sudden change in health.

2018-144.sentence: Legal responsibility asks whether the person can see their own wish and still choose. The man with severe alcohol use who robs a liquor store for vodka is most likely responsible: intoxication he sought does not erase the act the way command hallucinations, severe intellectual disability under a father’s demand, or statutory-age mistake can.

2018-147.sentence: Collaborative care exists because specialty mental health cannot mirror every patient’s need for an available, competent other — the workforce simply does not have that capacity. The care manager and weekly caseload review restore a bit of idealized competence in the primary-care home instead of sending people into a waitlist that cannot hold them.

2018-148.sentence: When you and the patient are already living the split — one hour you are all-good, the next you are trash — that is an enactment: the old Kleinian pattern is happening between you, not just being described. The depressive position is the later capacity to hold one mother, one therapist, as both helpful and frustrating at the same time, which is exactly what this enactment has not yet allowed.

2018-152.sentence: Ask the parents one trial comment: “So the storm starts when a no lands, not out of the blue?” If they can use that, they are seeing a protest at a limit, which is oppositional defiant disorder, not a bipolar switch. Psychological mindedness here is noticing the trigger is the word no, not an endogenous mood cycle.

2018-153.sentence: You asked a CBT meaning question and she filled the hour with a chain that runs from one physics exam to exile from the family; that is catastrophic thinking, not a request to cancel the exam. Hold the frame: stay with the thought, name the leap, and do not collude by rescheduling reality so she never has to sit the test.

2018-156.sentence: Vertical nystagmus plus a clouded, agitated eighteen-year-old is phencyclidine, and the ED often answers with matching force: more holds, more shouting, more bodies. That is an enactment: the room starts living PCP’s fight instead of containing it with quiet, space, and benzos.

2018-157.sentence: He starts the sexual story, then blanks—the mind leaves the chair while the body stays. “You’re doing fine. Go on.” is a tether: you keep him in the room with the words instead of letting the split finish the sentence for him.

2018-159.sentence: Tying shoelaces is last because the child must sit with two hands, a knot, and frustration while you stay nearby as the secure base. Velcro and snaps let the parent finish the job; laces ask the child to use you for regulation, not for the bow.

2018-162.sentence: In acute refeeding the starving superego—the inner prosecutor—is already running the unit; insight work just hands it more charges. Coach, support, and reinforce calories so conscience is not recruited as another reason she does not deserve food.

2018-163.sentence: Transvestic disorder is not a late-arriving gender identity; the erotic charge still lives in the garment, and that is a different developmental line from wanting to be the other sex. Distress here is shame about the fetish, not a child’s-then-adult’s conviction that the body is the wrong one, which is why gender dysphoria does not fit.

2018-164.sentence: Asking how the parents respond when the child is afraid of the bus locates the payoff: the symptom is doing work, not just ringing an old alarm. If fear reliably brings closeness, exemption, or a cancelled ride, the crash fantasy is being reinforced as a family signal, which is the operant story.

2018-165.sentence: An adolescent with anorexia often cannot yet use individual uncovering; the family has to hold the meals and the fight until that capacity returns. Family therapy beating individual work at 6–12 months is the clinical translation: more support now, better autonomy later, not a forever family treatment for adults.

2018-166.sentence: He is using projection, putting his own disowned doubt and hostility into the wife’s inbox and the friends’ “side,” then policing them as if the threat were outside. That pattern without a mood drop or a true delusion is paranoid personality, not delusional disorder: the jealousy is a character habit, not a break with reality.

2018-170.sentence: The harsh conscience says methadone is a moral stain and that a “good mother” must detox for the fetus. Continuing methadone maintenance is the sanctioned gap: you refuse that guilt ritual because withdrawal and relapse hurt mother and baby more than staying on the agonist.

2018-171.sentence: Asking you about a bipolar mood app is a recruitment: you are being invited to become either the all-knowing endorser or the scolding parent who forbids it. Reviewing the app yourself, then discussing it, keeps you as a thinking partner instead of acting out that transference.

2018-172.sentence: Amnesia for everyday events is not just trauma-forgetting; it is the symptom doing identity work, carving ordinary hours into unowned time. PTSD can blank the assault; dissociative identity disorder blanks Tuesday, so another part can carry the day.

2018-174.sentence: Non-judgmental noticing of inner and outer stimuli is a mirroring function: you treat each sensation as legitimate instead of grading it. That stance props up self-esteem until the patient can hold experience without the inner critic collapsing the self.

2018-175.sentence: Metacognitive therapy is a container: it takes raw, unthinkable fragments—jumping to conclusions, missed social cues, no sense of what your own mind can and cannot do—and names them so they can be thought instead of evacuated. Without that naming, the patient is left with nameless dread, the feeling that something is happening in the mind that cannot be known, only acted out as certainty or withdrawal.

2018-177.sentence: The six-year-old wants contact—friends, jokes, the teacher's greeting—and the prohibition is the missing pragmatic code: turn-taking, greeting, nonliteral speech. Social (pragmatic) communication disorder is that collision as a symptom: the wish to join stays intact, while the social rule that would make joining work is the part that cannot be used.

2018-180.sentence: Entrainment works because a psychogenic tremor is listening to the room, not to a damaged circuit — ask the patient to tap a different rhythm, and the "tremor" follows the tapping hand instead of keeping its own rate. That's the tell that the movement is being generated by attention and expectation, not by disease.

2018-182.sentence: Dextromethorphan sits in a sanctioned moral gap: cough syrup is “medicine,” so the adolescent’s conscience does not file “I’m walking on air,” hallucinations, and tachycardia as getting high. The superego (the inner prosecutor) stays quiet precisely because the bottle is OTC, which is why you ask about Robitussin before you write first-break psychosis.

2018-183.sentence: Fitness-for-duty is not therapy; the frame is a three-person room—you, the officer, and the department—so secrecy cannot be the usual clinical promise. Informed consent about the limits of confidentiality is how you keep from sliding into double agentry: serving two masters while pretending you have only one.

2018-184.sentence: The crack house is not a “temptation” speech; it is a conditioned stimulus that fires craving before intention shows up. Classical conditioning means the block does the wanting for him—Pavlov’s bell, not a character flaw—so the work is cue exposure and route change, not more lectures on willpower.

2018-187.sentence: In Kleinian terms this is projective identification: the patient dumps the “I caused this” part into you and then swats away every return of it, so the shame never has to live in him. Narcissistic structure needs you to stay the stupid, attacking object; if you stay curious instead of collapsing or counterattacking, you are doing the repair he cannot yet do.

2018-191.sentence: Offering a quiet room or a calming med is two people rewriting the crisis instead of one mind “managing” a bad object. If you jump to IM haloperidol, threats, or restraints first, you and she co-author the old scene—someone overpowers, she proves the world is assaultive.

2018-192.sentence: Nonmaleficence here is technical humility: after failed psychotherapy and adequate med trials, more uncovering or another cocktail by guesswork is harm. The consult is the supportive move this treatment can actually use—another mind, not another probe.

2018-194.sentence: Hyperactivity is the ADHD feature most likely to fade with age; inattention, impulsivity, school strain, and peer trouble often linger. Parents who hear that running-and-climbing will quiet can slip into denial, treating the quieter teen as “cured” while the sitting-still, homework, and social costs still need scaffolding.

2018-196.sentence: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder is involuntary spasm plus fear of penetration after a normal pelvic exam, not low desire or anorgasmia. In the room she leaves without leaving the chair: talking about the spasm itself is dissociated, so stay with the body fact (tightening, anticipatory anxiety, avoidance) until speech can rejoin sensation.

2018-197.sentence: Poverty of speech means the words themselves have thinned, not that this 80-year-old is being cagey or withholding on purpose — it's a sign the mind has less capacity right now to hold and elaborate a feeling into a full sentence. Slow down and lengthen your pauses instead of stacking more open-ended questions; a rushed interview just proves the point that nothing is there to find.

2018-198.sentence: HIPAA allows you to share information when the patient lacks capacity and disclosure is likely to benefit care, even over a Capgras-like refusal that the parents are imposters. Developmentally this 21-year-old has not yet held a stable adult self who can use parents as allies; the delusion freezes that late-arriving capacity, so you speak with them as needed while you keep treating the psychosis that stole consent.

2018-202.sentence: The parents split “good boy” from “girly boy” and hand you the bad half as if the child’s play were a damaged object in the family. When the ten-year-old has no distress or impairment, the diagnosis is nonconformity to gender role—keep the good and the unconventional in one child instead of pathologizing the doll play as gender dysphoria.

2018-203.sentence: The spouse’s complaint that he “won’t get up and care” can feel like a projected deadness dumped into you—classic projective identification: you are made to hold the lifelessness. Name it as Parkinson apathy with stable slowness of thought on carbidopa/levodopa, not depression, so you repair the couple’s story instead of treating imagined guilt and sadness that are not there.

2018-209.sentence: Those long, suppressible, talking limb-shakes recruit you as the neurologist who must either catch a seizure or catch a lie. Insidious onset—not mood comorbidity, a clear stressor, high IQ, or a short wait to treatment—predicts a worse functional-neurologic course, because the two of you inherit a symptom that never announced itself as a conflict.

2018-212.sentence: Moving the hour to a coffee bar after hours is already an enactment: the two of you are living the wish to make treatment feel less clinical instead of talking about why the clinic feels unbearable. The frame is the treatment; once you leave it, you are no longer doing the work you were hired to do.

2018-215.sentence: Atomoxetine’s black-box warning for suicidal ideation in children is the limit you hold with the parent, not a detail you bury because stimulants “always work.” You name the risk in the same breath as the tic-friendly reason you chose a non-stimulant, so consent stays a frame, not a sales pitch.

2018-216.sentence: Ask whether he can see that the fear arrived after a successful bone marrow transplant, when leaving the unit means losing the staff who kept him alive. If a trial comment like that lands, you have adjustment anxiety with some insight, not a personality that was always this dependent.

2018-217.sentence: Anxiety in boys can work as a developmental brake: it holds first intercourse until after 18 instead of letting peer time set the clock. That delay is a limit, not a failure—the capacity for a sexual beginning cannot be rushed just because a father wants his son caught up.

2018-219.sentence: At 25 this body-dysmorphic preoccupation sits on Erikson’s intimacy-versus-isolation task: you cannot bring a face to someone if that face feels like a fake. Fluoxetine treats the obsessive grip on the imagined defect so identity can stop organizing around the mirror.

2018-220.sentence: Avoidance is the defense: skip the cafeteria seat and the speech and you never have to survive being looked at. The blushing and twitching still leak the shame social anxiety is trying to hide, which is why the picture is not panic, phobia, or schizoid withdrawal.

2018-221.sentence: It's tempting to call a 75-year-old who is groping for words 'confused,' but nonfluent aphasia is comprehension trapped behind broken output — he understands you fine, he just can't get the word out. Resist the urge to finish his sentences for him; that habit relieves your own discomfort with the silence more than it helps him find the word.

2018-222.sentence: Once you feel flattered and attracted, the frame is already under load—fee, time, and the incest taboo of the dyad no longer hold themselves. Consultation is who holds the limit: you do not decide alone whether to lean in, pull back, or end, and you do not tell her the erotic transference “isn’t real.”

2018-226.sentence: The BPRS works because it runs on the clinician's live observation, not the patient's own report — and in active psychosis that matters, because the stable self that would need to sit still and rate itself on a checklist isn't reliably there yet. You end up being the steadier instrument in the room until reality testing comes back online.

2018-227.sentence: Fear of dying in pain is raw sensation that has not yet become a thinkable thought, so it arrives as nameless dread. Containment here is naming the pain plan, not a vague “we’ll take care of you,” so the dread can be held instead of evacuated into the team.

2018-228.sentence: Depression is the most common neuropsychiatric symptom in mild neurocognitive disorder, and it often shows up as lost interest before a story of loss can be told. What cannot be remembered as “I am slipping” is repeated as a flat mood in the body and in the family.

2018-230.sentence: Informed consent is an adult capacity: a real yes and a real no. “Sign in voluntarily or I will commit you” treats the manic patient as if that capacity never arrived, so the signature is not consent—it is a child’s forced choice.

2018-231.sentence: A WISC full-scale IQ of 60 names a score, not a life. The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales ask what the low IQ is doing in daily function—communication, self-care, social skill—because intellectual disability is that lived deficit, not the number alone.

2018-234.sentence: The wish is to be the kind neighbor who fixes the fluoxetine while his doctor is away. Advising a dose increase is where that wish beats the prohibition—and that specific medical order, not the barbecue chat, is what creates a doctor–patient relationship.

2018-237.sentence: Calling you a “wise and loving doctor” is an idealizing selfobject need: she is borrowing your shine to hold a shaky self together. In supportive work you use that idealization to strengthen the alliance; you do not puncture the mirror just to prove you are modest.

2018-240.sentence: Saturday-night palsy recruits you as either the scold or the neurologist: the radial nerve was compressed on the chair, wrist and finger extension gone, grip spared. Notice the countertransference pull to moralize the drinking; name the radial lesion first so you are not living the lecture instead of examining the wrist drop.

2018-243.sentence: Erikson’s stages are sequential because the self needs a new mirroring job at each crisis; identity versus role confusion is the adolescent’s need to be seen as a coherent someone, not a pile of roles. If that mirroring fails, she withdraws not from “laziness” but from a self that has no confirming other to lean on.

2018-249.sentence: By four, the child can keep two objects of the same toy: the one she sees and the one still sitting in the other person's mind. That is theory of mind as object relations—good enough development means she no longer assumes her inner picture is the only reality in the room.

2018-252.sentence: The mind walls off the ambush and leaves the rest of memory standing—that is repression working locally, not a global amnesia. Dense gaps limited to a few traumatic episodes are the defense succeeding: the war is gone from recall while new learning still works.

2018-255.sentence: Core gender identity is usually in place by three years, so the child’s consistent self-label is already a two-person fact, not a future maybe. The work is with the parents’ alarm, not with “correcting” a three-year-old who has already told you who she is.

2018-259.sentence: Quality of parenting is the adult who can hold the child’s rage and need without collapsing, so the wish to be kept safe does not have to fight a parent who is also the source of danger. Resilience is not IQ or an easy temperament winning; it is that collision getting metabolized in a real relationship.

2018-262.sentence: The wish to protect the child and the prohibition against “harming” them with a shot collide; CDC facts do not dissolve that fight. Tie vaccination to the group’s own values and the wish and the rule can sit in the same sentence instead of splitting into anti-vax versus science.

2018-263.sentence: Decentration is the child giving up the grandiose job of having caused the divorce; the self no longer has to be the omnipotent center to feel real. He can stay sad and angry and still keep a self that is not wrecked by blame—mirroring that he is a person in the story, not the engine of it.

2018-265.sentence: It's tempting to push the antipsychotic dose up fast when a first-episode patient is this frightened and unwell — but that urgency is exactly what produces the akathisia: the team's anxiety to fix things quickly, not the illness itself, is driving the harm. A slower titration is easier to tolerate than the restlessness that rushing creates.

2018-267.sentence: The mental health court holds the limit: legal leverage is the frame that gets participants into community treatment faster, not a cheaper system. Ethics means saying that out loud so families are not sold cost savings or a guaranteed drop in re-arrest as the proven outcome.

2018-268.sentence: A three-month collapse into dementia and myoclonus moves fast enough that everyone wants to do something — another scan, a hopeful reframe, a transfer. With Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, the harder and more honest job is to sit with the family in how quickly this is moving rather than offer false hope or chase procedures that won't change the course.

2018-270.sentence: A wish to have Hindu meanings count collides with a prohibition against bringing those explanations into a Western first visit. Asking what he believes explains the weakness, palpitations, and suicidal ideation lets that wish speak instead of forcing the conflict into an instant major-depression script.

2018-273.sentence: Illness anxiety here is a failed idealizing search: the cousin who died of a brain tumor is the terrifying parent-object, and each new MRI is a bid to restore a competent, mirroring doctor who can make the self feel intact. Almost no somatic symptoms means the wound is in self-esteem and safety, not in a body part asking to be interpreted.

2018-277.sentence: The grocery store is now a stand-in for danger, and the conscience can treat avoidance as a moral duty: stay out or you were reckless. Lorazepam soothes the panic, but it also licenses a tidy gap—chemical permission not to face the store, while the crash and the panic remain the unconditioned truth.

2018-279.sentence: It's easy for a resident to read '11% of medical students report suicidal ideation' and quietly assume they'd fall in the other 89% — that quiet exemption is denial doing its job, keeping the thought safely about someone else. Naming how ordinary that thought actually is among peers is what makes it safer to say out loud.

2018-281.sentence: When Winnicott’s holding environment never quite arrives, the infant builds a false self: a compliant surface that manages the mother instead of showing real need. Grandiosity and idealization of self-objects belong later; here the developmental failure is early, and the defense is to become what the caregiver can bear.

2018-282.sentence: Suicide as the leading trigger of psychiatric malpractice claims is also a superego crisis: the field treats a death as proof the doctor failed a duty of care. Sexual misconduct shocks the conscience louder, but the common lawsuit is the one that says you should have prevented the unpreventable.

2018-285.sentence: The attack that you are controlling and uncaring is projective identification: the patient evacuates a harsh internal object into you and then treats you as if you already are it. In Kleinian terms this is paranoid-schizoid transference, not a request that you prove you are nice; interpret the need to park the bad object in you rather than argue the charge.

2018-287.sentence: Freud's latency lines up with Erikson's industry versus inferiority: the job is competence at school and with peers, not another oedipal showdown. School refusal at eight often means the child is losing that industry battle and taking on inferiority; frame the work as restoring mastery, not just getting him through the door.

2018-289.sentence: Dissociative amnesia with major depression is a proximity move: the mind drops an unbearable stretch of autobiography so the attachment can stay intact. Unlike Alzheimer retrograde loss, Wernicke-Korsakoff anterograde loss, or the anesthetic gap, this forgetting is reversible once the relationship can hold the affect again.

2018-291.sentence: A preschooler facing leukemia does not yet live in Klein’s depressive position, where death is a real, permanent loss you can mourn. Absence of the caretaker still feels like annihilation of the good object, so the fear to name is separation, not afterlife or disappointing the parents.

2018-295.sentence: By five years a typical child can answer why, when, and how because language has become a way to keep a caregiver close as a thinking partner, not just a body in the room. Those questions are proximity-seeking with words: the child uses you as a secure base while the mind goes out to explore cause and time.

2018-296.sentence: This man has already shown failed impulse control and thin affect tolerance: bipolar illness, cardiac ischemia, a violence record, and a named plan to hunt an ex and “teach her a lesson.” Most states require you to inform the police because his ego cannot be trusted to hold the rage, so the frame has to hold it for him.

2018-297.sentence: “If I didn’t smoke, I could use the money for music” is change talk because the patient is giving the habit a competitor that actually matters to him. Smoking is no longer just a habit; it is a symptom with a price tag, and music is the meaning that starts to argue against it.

2018-299.sentence: Parental death by suicide, homicide, or accident in early childhood hits before mourning is a usable defense, so the child often relies on denial or identification rather than grief that can be thought. By young adulthood that unfinished loss shows up as depression because the mind never got a chance to metabolize the death in words.

2019-1.sentence: Lack of insight is doing work: it keeps the gangrene from becoming *his* problem, so he never has to authorize losing the limb. Appreciation fails first because knowing would collapse the last defense against a mutilating choice.

2019-7.sentence: Cardiovascular disease is the conscience of this visit: the “good patient” on clozapine who never missed a refill can still die of BP 158/96, glucose 142, high LDL, and a pack a day while you and he treat those numbers as optional extras. That is a sanctioned gap in morality—psychosis gets the full ethical heat, and the heart is allowed to fail off-stage.

2019-10.sentence: In Lewy body disease the visual hallucinations and overnight agitation are doing work: they keep the night team reaching for haloperidol, which this brain cannot tolerate. The symptom is a warning, not an invitation—severe extrapyramidal side effects are the price of treating the picture instead of the diagnosis.

2019-14.sentence: Intense fear of gaining weight is not just a DSM checkbox; it is terror that has no story yet, so it is enacted in starvation instead of remembered as a thought. The body becomes the place the unthinkable is repeated: if she cannot put words to the dread, she will keep living it at BMI 16.

2019-15.sentence: Formal operations means he can now hold a wish (feel better) and a prohibition (do not take a mind-altering drug) as ideas at the same time. Abstraction lets the conflict become thinkable—risks, hypotheses, a future self—instead of a mute yes or no to the SSRI.

2019-16.sentence: Prader-Willi rage often erupts when the self cannot borrow a calm, admiring other to regulate hunger and frustration. The microdeletion is biology; the outburst is also a collapse of self-esteem when competence fails and no idealized caretaker is felt to be there.

2019-18.sentence: Family psychoeducation strengthens the household’s ego: more affect tolerance, less blame, better impulse control around meds. Relapse after stopping antipsychotics is often a family system that cannot hold change; teaching them is building a container the patient does not yet have alone.

2019-19.sentence: A first depression is a snapshot; bipolarity shows itself over time, so the reliable test is staying close long enough to see a manic switch, not a one-visit MDQ or family tree. Longitudinal follow-up is the attachment move: you become a secure base, not a screening stranger, before you bet the farm on an antidepressant.

2019-20.sentence: Empathy and a real best friend mean the conscience has someone it can disappoint. The unkind blurt is the elementary-school gap: the superego—the inner rule-giver—can feel the standard and still lose to impulse before guilt brakes the mouth.

2019-22.sentence: When speech is gone, the wish that was never fully spoken will get acted out as a family fight at the bedside unless it already lives on paper. Advance directives are that written memory: they carry the patient's instructions about interventions so the dyad does not have to invent them under terror.

2019-24.sentence: Veracity is putting the whole contested triad in the chart: her wish to conceive, his doubt she is ready, and the valproate she already stopped. The live third in the room is the potential pregnancy—gendered, never discussed outpatient—and writing it down keeps that third from being edited out of the record.

2019-25.sentence: Living with a brain that seizes can feel like an inside attacker, a Kleinian persecutory object you cannot flee. Major depressive disorder is the most common psychiatric partner of epilepsy because many patients finally drop into depressive-position grief: sadness and a wish to repair a damaged self rather than only rage at the seizures.

2019-27.sentence: Winnicott’s holding environment is Erikson’s autonomy-versus-shame stage made physical: the adult stays close enough that the toddler can bang pots without catastrophe. Spontaneity with a safety net builds competence; hovering that removes all risk, or vanishing that leaves real harm, both collapse the same psychosocial task.

2019-28.sentence: ACT’s 24-hour-a-day coverage is the treatment frame when the usual office hour is a limit the patient cannot keep. The team holds time and availability so care does not depend on the person with schizophrenia arriving at a clinic; the frame moves to the street instead of punishing missed appointments.

2019-31.sentence: The coordinator is breaking the frame by recruiting the spouse in the patient's presence: that is a pressure on voluntarism, the right to say no without feeling you will harm the marriage or the trial. You hold the limit by taking the spouse out of the room and asking later, so consent is not a performance for the partner.

2019-32.sentence: The parent dumps a raw “I am a terrible parent” feeling into you; that is evacuation, getting rid of a state that cannot yet be thought. Goodness of fit is the container: you name the mismatch between this toddler’s intensity and the parent’s pace so the dread becomes a workable idea instead of a verdict.

2019-43.sentence: Around four, the child can keep a picture of the other person in mind long enough to care what they feel, so sharing stops being a parent demand and becomes a small act of concern. Before that, “mine” is not selfishness so much as a self that is still assembling.

2019-45.sentence: Calling cannabis “natural and harmless” is denial: she shuts out the finding that in-utero exposure tracks with later cognitive deficits so she can keep using. The consult’s job is to put that fact back in the room without shaming her into a tighter clamp.

2019-46.sentence: Sedation and analgesia are not extras; they are the relationship’s first feed, the proof that someone will not leave the child alone with the needle. Skip that prophylaxis for bone marrow biopsies and the body files it as trauma, which is why PTSD, not garden-variety worry, is the likely sequela.

2019-47.sentence: One in four people with 22q11.2 deletion develop schizophrenia, so the frame here is not wait-and-see charm; it is honest risk talk, close follow-up, and who gets told what. Holding that limit—without treating the teen as already doomed—is the ethical work.

2019-49.sentence: The song still owns a piece of childhood-style pairing: drink and cue fused before the mind could keep them separate. Extinction is the late-arriving capacity—hear that song again and again with no alcohol until the pairing finally dies of neglect.

2019-52.sentence: The church group is not a luxury hobby; it is her cultural third, a place she is a person and not only a daughter of Alzheimer dementia. If she quits it, caregiving swallows the last room that is still hers—so the first intervention is to protect that room.

2019-53.sentence: School-age work is Erikson’s industry: can I do the task, or am I the kid who cannot? A 504 plan keeps the same course and only changes access; an IEP can exempt the child from course requirements, which is a different message about what competence even means.

2019-56.sentence: Addington v. Texas sets clear and convincing evidence as the floor because commitment is a two-person fight over liberty, not a solo diagnosis you announce. You and the manic patient are already pulling opposite ways; the court refuses both a casual 'preponderance' shrug and a criminal 'beyond a reasonable doubt' lock so neither of you gets to win by force of personality.

2019-58.sentence: Forgetfulness, low energy, and poor concentration can be depression speaking as cognition instead of naming the mood. Neuropsychological testing is the first useful map: it shows whether memory is actually gone or just not being used, before you send him for a CT as if the story were already a lesion.

2019-59.sentence: She wants the new peer world and she also wants not to betray her parents; those two drives collide and the anxiety is the collision, not a failure of loyalty. Formation of a bicultural identity is the workable compromise: both wishes stay alive instead of one killing the other through total assimilation or total refusal.

2019-62.sentence: Concurrent psychosis gives the aggression a job: the person is striking at a threat that is not in the room. Word-finding, late stage, and premorbid anxiety do not supply that motive; the delusion or hallucination does.

2019-63.sentence: This is Erikson’s first task, trust versus mistrust, not a gifts-and-boundaries seminar. Accepting the cookie and thanking them lets a guarded schizotypal patient complete a small act of basic trust instead of confirming that closeness is dangerous.

2019-67.sentence: The mother is recruiting you to certify that a 10-year-old who already knows death is permanent is still “broken.” Your countertransference urge to over-work-up ordinary grief is her unheld death anxiety landing in you, not a delay in the child’s concept of permanence.

2019-68.sentence: After the screaming fight, speech itself threatened self-cohesion, so the self sacrificed the voice rather than risk another narcissistic crash in front of the spouse. The preserved cough shows conversion, not cord injury: mute to keep a scrap of esteem, not because the larynx failed.

2019-69.sentence: Naming the abandonment transference only stages the old wish-versus-prohibition collision; change is integration of insight, the ego holding the wish without having to repeat it. Transference is the theater, not the cure—shame and advice never metabolize that drive conflict.

2019-70.sentence: He splits the partner into an object who must stay innocent and you into the container of the dangerous HIV knowledge so the couple can stay all-good. Consulting state law refuses that split: the statute, not his denial or your rescue fantasy, decides partner notification.

2019-71.sentence: The wish to taper, clonidine-detox, or naltrexone-blast her is paranoid-schizoid: evacuate the bad heroin-object even if withdrawal attacks the fetus. Methadone maintenance is depressive-position repair—you keep an imperfect good object on board so mother and baby are not hammered by withdrawal.

2019-78.sentence: Claims data show fewer substance-related events in males with ADHD while they are on stimulants—the pill as regulation, not as the first hit. Treat the mother’s “you will make him an addict” as a poison fantasy about the script; the relationship task is to hold that fear while the methylphenidate or amphetamine actually lowers, not raises, the substance-event rate.

2019-79.sentence: “Nothing can destroy me” is denial: he is shoving terror of being small and breakable out of awareness. Verbal de-escalation talks to the person still behind that shield instead of proving that only needles and restraints can hold him.

2019-80.sentence: Orgasm is a capacity that cannot be rushed by estrogen, bupropion, or flibanserin. Directed masturbatory training honors the time limit: she has to learn her own body's map, not borrow climax from a pill or an interpretation.
