2019-81.sentence: Longer trauma overruns containment, Bion's word for holding a raw feeling until it can be thought. The mind evacuates the ordeal as dissociative amnesia rather than letting nameless dread stay long enough to become a memory.

2019-84.sentence: Higher education can work as a brittle reaction formation: looking capable to fend off any hint of collapse. When schizophrenia arrives, that armor fails, and the gap between the old résumé and the new illness raises suicide risk in transitional-age youth.

2019-85.sentence: Calling this disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, not bipolar I, can feel like refusing the mood stabilizer that would prove the rages are “real.” The parent may treat that pill as feed or as proof of need; stay with the chronic irritability instead of medicating a mania that is not there.

2019-90.sentence: The on-air disclaimer is aimed at duty, so callers cannot install him as their doctor by projective identification — the push to put their need into him until he behaves as if he is treating them. He is trying to stay in concern rather than omnipotence: offer a thought, not a repair a radio minute cannot finish.

2019-92.sentence: Worldwide, trance and dissociation most often sit inside religious and ritual events, so they can be identity work, not a depersonalization or PTSD diagnosis. If you pathologize Pentecostal tongues as a disorder, you mistake a culture's way of becoming a self for a broken ego.

2019-93.sentence: The 'I want to quit / I don't' split is not a stall; it is the symptom doing its job, keeping both sides of the drink alive so neither has to die yet. Motivational enhancement therapy treats that ambivalence as the work, instead of arguing the patient into one voice.

2019-94.sentence: Frieda Fromm-Reichmann's 'schizophrenogenic mother' was a developmental fairy tale: the child's psychosis was imagined as a late arrival of toxic mothering rather than a brain illness. When a parent asks if she caused it, name that history so guilt does not become the unofficial diagnosis.

2019-95.sentence: Frequent conversation and thinking aloud give the toddler words that will later become an inner voice—self-talk that can soothe, forbid, and plan. Flashcards feed vocabulary; overheard parental speech is how a conscience starts to sound like someone kind in the room.

2019-96.sentence: Dropout often happens when the therapist gets recruited into an old role—rescuer, critic, abandoning parent—and acts it instead of noticing it. Greater therapist experience is what most reliably keeps that transference from ending the treatment; matching gender or ethnicity is not the finding.

2019-98.sentence: Storytelling with words at four lets a child put a wish, a fear, and a parent into one plot instead of only acting them. The drive gets a beginning, middle, and end; without that narrative wrap, the same impulse stays a tantrum or a grab.

2019-106.sentence: The bell-and-pad pairs a wet sheet with an alarm so the bladder cue itself starts to wake the child—classical conditioning, not another sticker for willpower. That pairing can restore a bit of competence: the self feels more intact when the body begins to signal before shame does.

2019-109.sentence: A mother whose mental illness predates the birth doesn't just pass down genes — the infant can become the place where her own unmetabolized fear or despair gets lived out, what's called projective identification. That's why this outranks an SSRI in pregnancy on this list: a medication is a known, bounded risk, but a mind that can't yet hold its own distress has no way to keep it from landing on the baby.

2019-113.sentence: Waxy flexibility, mutism, and not eating recruit you into the one who must move a frozen body—that is the countertransference pull: helpless handler versus enforcer. Give lorazepam for catatonia; benztropine treats EPS, not this still, unseeing patient.

2019-115.sentence: In a family organized around an eating disorder, the fight about control and food is often not only hers — it's the whole family's unbearable anxiety, projected into her body and acted out there instead of spoken about. Structural family therapy works by handing the parents the job of feeding back to them, literally, so she isn't left alone holding what no one else could metabolize.

2019-116.sentence: Quitting two months before you graduate is the symptom doing a job: she leaves first so the abandonment is hers, not yours. Interpret that reversal now; arranging a transfer or politely allowing termination skips the meaning and lets the old loss go unspoken.

2019-121.sentence: Stigma is a hit to ego strength: people will not use help if walking in already means they are “the psych patient.” Putting personal counseling next to financial counseling at the same desk lets a burned-out physician ask for money help and still tolerate the feelings that come with needing a person.

2019-122.sentence: A seven-year-old with ADHD and ODD still uses the parent as a regulator, not as an insight machine. A home-and-school rewards plan built on what the child actually enjoys is a secure-base move: the adult stays close, names the target, and hands back a predictable yes when the child can stay in range.

2019-123.sentence: Appelbaum capacity is not a private IQ score; it is a conversation the twelve-year-old and the team can now hold together. Around that age the child can usually take in the facts, hold the choice, and answer you back, so her preference becomes part of the shared decision rather than something adults simply override.

2019-125.sentence: A locked-unit group never becomes a usable object if the faces change every day. Rapid patient turnover splits the room into a string of one-offs, so good and bad never get held long enough for cohesion to form.

2019-129.sentence: Those two-week stretches of 3–4 hours of sleep are doing different jobs: mania gives energy, insomnia steals it. Asking how well rested the person feels by day asks whether the missing sleep is a gift the mood is handing over or a wound.

2019-134.sentence: Capacity is the first question here, not the daughter's signature — can this person with dementia actually understand, weigh, and choose about the surgery, refusal and all. Reaching straight for a surrogate is often the team's way of avoiding a patient's no; capacity assessment forces you to take that no seriously first.

2019-137.sentence: ECT is indicated for catatonia, NMS, and psychotic depression; it is not a personality-disorder or dysthymia tool. Some endings cannot be rushed with talk: when eating, rigidity, or fever have already taken over, the limit is biological, and waiting for “more insight” is not treatment.

2019-138.sentence: Preschool emotion regulation tracks language, not walking, guilt, or cooperative play. Ego strength here is a word that can hold the feeling long enough that the impulse does not have to become a tantrum.

2019-151.sentence: The fitness-for-duty eval is a sanctioned leak in the usual confidentiality pact: the hospital’s physician-health committee is the real “patient,” and the surgeon’s secrets are not yours to keep. That is a superego bargain, not cruelty—you name the limit up front so your conscience and his both know the report is the work, not a private treatment alliance.

2019-157.sentence: Paranoid ideation is the interpersonal speed limit of schizotypal personality: odd speech, thrift-store eccentricity, and constricted affect already mark a mind that cannot be rushed into ordinary closeness. Ideas of persecution keep people at a distance you cannot interpret away in one consult; you work inside that limit instead of trying to terminate the oddness.

2019-158.sentence: Identification floods the intern so she becomes the dying patient's daughter; empathy keeps an observing ego, which is the capacity to feel the room and still think. If she cannot retain objectivity, drop uncovering and teach containment: name the feeling, then step back, because that mind cannot use deeper technique until the observing part is back online.

2019-162.sentence: Male gender is a hard risk marker for prolonged or complicated bereavement; the widower may recruit you as the lost wife, the stoic buddy, or the one who will not cry. Track that countertransference—what you feel pulled to become—because acceptance, money, a good marriage, and a calm first month do not protect him the way people wish they did.

2019-171.sentence: The teen is not in the room, so the frame is a parent consult, not a gender exam of an absent adolescent. Asking “What pronoun do you want me to use when referring to your child?” sets a speaking rule with the people present and keeps you from grabbing the limit that belongs to the missing teenager.

2019-173.sentence: After traumatic brain injury—the medical condition on this list with the highest suicide risk—the organ that watches itself is injured, so insight is not a reliable safety tool. A trial comment still matters, but you treat “can he see his own part?” as something the injury may have taken, not as a given you can talk him into.

2019-174.sentence: Holding is the mother’s slow work of taking in the infant’s state, mirroring it, and giving it back in a form the baby can use—not projective identification, where the feeling is dumped and left in the other. That capacity cannot be installed in one visit; you watch for it and wait, because rushing it is not teaching, it is crowding.

2019-175.sentence: The family has already been used as a dumping ground for raw violence and missed meds, so they refuse to be the container—the mind that can hold a feeling long enough to make it thinkable. Assertive community treatment is the next container: outreach that stays with the unmetabolized chaos instead of evacuating it back to the ward.

2019-180.sentence: Self-psychology (Kohut) treats the here-and-now idealizing or mirroring tie as co-created, not as a one-way projection you interpret away. That selfobject function has a clock you cannot rush; ending too soon is not insight, it is just withdrawing the borrowed self.

2019-183.sentence: Hair-pulling is often an evacuation: the student dumps nameless study-dread into the fingers so it never has to become a thought. Habit reversal works because it contains the urge in awareness-plus-competing response long enough for the feeling to become thinkable instead of just yanked out.

2019-184.sentence: Avoidant infants look cool because they have already used suppression: they push the need for the parent out of awareness so reunion cannot hurt. Little overt attention is the defense working, not independence; the child is managing attachment by not needing, which is still needing.

2019-188.sentence: This is still normal grief: disbelief, day-long thoughts of him, a wish to be with him without a plan to die. Attachment is a secure-base system; after sudden loss the protest can last months, and wanting proximity to him is not yet MDD.

2019-190.sentence: Medically certified sick leave tracks perceived poor relationship with the supervisor more than workload or decision latitude. In object-relations terms, the boss becomes the all-bad object—one person holding all the poison—so the body clocks out instead of the conflict getting named.

2019-191.sentence: Best first move: validate a normal reaction to failed treatment and a palliative plan, not CBT for “distortions” or a locked unit. Prognosis and technique: this mind needs support and naming of the overwhelm; uncovering or treating hope as a cognitive error would be too much.

2019-192.sentence: That package — psychoeducation, validating how real the emotional vulnerability feels, then pushing for change — is the core dialectic of DBT. Patients are often told their intensity is 'too much' long before anyone asks them to change anything; DBT's move is to validate the intensity as real first, so the push toward new skills doesn't land as one more person saying they're overreacting.

2019-193.sentence: Young adulthood to middle adulthood is when concern can leave the home and land on the larger social system—that is Klein's depressive position: you start to care that other people and institutions can be damaged and might need repair. Before that, politics is still mostly a self-object; after it, guilt and responsibility can attach to a world that is not you.

2019-196.sentence: Day-three baby blues with a depressed mother in the history is a two-person storm: the infant's needs and the new mother's own maternal imago arrive together. Psychoeducation is the relational intervention—naming the blues as expected so the pair do not have to enact 'I am a failed mother' before anyone has slept.

2019-197.sentence: Googling to tell grandiose delusion from reality can be a last-ditch way to stay a secure base: you need the world to stay real so the patient can still use you. Searching out of curiosity, to police psychotherapy, or to check if they can pay is using the patient as a proximity object for your own unease.

2019-206.sentence: Without emotional attunement the toddler’s hunger and night-waking never become a story; they stay as unrepresented states, raw body weather with no words. What the parent cannot feel with the child gets repeated in feeding and sleep instead of remembered as “I was scared.”

2019-209.sentence: OCD is a wish colliding with a prohibition until the ritual never stops; the anterior limb of the internal capsule is the white-matter corridor that carries that fight. Humanitarian-exemption DBS there is not “erasing the wish”—it is interrupting the highway between the urge and the punishing loop.

2019-217.sentence: When the MRI is clean but PET shows reduced perfusion in the bilateral lateral temporal lobes, invite a trial comment: “You still know these jokes land wrong, even if you cannot stop them.” If they can see their own part, you are looking at remaining insight; if they only blame the spouse, frontotemporal change has already eaten psychological mindedness.

2019-222.sentence: The reason an SSRI takes weeks to work isn't that the chemistry is slow to kick in — it's that the hippocampus has to grow new neurons before there's more capacity to hold and regulate feeling. Tell the patient the delay is the brain rebuilding room to feel, not proof the medication isn't working.

2019-226.sentence: Adjustment disorder is the commonest psychiatric diagnosis in cancer, and an antidepressant offered too fast can feel like a demand that she become a psychiatric patient instead of a person absorbing bad news. The pill is not feed here unless neurovegetative major depression is actually present; most of this is a relationship to the diagnosis, not a receptor gap.

2019-229.sentence: Federal 42 CFR Part 2 treats substance-use records as if the patient's capacity to seek help is still arriving and will collapse if the room is leaky. Extra confidentiality is the holding environment that lets a late-developing willingness to be known grow without being handed to a primary-care fax machine.

2019-232.sentence: A five-year-old can go to her mother's funeral if a familiar person stays beside her; that companion is the attachment figure who keeps the goodbye from becoming abandonment. Shielding the body, seating her in the back, or making her perform the service all miss the point: she needs a known adult who can stay when grief arrives.

2019-233.sentence: AA's first move is identity work in Erikson's sense: recognizing that they are an alcoholic consolidates a self that can then use a sponsor, a meeting, or a chip. Belief in God and weekly attendance matter later; without that identity the rest is role-play around a drink that still belongs to 'everyone else.

2019-234.sentence: When overwhelm exceeds affect tolerance, the binge-vomit cycle does the regulating the ego cannot, and elevated serum amylase is the lab echo of that repeated purge. Impulse control failed first; the parotids just keep the score.

2019-235.sentence: Oppositional defiant disorder often lives in the attachment system: the child uses argument and annoyance to keep a parent close when a calm bid for a secure base—someone they can rest on and return to—has stopped working. The talking-back is proximity-seeking with a sharp edge, a protest that says “stay in the fight with me” because quiet cooperation feels like being dropped.

2019-236.sentence: CATIE-AD’s week-12 win was reduced suspiciousness, not a better life for the caregiver or the patient, so the family and you can start chasing a calmer dyad instead of a miracle pill. The suspicion is a two-person event: when the drug takes the edge off paranoia, the caregiver’s hovering and the patient’s counter-attack can loosen together, if you name that pattern instead of only titrating milligrams.

2019-237.sentence: Evoking is the process where you draw out the patient’s own reasons to change, not the process where you deliver yours—support first, then just enough uncovering of their ambivalence. If you skip evoking and jump to planning, you are doing advice in motivational interviewing clothes, and an ambivalent mind will push back harder.

2019-241.sentence: The child's self is looking for a competent witness: a parent who only sees the 'good kid' at home cannot mirror the school self that is failing and frightened. Get the teacher's release first so you can name that split out loud, then the stomachaches stop being a mysterious body event and become a bid for someone to see him accurately.

2019-242.sentence: Supportive therapy is the trial comment you do not make: you build self-esteem and a more cohesive self instead of asking whether they can see their own part. Insight-oriented work needs psychological mindedness; this frame assumes they do not have it yet and treats esteem as the first holding environment.

2019-244.sentence: You may feel recruited to be the grim realist who confirms that aging is only loss; that countertransference misses the finding. Sense of well-being often rises even as body and cognition fall, so notice if you are becoming the voice of decline instead of the person who can hold both facts.

2019-246.sentence: The wish is that this is depression and a hint will bring the memory back; Alzheimer will not take the cue. The deficit that stays after hints or recognition is the collision: you wanted a recoverable mind, and the cortex will not grant it.

2019-250.sentence: Filing with CPS after a suicide attempt when the parent will not remove the guns trades on the parent's autonomy—the right to refuse your safety plan. You can still see your part: you used a trial comment about lethal means, they declined, and the report is the limit when insight stops.

2019-252.sentence: The mother's guilt and promise is raw beta-stuff she dumped in your lap; you soothed instead of thinking, and you did not report. Containing here means turning the bruise into a mandated report so the child's dread can become thinkable—and so legal sanctions do not land on you for the unreported earlier abuse.

2019-259.sentence: This mind already found a high-level way out: jealous rivalry with the gifted sibling got turned into martial-arts skill, which is sublimation, not a displacement that just dumps the anger on someone else. Do not interpret the sibling envy yet; support the dojo as the treatment, because this ten-year-old can use a channel more than an uncovering hour.

2019-264.sentence: The oven and carbon-monoxide checks are manic repair: a frantic undoing of the fantasy that the patient's own hate will kill the children. Exposure and response prevention asks the patient to sit in that Kleinian depressive worry, the fear of having harmed the loved ones, without the ritual that magically puts the family back together.

2019-269.sentence: Parents bring nameless dread—is this a phase?—and need you to hold it until it becomes a thought. Core gender identity, the basic sense of being a boy or a girl, is typically in place by age three, so the feeling is already organized rather than something to evacuate as temporary.

2019-273.sentence: At three, the body has usually arrived at reciprocal pedaling on a tricycle; skipping, tandem gait, and a copied triangle have not. If that motor capacity never quite shows up, you are looking at a developmental delay in the child’s use of the body, not a later “won’t cooperate” story.

2019-275.sentence: Therapeutic misconception is the wish that the protocol is still your personal doctor, deciding only for your good. Naming the trial’s real job—answering a research question, with drop-out allowed—protects consent from that rescue fantasy.

2019-276.sentence: Chronic zolpidem (or trazodone, diphenhydramine) is a night-by-night crutch; it does not grow the sleep-regulating capacity. CBT for insomnia is the treatment that leaves that capacity in place after the course ends, which is why long-term outcomes beat the pills.

2019-277.sentence: His conscience is prosecuting slowness as if it were a crime against competence. Name the finding plainly: healthy aging only stretches the time to learn; complete learning still happens, so the superego does not get to turn a slower hippocampus into a moral failure.

2019-280.sentence: Skipping insulin to shrink the body is a trauma logic that never gets words: the scale must change or the self disappears, so the pancreas becomes the scene of the repeat. That is psychological factors affecting other medical conditions, not factitious illness—she is not faking DKA; she is using type 1 diabetes as an unspoken weight-control ritual.

2019-284.sentence: Skin conductance falling is the body finally letting go of sympathetic sweat—relaxation you cannot hurry by staring at the number. Biofeedback only works when the patient stops chasing the readout and lets the arousal settle in its own time.

2019-292.sentence: An eight-year-old who sexualizes play and is seductive with peers is not showing curiosity or precocious puberty; the abuse that cannot be remembered is being repeated in the body and the schoolyard. Treat the sexualized behavior as an unrepresented state until a history of sexual abuse can be thought, not as a character label.

2019-294.sentence: Inhibited, comfort-refusing, affect-flat behavior in a recently adopted three-year-old is not a conscience problem and not autism until you have the missing piece: serious neglect, the DSM-5 requirement for reactive attachment disorder. Without a caregiver who answered distress, attachment did not form; you are seeing the absence of a bond, not a guilty withdrawal.

2019-295.sentence: Once a 15-month-old can treat you as a mind that is not theirs, they start recruiting you: you become the one who knows, soothes, or withholds. Notice what role you feel pulled into in the visit; that countertransference is early evidence that other-minds have arrived.

2019-296.sentence: The nagging is doing a job: it keeps the patient as the household superego so the partner never has to want the chore. Warm, specific praise after a completed dish pile is a positive reinforcer; it tries to make cleanliness belong to the partner instead of to the complaint.

2019-297.sentence: Asking for APOE testing is a bid to grow up into a known future, as if a lab could finish the developmental work of waiting. You have to say the hard limit: in a symptom-free 45-year-old, APOE e4 only shifts risk and has limited predictive value for Alzheimer disease.

2019-298.sentence: Attention regulation is a childhood capacity that often never quite arrives on time and then travels forward. A significant number of children with ADHD become adults with ADHD, so you still hunt the childhood timeline instead of treating adult restlessness as a new self.

2019-299.sentence: The request to call lung cancer pneumonia is a plea that you absorb the spouse’s panic so the patient’s ego does not have to. You keep two functions intact: you will not lie, and you tell the spouse only that the patient has not given permission to discuss the care.

2019-300.sentence: Needle exchange is harm reduction: it treats the syringe as a life-preserving tool while the person cannot yet use abstinence as a thought. The finding is doing work—fewer abscesses, HIV, and hepatitis—without demanding that the craving already have a story.

2020-1.sentence: By three, a flat "I'm a boy" isn't up for negotiation — it's a core identity locking into place, which is exactly why the adult's reflexive reaction in that moment gets folded into how solid or shaky it feels going forward. Notice your own face before you correct someone else's three-year-old.

2020-2.sentence: Generativity has a clock: the 40-to-60-year-old either puts something into the next generation or the hour just empties. You cannot rush a 52-year-old into Erikson’s later integrity work; first they have to find a use that outlives the career.

2020-7.sentence: Kohut’s point is that childhood narcissism is not a character flaw you should shame; it is the raw material of a cohesive self that needs mirroring—being seen as special without being crushed. If you feel irritated or morally superior toward a patient’s grandiosity, you are being recruited as the parent who withdrew admiration, and that countertransference will teach them that self-regard is dangerous.

2020-8.sentence: Acknowledging the patient’s frustrations is support, not uncovering: you name the affect so the frontal lobes can come back online. This mind cannot use interpretation while it is still in fight-or-flight, so you lower stimulation—no staring contest, no standing over them, no touch that can be read as a grab.

2020-9.sentence: The hospital, the car ride, even the smell of the lobby have become paired with the unconditioned nausea of chemo, so two people—the child and whoever is driving—now live inside a conditioned scene. You treat the pair: change cues, space visits, and name the automatic body reaction so the family does not turn the trip into a battle about “being difficult.”

2020-13.sentence: Nine P-words and twelve animals is not a shy, undereducated, or “not trying” patient. Letter fluency is a frontal generator task; category fluency still uses a stored semantic list, so the drop on P-words is the dorsolateral executive engine failing, not a personality.

2020-14.sentence: It's tempting to read this patient's withdrawal and forgetfulness as denial or depression about the AIDS diagnosis — but with an acellular tap and multifocal white-matter lesions, JC virus has already destroyed the oligodendrocytes doing the work of insight. You're not talking to a closed mind; you're talking to a damaged one.

2020-19.sentence: The cough is not a comment; it is an unrepresented scrap of old attack that she cannot remember as a story, so she repeats it in the room by turning you into the aggressor. Transference-focused psychotherapy names that live replay instead of arguing about the cough.

2020-20.sentence: Each online art buy is a tiny ego dodge: a mood lift arrives fast enough that he never has to tolerate the loneliness underneath. Operant conditioning just names the mechanism—the purchase is rewarded—so the work is to grow enough affect tolerance that he can wait out the urge.

2020-21.sentence: The orbitofrontal circuit is the brake pedal: it lets you feel the insult and still not strike or rant. When that circuit is out, hostility is not “who he is”; it is impulse with no delay.

2020-23.sentence: Coherent at 10am and disorganized by 4pm isn't a new personality showing through — it's the fluctuating attention of delirium, which is exactly why you compare the two exams instead of trusting whichever one you happened to catch. A single low MMSE could be dementia; only the swing between exams says delirium.

2020-25.sentence: Persecution is projection: hostility that cannot be owned is thrown onto coworkers, then felt as coming back. Do not interpret the denied rage yet; that mind needs you to hold the danger as real first, then slowly ask what part of the threat might live inside.

2020-26.sentence: The family recruits you to ratify a story that the widower prefers solitude, so you will stop noticing the arthritis and the fall. Your countertransference job is to refuse that role and keep naming reduced mobility as the thing that actually emptied the social world.

2020-27.sentence: The cigarette smell plus a request for cessation papers is contemplation: conscience is awake, but the habit still wins the hour. If you lecture or prescribe on the spot, you become either a scolding superego or a shortcut that lets him skip the conflict.

2020-28.sentence: Benztropine plus an 84-year-old brain is anticholinergic toxicity, not a new psychosis: fever, dry mouth, tachycardia, restlessness, visual hallucinations. Age has thinned the buffer that once absorbed that drug’s load, so the body now speaks the overdose the history may not.

2020-29.sentence: Fetishistic disorder stays off the police blotter because the arousal is tied to an object, not a nonconsenting person. The object can hold the sexual charge so the person never has to approach a live other who might overwhelm, refuse, or reopen old trauma.

2020-30.sentence: Hourly mood swings, bingeing, shopping, and “you are the only one who listens” in the first ten minutes is already an enactment: you are being installed as the perfect rescuer while everyone else is trash. Name the idealization as data, not as proof you are special, or you will live the abandonment story instead of treating borderline personality disorder.

2020-32.sentence: The eye recovers in six weeks, but what she's really facing now is the wait to find out whether this was the opening chapter of multiple sclerosis — your job shifts from restoring vision to helping her tolerate that uncertainty instead of panicking through it or pretending it isn't there.

2020-33.sentence: Rushing from an Alzheimer label to a surrogate is denial: the team treats the diagnosis as if it already answered whether he can refuse repair of a displaced radius. Capacity is decision-specific; you still have to see whether he can hold the fracture, the operation, and the risk of saying no.

2020-36.sentence: After the parent's pancreatic death, postprandial fullness never becomes a thinkable sensation; it stays nameless dread of the same cancer. The scale evacuates the feeling into a number, and avoiding the annual exam refuses the one person who might actually contain it.

2020-37.sentence: The snap “you must really hate me” is projection: the patient’s own hostility toward you is too raw to own, so it is thrown onto you and experienced as your hatred. Name the mechanism quietly rather than arguing your innocence; defending yourself only confirms the projected picture.

2020-38.sentence: The child’s wish to attach still collides with a history of lost foster homes, so the drive is shut down instead of risked again. Reactive attachment disorder is that compromise: comfort-seeking and smiling are inhibited so another abandonment cannot land as hard.

2020-40.sentence: REM sleep behavior disorder is a failure of the nighttime motor brake (lost REM atonia), not a daytime wish to punch. Ego strength can still look fine by day while Parkinson disease is already leaking through dream enactment.

2020-41.sentence: Psychiatry’s high suicide rank can sit beside a vertical split: the part that treats despair stays at work, and the part that is despairing is not allowed in the same hour. Wellness talk has to reach the split, not only the colleague’s caseload.

2020-42.sentence: Capgras is a prediction error: the face is recognized, the expected warm familiarity does not arrive, so the mind concludes “impostor.” The couple is already in an enactment—the wife is treated as a double—before anyone names the missing emotional signal.

2020-44.sentence: Living with a brain that can seize without warning tends to split someone in two: the self who still functions, and the self the temporal lobe hijacks. Depression often shows up when that second, unpredictable self starts to feel like the only real one — so treat both, not just whichever one is in the room that day.

2020-45.sentence: IDEA is a supportive, not an uncovering, intervention: eligibility needs intellectual disability plus failed academic progress, not a deeper interpretation of the child. Interpret less and scaffold more—IEP, concrete skills—because insight will not close that achievement gap.

2020-49.sentence: Cocaine and other psychostimulants flood the mesolimbic dopamine tract, so the high briefly supplies the missing selfobject: an outside source that makes the self feel whole, competent, and worth looking at. The dollar bill then works like a cheap mirror—it promises that same surge of cohesion without anyone actually seeing you.

2020-51.sentence: In a competency eval you drop the usual promise of confidentiality, so this mind cannot use uncovering the way a patient can. Stay supportive and factual; if you invite free association here, you are doing therapy in a courtroom and the material will not be held.

2020-54.sentence: Duty-hour reform hits the cultural third in training: the resident as endlessly available laborer versus the resident as a mind that needs sleep. High-quality studies show cognitive performance improved, which undercuts the old class story that staying later is how you become a real doctor.

2020-55.sentence: At thirty, contamination OCD has already stolen the intimacy-versus-isolation years: rituals keep people out so the self never has to risk being known. When washing no longer holds that bargain, the leftover affect is major depression—the most common comorbidity—not a second random illness.

2020-57.sentence: Eight weeks of sertraline already meant asking a suicidal, pregnant woman to wait through one slow trial — continuous suicidal ideation with a plan means she doesn't have time for another. ECT treats the emergency actually in front of you instead of the one you wish you had more time for.

2020-62.sentence: General systems theory starts here: a change in one member is already a change in the whole family. You cannot close the case by discharging the teen as the only patient while the rest of the system still needs his depression as the organ that holds the limit.

2020-66.sentence: The FDA flags paradoxical dissociative-like states with sedative-hypnotics, including chronic benzodiazepines. Before you name a new trauma diagnosis, treat the unreality as something the drug can write into the body when the original fear still has no words.

2020-71.sentence: Depersonalization/derealization is an unrepresented state shown in the body: numbness, the robotic self, watching life from outside so nothing has to happen to a “me.” Do not argue them back into the body; name the distance so the state can start to have words rather than only a numb field.

2020-75.sentence: It's easy to keep chasing infection in a newly started clozapine patient because a psychotic patient's cardiac symptoms don't feel as urgent as the psychosis did — but eosinophilia and T-wave changes in week three are myocarditis until a troponin says otherwise. Don't let the psychiatric diagnosis buy the physical symptoms less attention.

2020-76.sentence: The wish is to stay one person who knows her own life; the prohibition is against knowing what another self already lived. Extensive inability to recall personal information is the compromise—identity can shift only if memory takes the hit.

2020-78.sentence: Being right about the dose isn't enough when a senior colleague pushes back — the move that actually protects the patient is bringing your supervising attending in, not quietly complying or unilaterally overriding on your own. Use the hierarchy that exists to make disagreement safe, instead of absorbing it yourself.

2020-80.sentence: Adolescence is Erikson’s identity-versus-role-confusion stretch: the kid is trying to know whose feelings these even are. A daily diary in CBT psychoeducation is a scaffold for that task—he rates moods and triggers so the self becomes something he can observe, not just act.

2020-84.sentence: This eight-year-old can use support, not a deep uncovering campaign: clinginess and fear for the surviving parent are age-typical bereavement, not a warrant to hunt hidden guilt or attachment failure. Stay with the living parent’s availability and the child’s questions; interpret less, hold more, and treat new depression as a later problem if it actually appears.

2020-87.sentence: Derealization is the ego stepping back from the room so the fuzzy white-noise world does not flood her. That is affect intolerance wearing a perceptual mask: she stays seated, but reality-testing of the environment goes dim so depression and anxiety do not have to be felt at full volume.

2020-91.sentence: The SICU's push for benzos is a sanctioned moral shortcut: if we can just quiet the thrashing, we do not have to feel the guilt of an intubated person whose mind is failing. Name the chemistry anyway—delirium here tracks acetylcholine deficit, so sedation that further wrecks ACh is not mercy, it is the team buying a clean conscience.

2020-92.sentence: The daughter is recruiting you to be the loyal child who locates the danger in a 'crazy' 72-year-old and never in the household. Your countertransference—relief that the MoCA is 26, irritation at the nurse, eagerness to medicate 'aggression'—is the pull to join that story instead of asking who is actually being hurt.

2020-94.sentence: A relapse after Roux-en-Y isn't a moral failure — it's genuinely more dangerous now, because the surgery itself turned "a couple of drinks" into something that can kill. Hold both truths with her: she isn't a bad patient for slipping, and you still have to treat this like the emergency her new anatomy makes it.

2020-98.sentence: Midlife often means using the partner as a secure base in a new way: you look again at who you lean on, not only at the job or the empty nest. Reappraising the marriage is typical attachment work—testing whether proximity still regulates you—rather than a sudden impulsive break or a required depression when the last child leaves.

2020-99.sentence: The family and the patient are no longer in the same story: they still expect the lively man they knew, while Huntington-related frontal-subcortical change has left him apathetic, sparse of speech, and unbothered. That mismatch is interpersonal, not a shared depressive duet—he denies low mood, so this is personality change due to another medical condition, not MDD or adjustment.

2020-100.sentence: Awareness of the situation is the function that makes the rest of a competence exam usable: if the person cannot grasp the predicament, MSE findings, a mild dementia label, or whether they can pay bills sit in a vacuum. You are checking whether they can hold the facts of their life in mind, not whether they keep a tidy house.

2020-103.sentence: This is latency: sexual drive quiets from about age six to puberty so the school-age child can work the Erikson task of industry versus inferiority, learning to do things well with teachers and peers. If you treat that child as if they were still in oedipal heat or already in adolescent identity crisis, you miss the actual job of this period.

2020-104.sentence: A dropping carbamazepine level after a few weeks is CYP3A4 autoinduction, the drug inducing and then being eaten by its own enzyme, not a secret refusal of the medicine. Read the number before you read the relationship; otherwise you will chase “nonadherence” while the dose simply needs to go up.

2020-107.sentence: The tics are classic Tourette and barely distress him; the school failure is most often ADHD riding along, so you treat attention, not more uncovering of the movements. Insight into blinking and barking will not raise grades if working memory and impulse control are what the classroom actually needs.

2020-110.sentence: Dissociative amnesia erases autobiographical memory while implicit, working, and procedural skills stay online. Conscience can sanction that hole: the personal story becomes unthinkable after the assault, but riding the bus does not violate the same rule.

2020-114.sentence: Normal developmental regression is a transient return to earlier behaviors while overall maturation still holds. The newly trained three-year-old who wets after a sibling arrives is grabbing for the mirroring that just left the room.

2020-117.sentence: Fights, online bullying, and stealing the classmate’s phone are evacuations: raw rage is dumped into action so nobody has to think it. Conduct disorder, not ODD or a one-off IED burst, is the diagnosis when the uncontained feeling keeps becoming another victim instead of a thought.

2020-120.sentence: Evoked potentials ask whether the sensory pathway still fires while the left leg “cannot feel.” Intact potentials say the finding is doing psychic work—keeping a conflict out of words—rather than proving a lesion on EEG or MRI.

2020-121.sentence: A developmental capacity that should arrive in adolescence—being held by a continuous adult world—never quite arrives when historical trauma, disrupted kinship, and reservation-level resource gaps keep cutting the line. That is why American Indian and Alaska Native youth carry the highest U.S. suicide rate: the holding environment failed before the self could use it.

2020-124.sentence: You are being asked to hold two objects that will not sit in one mind: the capacitated patient as a separate subject who may choose aid in dying (autonomy), and the doctor who must not become an instrument of her overdose (nonmaleficence). Empathy that collapses those two into one “good” position is a split, not a synthesis.

2020-127.sentence: This sits on identity versus role confusion: the child still has to assemble a self from many identifications, and two mothers or two fathers do not skip that work or hand them a finished sexual orientation. Decades of data land on absence of adverse psychological consequences, which is Erikson’s point in clinic language—trust, industry, and identity keep unfolding if the caregiving is decent, not if the couple is heterosexual.

2020-130.sentence: Guns enter as a cultural third: politics, fear, and identity sit between you and the patient the moment you ask who has a firearm at home. Courts protected that question as freedom of speech, not as a malpractice shield or a license-scope trick, so the gag law does not get to decide what you may name in the room.

2020-132.sentence: “I am worthless” is a core belief: the whole self is painted with one bad object, not a passing automatic thought about today’s incompetence. In object-relations language the patient is not describing a mood; they are living as if the harsh internal figure is the only true picture of who they are.

2020-134.sentence: Sensate focusing bans breasts and genitals on purpose so the couple can make a new interpersonal sequence: touch as curiosity, not as a pass/fail exam of desire. The homework is two-person work—each partner’s anxiety and demand used to live in the other’s body; taking the goal off intercourse lets them feel that pattern instead of performing it.

2020-135.sentence: Cannabis carries the highest conversion rate to schizophrenia of any drug-induced psychosis on this list — which matters most for the family or teenager hoping to hear it was "just the weed." That reassurance isn't available here, so take the minimizing seriously enough to actually correct it.

2020-136.sentence: IED outbursts are triggered by anger, erupt in seconds, and are grossly out of proportion—not planned, not substance-timed, not dementia theater. Ego strength fails at the affect-tolerance step: anger floods before impulse control or reality testing can say “this slight is not a war,” and remorse after the fact does not count as control during it.

2020-138.sentence: Patients with delayed sleep phase often carry real shame about it — "I'm broken, I can't even sleep right" — when the truth is just that their clock runs a couple hours later than everyone else's. Timing melatonin to that window before their natural bedtime is a nudge to the clock, not a fix for a character flaw.

2020-139.sentence: Kandel’s point is that the wish to stay safe by avoiding and the prohibition on facing the feared cue keep rewriting gene expression until the circuit is the habit. Exposure is unlearning: you ask the same synapses that learned the neurotic pattern to change their gene expression again, not just swallow a pill and hope the old wiring goes quiet.

2020-140.sentence: Anosognosia after bilateral PCA strokes pulls you into a two-person scene: he cheerfully names dim lights and missing glasses while you keep naming the blindness he cannot own. That is an enactment—the two of you are living the deficit (he insists, you insist) instead of treating the denial as the neurologic finding it is.

2020-141.sentence: When the amygdala goes, fear and anger drop out of a person's read of faces and voices while happiness and disgust stay perfectly readable — it isn't apathy or a changed personality, it's one specific channel going dark. Don't expect this patient to "just know" when someone nearby is dangerous; that wiring is gone.

2020-145.sentence: Split treatment only works if you know how much uncovering this mind can use: you hold the supportive medical frame so the therapist can go deeper, or you both stay concrete if affect tolerance is thin. Regular contact with the therapist is the technique that keeps the two of you from becoming the good object and the bad pill-pusher.

2020-146.sentence: An internal locus of control is ego strength in plain clothes: the child can feel a feeling, choose a next move, and believe the move matters. That is better armor than MAOA levels or gender when the outside world is chaotic.

2020-148.sentence: In Piaget’s preoperational period the puppet can stand for mother, which means mother now lives as a symbol, not only as a body in the room. That is the cognitive hinge that lets a child play loss and reunion instead of only living them.

2020-151.sentence: Voices arguing are two inner claims fighting out loud: one accuses, one defends, and the listener is the battlefield. Schneider heard that as drive conflict made public—the wish and the prohibition no longer stay inside as thought; they speak as other people.

2020-152.sentence: Waiting for a completely risk-free antidepressant is its own kind of harm when mother and baby are both living inside untreated depression in the meantime. Sertraline, with the lowest milk transfer and the best safety data, is how you stop the wait instead of extending it.

2020-154.sentence: Verbal ability is the old conscience of the mind: vocabulary and verbal reasoning stay, even when timed recall and new encoding slip. The 85-year-old’s worry that slowness equals dementia is a harsh superego verdict; crystallized words are allowed to remain competent.

2020-155.sentence: Age 55 is midlife, not late old age: empty nest and menopause arrive as a developmental demand the self may not have words for. Completed suicide risk in women peaks here, when the next stage is required and the psyche still treats it as a private failure.

2020-156.sentence: "I'm being left out again" fires the instant the roommate walks out — that's an automatic thought, not a core belief or an idea of reference, and how fast and specific it is is exactly what tells you which one you're looking at. Trace it back to this situation, not to a verdict about who the patient fundamentally is.

2020-157.sentence: The laughing is not a joke aimed at you, but amitriptyline is treating a disconnected affect-release circuit, so your job is not to play the audience who must laugh along or shut it down. Notice the pull to feel embarrassed or to over-soothe the family; that countertransference, the feeling you are being recruited into, is a clue that the affect is happening without a person behind it.

2020-158.sentence: Linezolid plus sertraline is the interaction: MAO-A blockade stacked on an SSRI, so the tremor, hyperreflexia, myoclonus, and fever are serotonin flooding, not a hidden wish to die. Do not treat the consult as a personality crisis first; hold the medical meaning of the symptom or you will keep talking about suicide while the syndrome worsens.

2020-159.sentence: The hippocampus fails first, so new days do not stick while old self-stories stay fluent; the family then becomes the external memory. That is a developmental injury in reverse: the person cannot lay down the next chapter, so relatives start living as the archive instead of as children.

2020-161.sentence: A positive therapeutic alliance is the finding that actually tracks outcome, because the wish to be helped and the prohibition against needing anyone collide in the room. When the patient feels rushed, the protocol becomes the prohibition; you restore the work by naming the wish, not by stacking more worksheets.

2020-162.sentence: WAIS Vocabulary holds because old word-knowledge is a stored self, not a fresh performance, so it is the best hint of premorbid functioning after trauma. Use that score as a mirror of who he was, not as a verdict on who he is now, or you flatten his remaining self-esteem into a single deficit number.

2020-163.sentence: Parents often dump the wet sheets and the shame into you as raw panic—nameless dread, a feeling with no name yet—because they cannot think “this runs in families” without it meaning they failed. Your job is containment: you take that mess, metabolize it into one thinkable fact (family history of enuresis), and hand it back so the child is a bladder-and-genes kid, not a moral emergency.

2020-166.sentence: HIPAA’s Privacy Rule lets patients see the chart but carves out psychotherapy notes kept out of the general medical record—that is the frame holding the work. You, not the records clerk, hold that limit: process notes stay private so the room can stay a place to speak, not a place to be exhibited.

2020-167.sentence: Families often want one intervention that quietly fixes the kid and keeps him out of placement — multisystemic therapy asks the opposite: home, school, peers, and court all have to change together for it to work. That's a harder sell than a prescription, but it's what the evidence actually supports.

2020-170.sentence: Leaving the store is not just negative reinforcement—escape that removes panic and thereby trains more escape. A harsh conscience also blesses the exit: “good patients never stay with terror,” so the relief feels morally earned and the exposure work never starts.

2020-171.sentence: Greater mortality in widowers often means a self-care capacity that lived in the marriage and never quite arrived as his own. Cooking, pills, and cardiology were her ego functions; when she dies, the developmental job of being a body without her is still unfinished.

2020-172.sentence: The housebound “anxiety” is doing work: it keeps him off stairs and curbs that progressive supranuclear palsy has made treacherous because vertical gaze and axial tone are failing. Treat the symptom as a crude safety signal around falls, not as a phobia that insight will talk away.
